News.title: World-famous rollercoaster leaves riders with brain injuries & is linked to lifelong disabilities, probe finds
News.content:
A WORLD-FAMOUS rollercoaster dubbed a “rite of passage for the ultimate daredevil” has been linked to brain injuries, comas and deaths, a probe has found.

The terrifying X2 at Six Flags Magic Mountain in Southern California has left riders with traumatic brain injuries, according to doctors who treated two women injured within days of each other.



Both suffered severe brain haemorrhages in July after riding the 76mph monster, CNN reported.

One of the women, Pamela Guillen, suffered a severe subdural haematoma and brain compression after repeatedly smashing her head against the ride’s headrest.



The 40-year-old lost consciousness and was placed on a ventilator in the back of an ambulance as surgeons fought to save her.

Doctors were forced to remove part of her skull to relieve pressure on her swelling brain.

Guillen said after regaining consciousness two weeks later: “You go in as yourself, and then when you come back, you’re a medical emergency.

“I still can’t wrap my head around that.”

The brutal injury left her having to relearn how to walk and talk, while she now relies on medication to prevent seizures.

She told CNN: “I’m very lucky to be alive.



“I’m taking it a day at a time to not overwhelm myself and to not go into a dark hole of mourning who I was and what I was able to do before this.”

Just days later, Los Angeles woman Naomi Greer-Wilkinson climbed aboard the same attraction.

She remains in a coma, hooked up to a ventilator and feeding tube after suffering a traumatic brain injury.

Her devastated parents were told by doctors that she was in a critical condition and should prepare for the worst.

Her mother said: “This is the hardest thing a human being could go through.”



Six Flags shut X2 on July 12, almost a day after Greer-Wilkinson’s injury.

Yet the park has not explained why the ride initially remained open after Guillen was rushed to hospital.

Three neurosurgeons who treated the women gave a damning assessment of what happened.



They said: “In our professional opinion, the severe brain injuries requiring emergent neurosurgical attention were the result of a traumatic rapid acceleration-deceleration event experienced while on the X2 ride.”

The ride’s stomach-churning design sees seats spin 360 degrees independently of the track as the train plunges down steep drops at speeds of nearly 80mph.

Promoted as a “[rite] of passage for the ultimate daredevil”, X2 is one of just three four-dimensional rollercoasters in the world.

A CNN investigation found the attraction has been linked to more than a dozen serious injuries and hospitalisations over nearly two decades.

Court files also reveal a grim trail of life-altering disabilities, comas and two deaths allegedly connected to the ride.



Christopher Hawley died in June 2022 after riding X2, with doctors finding his brain so swollen it began bulging through an opening in his skull.

His surgeon compared the devastating injury to “shaken baby syndrome”, while a medical examiner ruled that blunt head trauma from “a park ride accident” caused his death.

Another rider, 28-year-old mother Hilda Farias, died after riding the attraction in 2010, with experts suspecting a ruptured brain abnormality.

Despite the dark track record, the ride has continued operating after years of complaints about head and neck injuries, according to court records.

Lyndia Wu, a mechanical engineering professor at the University of British Columbia who has researched rollercoasters and the brain, said: “I personally don’t think head injury should be an expected risk from going on a roller coaster ride, and there is no reason a ride can’t be properly designed to prevent injuries like this.”



Six Flags has defended X2 in court, arguing that warning signs alert passengers to “inherent risks in the participation in or on any amusement ride or attraction”.

Lawyers have also claimed the attraction is regularly tested and is not powerful enough to cause a traumatic brain injury when a “normal” rider uses it “as instructed”.

But the three neurosurgeons who treated the two latest victims directly disputed that defence.

California’s Division of Occupational Safety and Health, which oversees amusement park rides, said an inspection of X2 remains ongoing.

Six Flags declined to answer detailed questions about the latest injuries or why the ride stayed open after Guillen’s hospitalisation.

A park spokesman said simply: “The ride remains closed at this time.”

The ride’s manufacturer, Arrow Dynamics, went bankrupt more than two decades ago, leaving the notorious attraction at the centre of an increasingly disturbing safety probe.

News.title: Trump signs order to rename Lake Ontario to Lake America as he feuds with neighbour Canada over trade war
News.content:
DONALD Trump has ordered Lake Ontario to be renamed “Lake America” amid a bitter feud with Canada as a fresh trade war rages between the neighbours.

The US President signed an executive order on Thursday demanding the historic lake be known as Lake America for US federal purposes.



Trump declared the change was “official, effective immediately,” as he continued his campaign to put his stamp on America’s landmarks.

The US leader told reporters at the Oval Office: “We’re going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America.”



Trump claimed he had been plotting the controversial switch “for a long time”.

Yet the dramatic order only applies to US federal usage and cannot force Canada, international organisations or other bodies to ditch the lake’s 400-year-old name.

More than half of Lake Ontario’s surface – around 52 per cent – lies in Canada.

The remainder is in New York under a 1909 treaty.

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney swiftly hit back, making clear Ottawa would not bow to Trump’s renaming bid.

Carney said: “We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms.”



“Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario then, now and always.”

The furious row comes as US-Canada trade talks have spectacularly collapsed, with Washington imposing new 50 per cent tariffs on around $20billion worth of Canadian goods.

Carney has vowed to retaliate “dollar for dollar”, threatening to pile fresh pressure on American exporters.

The latest salvo has plunged relations between the long-standing allies to fresh lows after three days of last-ditch negotiations ended without a deal.



Trump has accused Canada of “ripping us off for a long time on trade”, while Ottawa says last-minute US demands helped torpedo the talks.

New York Governor Kathy Hochul also rejected the proposed name change, while Vermont Governor Phil Scott branded it “petty and disappointing”.



Grand Chief Pierre Picard of the Wendat Nation in Quebec accused Trump of trying to “erase our history”.

He said: “Outraged, appalled, shocked: there are no other words to express how I feel following President Trumps decision to rename Lake Ontario ‘Lake America.”

The lake’s name predates both Canada and the United States and originates from the Wendat language, meaning “the lake is beautiful, great.”

Trump has now hinted that his naming spree could stretch even further – joking that he could target the world’s oceans next.

He said: “We have a gulf and we have a lake, now all we need is an ocean, so maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them both.”



His latest move echoes his January 2025 order changing the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America for US federal use.

That previous decision sparked a bitter row with Mexico, while Google Maps now displays different names depending on where users are viewing the gulf.

Trump’s latest territorial naming clash comes as he repeatedly taunts Canada over becoming America’s 51st state – a proposal Canadian leaders have repeatedly dismissed.

The trade dispute has meanwhile piled fresh strain onto already bruised relations, with billions of dollars of goods crossing the border between the two countries.

Canada and the US traded around $880billion worth of goods and services last year, while almost 72 per cent of Canada’s goods exports were sold to its southern neighbour.



Despite the cross-border dispute, there was a glimmer of hope for negotiations.

Canadian trade minister Dominic LeBlanc said Washington had withdrawn some demands over French-language labelling.

He said the move created “the possibility of a mutually beneficial trade agreement that respects Canadian sovereignty”.

News.title: Cars torched by yobs at twisted vigil for victim of A66 wrong-way crash after mum asked for ‘send-off he deserves’
News.content:
CARS have been torched at a twisted vigil for one of the joyriders killed in the A66 wrong-way crash – just hours after police launched a crackdown on a gang war.

Yobs paying tribute to their dead pal burned the motors as they released balloons into the air near Haswell, County Durham, footage posted to social media by attendees last night showed.



Five motors were burned to a crisp at the remembrance for Michael Robert Cahill, 23, after he and four others died in the A66 smash on Saturday morning.

The joyriders had driven the wrong way down the dual carriageway in Middlesbrough and crashed into a police car, also killing PC Matthew Blades, 37, and PC Tom Clough, 38.



Cahill’s friends paid tribute to him by skidding the cars around a farmer’s field and churning up the ground before setting the motors alight.

The two-dozen-or-so youths then set off blue flares as the fire began to take hold – with other masked yobs able to be seen near the motors.



Balloons spelling out “Michael” were released into the sky over the sound of loud engines and horns from a group of masked bikers in the crowd.

Fire crews and police rushed to the scene before the youths abandoned the burning cars to their fate.

Locals were left aghast at the chaos with one saying: “I was showing my niece the horses out the back of mine and they were terrified.”

Another said: “Absolutely disgusting.”



The local farmer was left to dispose of the wrecks and deal with the scorched grass, according to the locals.

Footage showed the burned out carcasses being moved around by the farmer’s JCB as smoke still rose from them.

Cahills’s mum had urged for people to bring “bikes, jeeps, cars and quads” and give her son “the send off he deserves” as she encouraged people to the memorial.

It comes as more than 200 police officers were deployed to Middlesbrough as gang warfare spirals.



Officers include firearms cops and detectives with years of experience in tackling gang-related violence.

The move was announced last night violence in the town left nine dead in under a week, including Valentina Foster, 7, and her aunt Natalie McDonald, 34.

The four other occupants of the VW Passat who died in Saturday’s crash were: Theo Rae, 17, Cole Robert Worthy, 17, Jacob Matusiak, 23, and Makai Saddington, 18.



Sources said the gang was hell-bent on revenge after rivals had earlier rammed a number of properties in the area. Another home was rammed yesterday.

Gangland pals of the five are also believed to be linked to the fire-bombing of a house in the Grangetown area that killed innocent Valentina and Natalie.

Another woman, 48, who was pulled from the burning building, remains in a critical condition in hospital.



Armed police last night also swooped on a house and arrested a man at gunpoint only five miles from Middlesbrough.

It’s unclear weather that arrest related to the gang warfare, but the spiralling violence also saw armed officers scrambled to an estate yesterday after a stabbing.

Tasteless vigils for the five have been held all week, with balaclava-clad pals setting off fireworks and flares in their memory.



On Monday, masked youths sparked outrage after setting off flares in memory of Jakub Matusiak.

The gathering which took place on South Bank field near Middlesbrough was quickly branded “disrespectful” after the crown descended into an angry mob.

What set out as a balloon release became around 200 people lighting up the sky with rockets and orange smoke.

A gang of around 20 masked youths on scooters, off-road bikes and quad bikes roared around a field in South Bank, near Middlesbrough, in honour of Matusiak, who himself had convictions for motoring offences.

At just after 5pm hundreds of orange balloons – chosen because it was his favourite colour – were released into the sky amid cheers from the crowd.



One Haswell local questioned why those memorials hadn’t involved “burning cars or rallying cards crashing into each other”.

In stark contrast, devastated ­colleagues of the two officers ­bowed their heads for a poignant minute’s silence for the fallen PCs.

Local Labour MP Andy ­McDonald said: “People feel unsafe even leaving their homes to go to the shops.

News.title: Body found during search for missing Brit tourist, 28, in mountains after he disappeared without backpack and documents
News.content:
HOLS HORROR Body found during search for missing Brit tourist, 28, in mountains after he disappeared without backpack and documents

A BODY has been found in the search for a British tourist missing in the Pyrenees, a day after police and firefighters launched a rescue mission.

The 28-year-old was last seen in the early hours of Sunday after leaving a hostel in Andorra where he had checked in for a three-night stay.



When he failed to return on Wednesday morning, staff alerted the authorities.

He had left his backpack, travel documents and other belongings at the property in the town of Escaldes-Engordany – in the southeastern part of Andorra.



The unnamed man also missed a bus he had booked for midday on Tuesday.

Earlier today Andorran police announced a body had been recovered in the mountainous Tristaina Lakes area which is known for its picturesque landscapes.



They said in a statement: “This Thursday at midday the Fire Brigade located a lifeless body in the Tristaina area as part of the active search for a 28-year-old British tourist whom the police, with the collaboration of the Rescue Service, began searching for on Wednesday.

“From the moment the alert was raised about his possible disappearance, officers from the Public Security, Judicial Police and Criminal Investigation, and International Cooperation areas launched an investigation.

“With the support of the Fire Brigade, a search was begun in the urban area while efforts were made to reconstruct the route the young man might have taken.”

It follows an extensive search operation, which saw search and rescue teams deploy a helicopter and drone to scan the area.



“While the search was being carried out, a citizen alerted the Rescue Service around noon, after appearing to see a person who might be deceased,” they added.

“The police will have to proceed with identifying the body and verify whether it is the British tourist who had been missing since Wednesday.”

Local reports published at the time of his disappearance indicated his reduced mobility on the right side of his body.

Rescue efforts initially focused on the area where he was staying and a nearby river.

The Tristiana Lakes are high-altitude glacial lakes located in the Ordino Parish of Andorra along the French border.



The scenic circular hike is one of the most popular treks in Europe.

It follows the tragic death of a 19-year-old hiker, who plunged 650ft off a mountain in Germany and vanished without a trace.

His body was discovered on the north face of the Fuderheuberg mountain in July, following a frantic search.

News.title: Superyacht stewardess, 21, took her own life after being sacked for boozy night out & row with boyfriend
News.content:
TRAGIC END Superyacht stewardess, 21, took her own life after being sacked for boozy night out & row with boyfriend

A SUPERYACHT stewardess, 21, took her own life following a heated row with her boyfriend, two months after she was sacked for a drunken night out, an inquest has heard.

Imogen Amesbury was asked to leave the luxury yacht Queen Miri docked off St Martin in the Caribbean, after coming back drunk and high on cocaine in November 2021.



The young stewardess returned home to Lyme Regis, Dorset, rekindling a relationship with her ex, Andrew Hewitt, Bournemouth Coroner’s Court heard on Thursday.

The two had fallen out while staying at Imogen’s mum’s home on January 12, 2022, with Hewitt leaving the house at 4.10am.



Imogen followed him for a short while, then later told him on the phone that she was “going to kill herself and wanted to die”.

Hewitt dismissed her threats, telling her “don’t be stupid” before she told him to “f*** off” and hung up on him.

Her ex did not raise the alarm following the harrowing phone call and her mum discovered her body at the property later that day.

The cause of death given was hanging.

Alex Sawyer, who worked as a chef on Queen Miri, said: “She lost her job on the yacht in November 2021 as she had been on a night out and returned drunk and under the influence of cocaine.

“I think she had been given a previous verbal and written warning so she was fired and had to leave the yacht at St Martin.”



Despite losing her job, she had apparently returned home in “high spirits”.

However, the court heard how the 21-year-old had previously struggled with her mental health, including a two-week stint in The Priory treatment centre in 2021.

Mum Marie Amesbury broke down in tears as she paid a heartwrenching tribute to her daughter, who was awarded an art scholarship at Queen’s College Taunton and was also a talented sportswoman.

She said: “Imo was gentle and warmhearted but quietly determined, adventurous and courageous.

“At 19 she became a stewardess on superyachts. She was my most beautiful, talented and adventurous child.”



She added that her daughter had had “so much more” life to live and pursue her talents.

“There are no words that can adequately describe the deep pain her death has left in her family or what it means to try and create our lives without her,” she said.

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this article, please call the Samaritans for free on 116123.

Her father, Peter Woolford, wept as he blamed his daughter’s ex for her death, believing she was “under the control and duress” of Hewitt.

“I have been in the room with her when she’s had a drink and she was erudite, funny, articulate and intelligent,” he said.

“And then in a room with Andrew and she fell apart.



“He stole money from her, insulted her, sent her text messages when he’s putting 1p in her bank account.

“He demeaned her, told her his adulterous affairs, disrespected her.”

He said he feared Hewitt was only going to do it again and that “another family” would end up at an inquest.

“Imo pulled the trigger but Mr Hewitt loaded the magazine with bullets that she fired,” he said.

“The control he had was astonishing and when I told her it was toxic she defended him.



“It was suicide under duress.”

How to get help EVERY 90 minutes in the UK a life is lost to suicide It doesn’t discriminate, touching the lives of people in every corner of society – from the homeless and unemployed to builders and doctors, reality stars and footballers. It’s the biggest killer of people under the age of 35, more deadly than cancer and car crashes. And men are three times more likely to take their own life than women. Yet it’s rarely spoken of, a taboo that threatens to continue its deadly rampage unless we all stop and take notice, now. Hewitt, giving evidence, said the two of them had tried to separate before but were “too deeply intertwined” with one another.

Reflecting on her threats to kill herself, he said: “I thought it was at the time an empty threat as she had been known to say it.

“When she spoke to me on the phone she sounded so nonchalant about killing herself but I didn’t think she was being serious.”

He was asked if he had ever hit Imogen or threatened to send intimate pictures of her, which he denied.



Hewitt was also asked whether he had ever texted her to “go kill herself”, to which he replied no comment.

A toxicology report revealed Imogen had been inebriated when she died, at nearly three times over the alcohol drink drive limit.

She had also taken a “recreational” amount of cocaine.

Her family raised concerns about the on-off nature of her relationship with Hewitt and the impact it had on her mental state, the court head.

News.title: Burnham ‘risks trade war with Trump’ over plans to impose sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements
News.content:
ANDY Burnham has been warned he is risking a trade war with Donald Trump over plans to impose sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements.

The PM is poised to announce a boycott on goods and services from the outposts on Palestinian land in a bid to please lefty Labour MPs.



However, others in the party are warning him the stand could spark retaliation from Trump.

The US criticised Ireland for a similar move last month.



President Trump also threatened a full trade embargo with Spain.

It came after they banned goods being imported from illegal settlements.



One Labour MP said: “Our trade and diplomatic relationship with the US is fragile enough as it is.

“We shouldn’t be naive enough to believe we could sanction Israel and not face consequences from the White House.”

We told last month how, after the White House imposed 10 per cent levies on Britain and the EU, the UK must then pay duties on top, whereas Brussels levies are all-inclusive.

The trade deal struck with the US means pharmaceuticals, steel and aluminum are protected from these changes.



But Whitehall insiders said products where the EU now faces a lower tariff than the UK are only around 10 per cent of UK exports heading stateside.

Charlotte Brumpton-Childs, GMB national secretary, said: “The EU now has a better trading relationship with the US than we do – which undermines the so-called ‘special relationship’.

News.title: Andy Burnham must do voters a favour by revealing the true scale of the illegal migrant crimewave ruining British lives
News.content:
Border betrayal

LABOUR’S open borders lunatics are betraying voters with an effective free-for-all for migrants.

Figures released yesterday showed 140,122 migrants — or one every MINUTE — was granted indefinite leave to remain or British citizenship in just the three months to June.



Overall, 200,000 were given ILR in the last year, the highest number since 2011.

It’s anyone’s guess how many of those people could end up joining the almost 1.3million migrants ALREADY claiming £6BILLION in Universal Credit benefits.



The spin from Labour over yesterday’s grim migration figures was shocking.

Ministers hailed cutting the asylum cases backlog by 56 per cent.



But what good is that if the Government is letting everyone stay? Labour also claimed success in halving the numbers placed in asylum hotels.

But 73,000 have simply been dumped in HMO properties in local communities.

There are even disturbing reports that Brit renters are being turfed out of flats by unscrupulous landlords wanting to turn their blocks into HMOs to get guaranteed Government cash.

Worse, 17,500 foreign criminals are free on our streets and have still not been deported. Frightened families are bearing this enormous risk.



Every day brings news of another horrifying case of rape, sexual assault or violence committed by young foreign men who have broken into this country.

Just this week a Sudanese migrant was found guilty of slashing a woman 30 times with a broken bottle.

We don’t even know the true scale of crime committed by small boat migrants. That’s because Labour has launched legal action to keep it a secret.

Among those fighting Government lawyers in court are Ann Newman, the partner of dog-walker Wayne Broadhurst — killed by an Afghan national — and the family of Rhiannon Whyte, a hotel worker stabbed to death by a Sudanese migrant.

Real people who have paid a terrible price for Government failure. Yet still the boats come, with another five containing hundreds of illegals landing yesterday.



Why wouldn’t migrants chance it when they know if they can get to the UK they will almost certainly stay?

Andy Burnham repeatedly claims he wants to be honest with the people.

The Prime Minister could start by being straight about where asylum seekers are being housed.

Then do voters a favour by revealing the true scale of the illegal migrant crimewave ruining British lives.

Lost generation

PAT McFadden might be the only Labour minister to speak the truth on benefits.



Yesterday, he admitted the welfare system was “flawed” for writing off people’s chances of ever working.

News.title: Fears grow a SECOND deadly flood could hit Nepal within 48 hours as 33 Brits among 1,500 still missing
News.content:
HOPE was fading last night for more than 1,500 people still missing after the monster flash floods that scythed through the Nepal-Tibet border.

Fears are also rising of a second tsunami as huge amounts of water flow into two new lakes formed by debris from the first disaster creating an unstable dam.



More than 900 tourists — including 33 Britons — remained among the grim toll of the missing as a travel chief warned of a “one per cent” chance of finding any more survivors.

Eleven of the Britons — including a girl of 13 — were in a group that crossed into Tibet just as the wall of water hit.



Ram Kumar Adhikari, of Alpine Eco Trek, last heard from them at 8.40am at immigration on the Gyirong border. The others are three men aged 52 to 65, and seven women aged 44 to 65.

Mr Adhikari said: “There is no internet access on the Chinese side, so we had no reason to be immediately concerned. Then we received news of the massive flood.



“Authorities later released video showing a huge surge of water sweeping away the Chinese immigration building. You can see people running, some could be members of our group.”

Another pilgrimage trekking group, Kailash Journeys, has lost contact with seven UK nationals — five women and two men aged 18 to 55 — who were also near immigration at the time.

Two more Britons, with Himalayan Glacier Group, are also missing. A 14-year-old British boy is also unaccounted for.

Distraught families in the UK were last night still in the dark, more than 24 hours after the flood of mud, water and debris tore along the Lende Khola river into the Bhote Koshi river, 100 miles north of Nepal’s capital Kathmandu.



The husband of missing Leena Bector, 53, frantically checked her online location after hearing of the disaster and realised she had not moved for seven hours.

Mobile phone data puts care agency boss Leena, from Slough, Berks, around an hour’s travel away from the now washed-away “Friendship Bridge”, which she was supposed to visit.

Bhupesh, who booked the next available flight to Nepal to search for his wife of 30 years, told The Times: “I want to go to Kathmandu now. I know she’s in Nepal for sure. So even if they find her today or tomorrow, I need to be there.”



British nurse Sarada Simkhada, from Dartford, Kent, is also missing. She moved to the UK 20 years ago and is a senior nurse at the town’s Darent Valley Hospital.

The British Hindu was on a pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in nearby Tibet — said to be the cosmic home of Lord Shiva.

Her brother Shambu wrote on social media: “May God protect you and guide the rescue team to find you safely.”

Fellow Hindu Nabhi Das from Streatham in South London was close to where the flood hit and has not been heard from since.

Originally from Kenya, the Kent University graduate works in finance and has travelled in the region before.



Sunil Amin last heard from his wife Hema on Monday after she travelled to Nepal with her sister on a pilgrimage to Gosainkunda lake.

Mr Amin, of Croydon, South London, said her phone rings but is not answered.

He said: “I keep trying to call her. I have a horrible, horrible feeling. We hope it’s good news, but don’t know exactly what happened to them. I’m devastated.”

Pramod Poudel, from Uckfield, East Sussex, said he was also flying to Nepal last night after failing to ­contact his wife Sumitra, mother, brother and uncle.



He said: “There is no proper communication so I can’t communicate with them. I guess there is no power so they can’t charge their phones — it’s a very hard and difficult time at the moment.

“Where my home town used to be, where my family used to live — my mum, dad, wife — there’s nothing there.”

At least 389 victims are confirmed dead after the 50ft high wall of water, mud and stone hit their homes and wiped them out.



The grim toll is likely to rocket as whole communities were swept away down the river valley in Rasuwa.

Disaster experts said the 20 million cubic metres flood was triggered when an iceberg-sized chunk of glacier broke off.

They fear a second flood could strike if the dam of debris that has formed a lake breaks.

Chinese officials said the landslide dam, where the Tsogyal and Purupqiangzangbu rivers meet, has a “high risk of breaching” within 48 hours.

It was estimated the newly formed lake had grown to two million cubic metres of water yesterday, with three million — the equivalent to more than 1,000 Olympic swimming pools — expected to rapidly add to it.



Last night authorities were desperately evacuating towns and villages downstream while frantic searches for survivors continued.

Nepalese army teams airlifted hundreds out of the Rasuwa district and more than two dozen tourists were brought to safety on Thursday.

Ruined communication infrastructure is hampering attempts to confirm victims’ identities.



The King and Camilla “are heartbroken to hear of the devastating flooding” and Prime Minister Andy Burnham pledged £5million aid to support rescue and recovery work there yesterday.

News.title: Blood moon lunar eclipse 2026 live: Peak time as 'earth's shadow' set to be visible across UK
News.content:
A “blood moon” lunar eclipse is set to be visible across the UK and Ireland in the early hours of Friday.

A partial lunar eclipse will see around 93% of the Moon move into Earth’s darkest shadow as the “blood moon” becomes visible across the UK.

A “blood moon” lunar eclipse is set to be visible across the UK and Ireland in the early hours of Friday, with the Moon expected to turn a reddish or copper colour.

The phenomenon happens when Earth moves between the Sun and the Moon, casting its shadow across the lunar surface. Around 93% of the Moon will move into the darkest part of Earth’s shadow, known as the umbra, at the eclipse’s maximum at 5.12am.

The penumbral phase begins at 2.23am, before the partial eclipse starts at 3.33am.

Cloud could make viewing difficult in parts of the UK, with the Met Office saying southern and eastern England have the greatest chance of seeing the earlier stages before cloud becomes more extensive.

The Moon will begin to set at around 6.15am in London, while no protective glasses are needed to watch the eclipse. The spectacle comes just over two weeks after the UK experienced a near-total solar eclipse

News.title: Nepal-Tibet floods live: King Charles 'heartbroken' with 1000s missing including Brit kids
News.content:
A 13-year-old girl and a 14-year-old boy are among 33 British tourists missing in Nepal and Tibet after an avalanche led to major flooding along the Bhotekoshi River

King Charles said he and the Queen are "heartbroken" by the "devastating" flash floods in a Nepal border area, where dozens of British nationals are among the hundreds missing and feared dead.

At least 389 people have died in Nepal and nearly 1,000 peope are missing, while 558 people are missing in Tibet, where three people have been confirmed dead.

On both sides of the border, hundreds of foreign nationals are among those missing, including 33 British citizens. A 13-year-old girl and a 14-year-old boy are believed to be the youngest UK citizens unaccounted for.

The Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said river levels rose by up to nine metres in just 30 minutes at the height of the flash floods on Wednesday.

According to the Red Cross, "entire villages and market areas" have been wiped out by the torrent of water and mud, which has flattened all in its path along the Bhotekoshi River.

News.title: Body found during search for missing Brit tourist, 28, in remote mountains near French border
News.content:
Body found during search for missing Brit tourist, 28, in remote mountains near French border

The 28-year-old was last seen in the early hours of Sunday after leaving a hostel in Andorra. On Wednesday Andorran firefighters and police launched a search to find the man and just a day later confirmed a body has been found

View 2 Images The search started on Wednesday and 24 hours later a body was found (Image: Andorra Policia)

A body has been found in the search for a missing British tourist a day after police and firefighters started searching the eastern Pyrenees mountains for him.

‌



The 28-year-old was last seen in the early hours of Sunday after leaving a hostel in Andorra. On Wednesday Andorran firefighters and police launched a search to find the man - who has not yet been named.

‌



Local media reports he had left his backpack, travel documents and other belongings at the hostel in the town of Escaldes-Engordany – in the southeastern part of Andorra.

‌



View 2 Images Andorra is a tiny, landlocked sovereign principality nestled in the eastern Pyrenees mountains between France and Spain. (Image: Getty Images)

‌



Just a day into the search a body was found in the Tristaina area. The Tristaina Lakes (Estanys de Tristaina) are a group of three high-mountain glacial lakes located in the Ordino parish of Andorra, near the French border.

A statement from Andorra Police shared on Facebook today reads: "Andorran firefighters located a body this Thursday at midday in the Tristaina area, as part of the active search for a 28-year-old British tourist that the Police—with the collaboration of the Rescue Service—had launched on Wednesday.

"From the moment the alert regarding his possible disappearance was raised, officers from the Public Security, Judicial Police and Criminal Investigation, and International Cooperation Office units launched an investigation. Supported by the fire service, they began searching urban areas while attempting to reconstruct the route the young man might have taken.

Article continues below

"On Thursday morning, once the Police obtained more precise information regarding his likely location in the Tristaina area, a search operation was activated there, involving firefighters using a helicopter and the Police using a drone. During the search, around noon, a member of the public alerted the Rescue Service after spotting what appeared to be a deceased person.

"The Police will now proceed to identify the body and verify whether it is the British tourist who had been the subject of the search since Wednesday."

News.title: Chilling gun law warning as report points to 39 murders using legal weapons
News.content:
Chilling gun law warning as report points to 39 murders using legal weapons

His Majesty’s Inspector of Constabulary, Lee Freeman, has called on ministers to tackle an alarming 'postcode lottery' around firearm licensing - saying existing systems are not fit for purpose

View 3 Images New rules were brought in following the 2021 gun murders in Plymouth (Image: PA)

Chilling failures have led to a "postcode lottery" for members of the public seeking to legally own guns, an inspection report has ruled.

‌



The independent police watchdog has warned the existing system is not fit for purpose with huge inconsistencies across England and Wales. A report by His Majesty’s Inspector of Constabulary, Lee Freeman, said there had been at least 39 murders involving legally-owned weapons in a decade.

‌



He warned that further tragedies should not be required before ministers take action. The report, published today, said poor guidance and supervision could be putting the public at risk and called for a new national firearms licensing authority. Calls for an overhaul have heightened since hate-filled misogynist Jake Davison shot and killed five people in Plymouth five years ago, including three-year-old Sophie Martyn and her dad Lee.

‌



Davison was authorised to own the pump-action shotgun he used by Devon and Cornwall Police. In a sickening series of shootings in August 2021 he also murdered his own mother, Maxine, and passers-by Stephen Washington, 59 and Kate Shepherd, 66. Two others were injured before the killer turned the gun on himself.

Under 18s in UK face new safety features on Facebook and Instagram after Meta legal case READ MORE :

View 3 Images Evil killer Jake Davison used a legally-owned shotgun to murder five people in 2021 (Image: PA)

New guidelines and rules for police were issued in the wake of the tragedy. But Mr Freeman said: “Most of the nearly 500,000 certificate holders use their firearms and shotguns responsibly for lawful recreation or as essential tools for work. But they are faced with a postcode lottery in the service they receive from firearms and explosive licensing units.

‌



“They, and the wider public, deserve a system that is clear, consistent and robust. We found the current system is none of these things. This is not the first time the inspectorate and others have raised concerns about firearms licensing, and change is now overdue.

“A new national firearms licensing authority should be created to better protect public safety. Further tragedies shouldn’t be required before action is taken.”

The latest damning document comes more than a decade after His Majesty’s Inspectorate of Constabulary and Fire & Rescue Services (HMICFRS) warned of weaknesses in the national firearms licensing system.

‌



View 3 Images The pump action shotgun (top) used by Jake Davison next to a police issue tactical single barrel 12-gauge pump action shotgun (below) (Image: PA)

The report points to inconsistent practice and decision-making, and calls for the 38 firearms and explosive licensing units (FELUs) in England and Wales to be abolished and replaced by a national body.

The watchdog also warned too much guidance is open to interpretation, licensing laws are outdated and overly complex and training for decision makers is inconsistent and sometimes non-existant.

‌



It also called for people who apply for firearm and shotgun licenses to undergo an in-person medical assessment and creating a digital verfication system to stop forged certificates being used to buy weapons.

Concerns have long been voiced about the licensing system. In 2023 Debbie Tedds, who led on the issue on the National Policing Council (NPCC) announced a national training programme would be introduced. This had been recommended by the Cullen Inquiry into the 1996 Dunblane massacre, but had not been implemented.

Sixteen children and a teacher were killed when a gunman opened fire opened fire at Dunblane Primary School in March 1996.

Article continues below

A Home Office spokesman said: “The UK has some of the toughest firearms laws in the world. We have taken significant steps in recent years to strengthen firearms licensing, including publication of robust statutory guidance for police, the introduction of mandatory medical checks, new national training for forces, and increases in firearms licensing fees.

“A number of recommendations in this report reflect work already underway. This includes a review of firearms licensing arrangements which is taking place as part of the Government's wider police reform agenda.

“We will work closely with policing partners to consider the report and take forward any further action that may be required to strengthen firearms controls and keep the public safe.”

News.title: Teen girl has dissolvable implant fitted as scaffold over her heart as she chases her rugby dream
News.content:
Teen girl has dissolvable implant fitted as scaffold over her heart as she chases her rugby dream

Lillie Yale, from Warrington, underwent surgery at Alder Hey Children's Hospital to have a biodegradable implant - around the size of a 10 pence piece - fitted to act as a scaffold over her heart

View 4 Images Lillie Yale becomes first person in UK to have dissolvable heart implant (Image: Becci Nichols/PA Wire)

A teenage girl hopes to fulfil her dream of playing pro rugby after becoming one of the first in the UK to have a dissolvable implant fitted to close a hole in her heart.

‌



Lillie Yale, 14, had a biodegradable implant - around the size of a 10 pence piece - fitted to act as a scaffold over her heart. This will allow her heart to heal itself over the coming months and years, before fully dissolving and leaving behind no trace.

‌



She had faced having a permanent metal device, which would have ruined her ambitions - but now she is already back playing on the rugby pitch. The procedure was performed by surgeons at Alder Hey Children's NHS Foundation Trust in Liverpool in June.

‌



Little boy who waited a world record eight years for a new heart is back home at last READ MORE :

NHS transplant landmark sees turbo charged lungs ‘breathe’ outside of body READ MORE :

View 4 Images Lillie had implant the size of a 10 pence piece fitted to heart (Image: Becci Nichols/PA Wire)

It is one of the first times the device, known as Memosorb, has been used on a patient with an atrial septal defect (ASD), a hole in the wall that divides the two upper chambers of the heart, in the UK.

Lillie’s mum, Becci Nichols, 38, from Warrington, Cheshire, described her daughter as healing perfectly and has since ran a 5k, visited a theme park and has returned to playing rugby.

‌



Memosorb is made of biomedical polymers, commonly used in dissolvable stitches.

View 4 Images Lillie hope to be a pro rugby player after operation (Image: Becci Nichols/PA Wire)

Dr Salim Jivanji, consultant paediatric cardiologist at Alder Hey, said: “The device looks very similar to a normal existing device that we have on the market. The difference being that it’s made out of a polymer.”

‌



He said with a traditional metal device, tissue would start lining the implant, while Memosorb acts as a “scaffold”, adding: “The body reacts with the structure of the device.

“It slowly covers it with the lining of the heart, and the polymer starts getting dissolved into carbon dioxide and water within the tissue and slowly disappears completely.

“I would say, in anywhere between six to 24 months the only thing you'll see is what looks like a normal septum with no hole in it.”

‌



According to Dr Jivanji, Lillie would not have been able to play rugby if she had a metal implant, as there is a risk it could be dislodged by heavy impact before her heart was fully healed. There is also a risk of mechanical stress to a metal device in the heart.

Alder Hey secured a special licence from the medicines regulator to use Memosorb.

Lillie said: “I’m really happy it’s all done now, and it’s amazing to know I was the first person in the UK to have this new type of implant. I’m enjoying doing the things I love and not having to worry about my heart.”

‌



She is now having check ups every couple of months to monitor her progress. Her mum said: “She is healing absolutely perfectly. She's been doing loads. She's back in her rugby full swing, and she did the Pretty Muddy 5k. She's been off to Alton Towers, and she's just getting on with everything now.”

View 4 Images The team at Alder Hey Children's Hospital (Image: Alder Hey Children's Hospital/PA Wire)

Becci was told that Lillie had ASD soon after she was born prematurely at 33 weeks. ASD affects roughly one to two in every 1,000 babies, and can sometimes be detected in adults as smaller holes cause fewer symptoms.

‌



Lillie had regular check ups and no symptoms until January 2025, when tests revealed her heart had become enlarged on the right side.

Becci said she was not too worried, as her own mother had discovered she had ASD when she was in her 40s: “I knew what it meant when it said that her heart was enlarged, and I knew how serious it can be.

“But it was only slightly enlarged, so I didn't worry too much. But I knew it needed rectifying.”

‌



Doctors initially said they would fit Lillie with an implant within two years, but her mother pushed for it to be sooner so the operation did not interrupt her GCSEs. It was only then Lillie was told she would not be able to continue with her sport if she had a traditional metal device put in her heart.

Becci said Dr Jivanji and his team “went above and beyond” to allow Lillie to “continue with her normal life”.

She said: “Sometimes you can leave an appointment feeling like someone is simply doing their job, but every member of the interventional cardiology team and nurses on ward 1C who cared for Lillie made us feel that they genuinely wanted the very best for her and for our family.

Article continues below

“Their kindness, compassion and dedication made an enormous difference to us throughout our journey.”

Dr Javanji also hailed the team at Alder Hey: “We constantly do really state-of-the-art kind of cases, but these cases require so much discussion, so much understanding...we advance innovation all the time, and it requires a real big team effort.”

News.title: 'We are doing more in fight against violence on women and girls - victims have waited too long'
News.content:
'We are doing more in fight against violence on women and girls - victims have waited too long'

Writing for The Mirror, Safeguarding Minister Satvir Kaur says she often thinks about the world her daughter will grow up in as she explains why the government is speeding up its violence against women and girls programme

View 2 Images Safeguarding Minister Satvir Kaur warns the scale of violence against women and girls is terrifying (Image: Ollie Thompson/Solent News)

Victims have waited too long. We are speeding up the fight against violence against women and girls.

‌



As a mum to a one-year-old daughter, I think often about the world she will grow up in.

‌



Like any parent, I would do anything to keep her safe. But I also want her to be free. Free to walk home at night without checking over her shoulder. Free to say no without fearing what might happen next.

‌



Free to go to work without being harassed. That should not be too much to ask. But for millions of women and girls in the UK, fear still shapes their everyday life.

The scale is terrifying. Around 900,000 people over the age of 16 experienced sexual assault or attempted assault in the year ending March 2025. Around 3.8 million experienced domestic abuse and 1.4 million experienced stalking. These are not just statistics. They represent mothers, daughters, friends and colleagues carrying pain. Living in dread. And feeling let down. We will not stand for it. The enormous scale of the challenge to tackle violence against women and girls, must to be met with the same level of ambition.

Andy Burnham faces pressure on council tax as two thirds of Brits brand system unfair READ MORE :

View 2 Images Police forces will have specialist rape and sexual violence teams in place by the end of next year (file image) (Image: pstonier)

‌



That is why today, the Prime Minister will announce he is bringing forward the deadline for every police force in England and Wales to have a specialist rape and sexual offence team. These teams will now be in place in every community by December 2027. A year and a half earlier than planned.

The teams will be dedicated to investigating some of the worst crimes imaginable. Their officers will have specialist skills and knowledge. They will support victims and survivors with trauma-informed care. And they will build stronger cases to put dangerous offenders behind bars. This is about going further and faster in ensuring no matter where you live the police have the expertise, resources and tools to hunt down rapists and sex offenders and give victims the support they deserve.

We know these specialist teams are only part of the solution, for policing to truly work for victims, it must also go hand in hand with stopping abusers and stalkers from terrorising their victims without consequences.

‌



That is why we are investing £13.3 million in new Violence Against Women and Girls Protection Order Teams, where up to 10 police forces will pioneer tougher ways to enforce court orders placed on perpetrators. The teams will try out new ways to make sure protection orders that protect victims are properly enforced, while helping to monitor perpetrators to prevent them causing further harm.

These orders cover a range of offences including domestic abuse, stalking, forced marriage and sexual offences. They can ban contact with the victim. They can force offenders to wear an electronic tag or attend programmes to change their behaviour. Importantly, if someone under an order breaks the rules, they could face up to five years in prison.

These measures are in addition to this government’s £53 million investment to expand the Drive Project across England and Wales. This scheme targets high-risk, serial domestic abusers to keep victims safe. Ten new areas are now benefiting from this proven approach where dedicated workers challenge their behaviour, with the police, local partners, and other services working together to protect survivors.

Article continues below

All of this is underpinned by a wave of measures, and part of our steadfast £1 billion mission, to halve violence against women and girls in a decade.

Victims and survivors remain at the heart of government action on this. To them directly, I say you deserve to be believed. You deserve to feel supported. And you deserve policing and protection that actually works.

This government and I will not stop until this is achieved.

News.title: Luton airport hit by lightning strike - flights cancelled and diverted
News.content:
Luton airport hit by lightning strike - flights cancelled and diverted

Operations at the busy airport were halted after air traffic control systems were hit by a lightning strike

View Image Travellers can reserve a 30-minute window to go through security (Image: Getty)

A lightning strike prompted flight cancellations and diversions at Luton Airport this evening, as bad weather conditions and storms swept across south east England.

‌



A spokesperson for the airport said operations were suspended between 5:40pm and 7:15pm, resulting in "a number of cancellations and diversions".

‌



Roads to and from the airport were flooded during the storm. A number of flights were diverted including Wizz Air flight W95378 from Turin to Luton which diverted to Gatwick airport and the Wizz Air flight W92601 from Prague which diverted to Stansted airport.

‌



"Flights to and from London Luton Airport have now resumed following an earlier suspension of operations caused by a lightning strike affecting Air Traffic Control equipment," the spokesperson told BBC South East.

"The disruption coincided with a period of severe weather across the area, resulting in flash flooding on local roads, and the airport approach.

Article continues below

"As operations return to normal, some flights may continue to experience delays or cancellations as airlines work to recover their schedules."

News.title: 'Labour finally has the numbers to show its asylum crackdown is working — but the job is far from done'
News.content:
'Labour finally has the numbers to show its asylum crackdown is working — but the job is far from done'

The number of asylum seekers housed in hotels has halved in just a year, as Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood declared the Government is "restoring control"

View Image Voice of the Mirror has its say...

Labour inherited an asylum system in disarray: hotels overflowing, claims taking too long, removals too low and public confidence badly damaged. Two years on, there are finally hard numbers showing that grip is being restored. The number of asylum seekers in hotels has halved in a year, the backlog has been slashed from its peak, asylum claims are down by a fifth, and removals are rising. Small boat arrivals are also now falling compared with last year. That matters because Labour promised competence after years of Conservative failure and, on one of the toughest issues facing any government, there are signs it is delivering. Of course, there is far more to do. The Channel crossings remain too high, and ministers cannot ease off. Immigration could well become the single issue that decides the next General Election, but these figures should give Labour confidence. If ministers keep driving the numbers down, they can show voters something their opponents offer mostly in slogans: evidence that firm, practical government can work.

‌



Middlesbrough cannot become lawless

Middlesbrough is living through a nightmare no community should have to endure. Nine people have died in five days. A seven-year-old girl and her aunt were killed in a house fire. Two police officers and five young men died in a horrific crash. Homes have been repeatedly rammed, there are reports of stabbings, and frightened families say they have spent years living under the shadow of rival gangs. Such violence cannot become normal. People who work hard, raise families and simply want to feel safe in their own homes are being intimidated into silence while criminals settle scores on residential streets. Cleveland Police now faces an enormous task, but it cannot do it with one hand tied behind its back. Ministers must give police the officers, intelligence and resources needed to break these gangs before other lives are lost.

Recipe for success

The Bake Off tent is about to get a whole lot hotter. Nigella Lawson’s wicked humour and easy flirtation have apparently met their match in Paul Hollywood, with arm-wrestling, teasing and enough innuendo to keep viewers entertained. Bake Off thrives on chemistry, and this pairing sounds like a recipe for TV gold.
