Sports.title: Ex-Liverpool star Jamie Carragher avoids being declared bankrupt despite ‘failing to pay huge tax bill’
Sports.content:
FOOTBALL’S Jamie Carragher has avoided being declared bankrupt after a tax dispute.

The Sky Sports pundit, 48, faced a High Court petition from the taxman after failing to pay a bill said to be between £700,000 and £800,000, the BBC reported.



The case was filed yesterday in London but the ex-Liverpool and England defender’s reps insisted the matter will be settled.

A judge would have declared him bankrupt had he not resolved it.



Carragher is thought to rake in more than £1million a year from TV punditry work.

He also does podcasts and is director of four firms.



Carragher’s spokesman told business newspaper City AM: “This is a private tax matter that should have been resolved sooner, and the appropriate steps are being taken today to settle it.

“It is understood that the matter will not proceed any further and will be resolved imminently.”

HMRC said it could not comment on Carragher’s finances.

It added: “We take a supportive approach to dealing with customers who have tax debts and do everything we can to help those who engage with us to get out of debt, such as offering instalment plans.



“We only petition for bankruptcy as a last resort.”

Sports.title: Fifa reduce Argentina players’ punishments for disgraceful World Cup final antics including Leandro Paredes punch-up
Sports.content:
FIFA have reduced the punishments for Argentina’s disgraceful World Cup final antics.

Thug Leandro Paredes was slapped with a TEN-match ban and fined £66,500 for his shocking behaviour at the end.



Nahuel Molina, Thiago Almada and coach Roberto Ayala also received bans and fines.

Molina got a seven-match ban, Almada one and Ayala three.



All four were involved in the horrendous brawl after full-time at the MetLife, with Paredes found guilty of three counts of “assault” after punching Spaniard Gavi and showing him to the ground.

Paredes was set to effectively be suspended from international football for more than a year.

However, Fifa approved the Argentine FA’s request to allow the bans to be served in Class A friendlies – as well as official games.

And it means the majority of Paredes’ suspension could be served before the end of 2026.

Argentina have not confirmed their fixture schedule but have already booked their spot at the 2030 World Cup as co-hosts and therefore do not need to go through qualifying.

The next Copa America, meanwhile, is not until 2028 – but there is no qualification for South American teams to play.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

But with the possibility for the three players – and coach – to serve their bans in friendlies, Argentina may decide to arrange a host of games as soon as possible.

There is now two international breaks in the autumn – a longer one where teams can cram in four matches across September and October before the regular two-break window in November.

Should Argentina arrange six Class A friendlies during that time, Paredes will have only four more to serve going into 2027 and Molina one, while Almada could play again from the end of September.

Incredibly, the Argentine FA are still hoping to cut the bans down and plan to appeal for reductions.



They were also hit with a whopping £237,000 fine and must play their next home match with a 50 per cent capacity for other violations during the tournament.

That included their ‘The Falklands are Argentine’ banner displayed after the semi-final win over England.

The ‘Malvinas’ banner saw Argentina found guilty of “using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature”.

In addition, the Argentines were held responsible for “team misconduct” after the game and “discrimination and racist abuse” by their fans as well as breaking rules on “order and security” at matches.

Argentina said in a statement on Thursday: “The Argentine Football Association (AFA) has formally requested Fifa to allow the sanctions imposed on its players during the 2026 World Cup final, and on the association itself, to be served in Class A friendly matches and/or official matches, whichever comes first.



“Based on the AFA’s submission, Fifa’s Disciplinary Committee has deemed the request approved in accordance with current regulations.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“Nevertheless, the AFA, in defense of its rights and those of its players, is awaiting the written justification for the decisions in order to file the corresponding appeals with FIFA’s Appeals Committee, with the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) potentially as the final recourse.”

Sports.title: Champions League group phase predicted by supercomputer with Man Utd having a nightmare after horror draw
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have been tipped to agonisingly miss out on the top eight of the Champions League league phase.

But three Premier League sides are backed to avoid the dreaded extra play-off round.



This year’s League Phase draw was conducted by Uefa bigwigs in Monaco, with Man Utd landing the likes of Bayern Munich and Atletico Madrid.

Boffins and brainiacs over at Football Ranked have crunched the numbers to predict the outcome.



And they reckon that United will finish NINTH – one place outside the much-coveted top eight that secures comfortable passage straight to the round of 16.

In addition to Bayern and Atleti, Michael Carrick‘s men will also take on Sporting CP, Roma, RB Leipzig, Villarreal, Como and Sabah.

Football Ranked projects the Red Devils to earn 14.1 points from these matches… only enough to finish ninth.

In both seasons since the Champions League was revamped, it has required 16 points to finish top eight.

If United do come ninth, they will be drawn in a play-off against either the team that places 23rd or 24th.

In Football Ranked’s simulation, this would mean a two-legged dust-up with either Lens or Lille – guaranteeing a trip to France’s North East.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Aston Villa, following a turbulent summer to say the least, are still tipped to come 10th.

This would see them take on the other of Lens or Lille.

The other three English clubs are all backed to secure safe progression.

Arsenal, who have glamour ties with Real Madrid and Bayern Munich to come, place second on 17.6 xPoints – only behind the German giants.



Two-time reigning champions Paris Saint-Germain are third, ahead of Manchester City in fourth on 16.9 xPoints.

Then come Real Madrid and Inter Milan – before Liverpool in seventh and Barcelona in eighth.

Big sides to miss out on the top eight include; Borussia Dortmund, Napoli and Atletico Madrid, who are all the way down in 19th.



The clubs to be eliminated for good include Spanish sides Real Betis and Villarreal, Istanbul giants Fenerbahce and Galatasaray and Ukrainians Shakhtar Donetsk, who will be playing their home matches at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Chelsea ratings: Malo Gusto stakes his claim for starting spot as Barco booed with every touch on solid Blues debut
Sports.content:
CHELSEA are into the third round of the Carabao Cup with minimal fuss as Danny Welbeck got off the mark in a 2-0 win at Stamford Bridge.

A goalless first half saw Chelsea test Luton‘s resolve with their very exciting trio of Estevao, Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers playing behind Danny Welbeck.



All of them had chances, but none could find the back of the net, with Rogers coming closest via a volley onto the crossbar.

And with young, tricky superstars stealing the show, it was only right that veteran goalscorer Welbeck stood up and was counted when the Blues needed a goal.



He headed home a Malo Gusto cross to give the Blues the lead just five minutes into the second half.

Chelsea were in the driving seat from then on, with Palmer almost scoring a wondergoal and getting minutes in the tank alongside Pedro Neto, Romeo Lavia and Joao Pedro from the bench.

Estevao capitalised on the Blues’ dominance with a late finish to make it 2-0 and see Xabi Alonso‘s side sail into the next round, where they will face Leeds at home.

Here is how SunSport Chelsea reporter Lloyd Canfield rated the players…

MIKE PENDERS – 7

There was a fair bit of pressure on young Mike Penders today, given the fact that Emiliano Martinez is about to join Chelsea to replace the man already in front of him, Robert Sanchez.

Nonetheless, he was great.



He looked commanding and particularly good with his feet, communicating well with those in front of him to deliver a performance more than good enough

BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

MALO GUSTO – 8

He tried and tried to get down the right side and deliver the ball into the box in the first half, without much luck.

In the second half, he got his golden touch, delivering a perfect cross onto the forehead of Welbeck to find the back of the net.

He defended well throughout with some great tackles and several other good crosses that unfortunately came to nothing.



The right-wing-back spot in Alonso’s side is far from locked down, and Gusto might still be in with a chance of nailing it with more performances like today.

JOSH ACHEAMPONG – 8

Was really impressive against Fulham, and was just as good again today, particularly with a crucial sliding tackle in the first half.

He sweeps things up brilliantly, steps into challenges well when required, and is good from passing out of the back too.



MAXENCE LACROIX – 7

Made more defensive contributions than any other Chelsea player, with several clearances, blocks, and interceptions.

Looks like a really strong signing already.

PEP CHAVARRIA – 6

Was noticeably good on the recovery and really solid at left-back for Chelsea.

It is hard not to see him as a great, understated signing so far — similar in many ways to when the Blues signed the legendary Cesar Azpilicueta.

VALENTIN BARCO – 6

Was booed every time he touched the ball by Luton fans for his World Cup wind-up antics with Argentina.



Nonetheless, he put in a solid midfield performance drifting out to the left side, creating some decent chances while remaining solid defensively.



REECE JAMES – 6

Came close after 19 minutes with a beautifully executed free-kick routine, but for a great save by Josh Keeley in the Luton net.

Was otherwise solid, keeping things ticking in midfield for the Blues with some good passing and defensive moments.

ESTEVAO – 8

Combined nicely with his team-mates, and if you thought the front three against Fulham was good, it could be even more frightening with this kid added to it.

He was a little hasty at times in the box and perhaps should have lifted his head up a bit more, but his persistence paid off when a low shot was deflected home to give the Blues a 2-0 lead.

A great showing from one of the most exciting young players on the planet, who will be looking for more minutes off the Blues’ ‘CPR’ front three.



COLE PALMER – 8

After his electric start in the Premier League against Fulham, Palmer really does look like the Palmer of old again – he looks so sharp and was at the heart of almost everything good Chelsea did going forward.

Almost scored a sensational effort from range with half an hour to go, but his curling effort licked the paint off the top of the crossbar.

MORGAN ROGERS – 7

Rattled the crossbar with a volley just before half-time having caused several problems for Luton throughout the first half.



DANNY WELBECK – 7

Linked up really nicely at times with Rogers and Palmer, but struggled to get into the game up top in the same ways that Joao Pedro often does in the first half.

In the second half though, he showed exactly why Chelsea signed him, he knows where the back of the net is.

Rose like a salmon to head home Malo Gusto’s perfect cross and give Chelsea the goal they needed.

SUBS:

JORREL HATO (MALO GUSTO, 67) – 6

Solid at the back, in Alonso’s back three system which probably suits him nicely, but didn’t have much to do.

PEDRO NETO (MORGAN ROGERS, 67) – 6

Settled nicely into the right wing back role once more and looked comfortable going in both directions.



ROMEO LAVIA (REECE JAMES, 67) – 6

Put in a heavy mistimed tackle, but was good overall at keeping things ticking, very similar to James before him.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

JOAO PEDRO (DANNY WELBECK, 75) – 6

Came close with a half chance late on, but it was saved by Keeley in the Luton goal.

JAMIE GITTENS (ESTEVAO, 80) – 7

Didn’t have much time to make an impact, but came close to scoring a beautiful goal from the left side with a left-footed effort coming off of the right post.

Sports.title: Chelsea 2 Luton 0: Danny Welbeck opens Stamford Bridge account on debut as Blues cruise through in Carabao Cup
Sports.content:
ALL’S Wel that ends well, and a debut goal for Chelsea’s new veteran striker set them on the road to victory.

Luton boss Jack Wilshere was hoping not to face any of the Blues front three who had torn Fulham apart on Monday night.



But although Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers both started, it was 35-year-old Danny Welbeck who set Xabi Alonso’s team on their way.

Welbeck, in for Joao Pedro, scored an old-fashioned centre forward’s goal just after half time, heading in a Malo Gusto cross.



And another of Alonso’s attacking options, Brazilian teenager Estevao, killed the game by forcing a Hakeem Odoffin goal with 12 minutes to go.

Wilshere’s side defended deep and doggedly. But they had neither enough possession, nor enough cutting edge when they did have the ball, to make their moneybags hosts sweat.

It was a comfortable night on the pitch for Chelsea, on a day with plenty of action off it, too.

Things are rarely as they seem at Stamford Bridge.

Alonso had said wantaway Enzo Fernandez would be involved. He wasn’t.

The Blues had insisted all summer they were happy with their goalkeepers. They were not.



BEST FREE BETS AND BETTING SIGN UP OFFERS

Before poor Mike Penders could even make his competitive debut, news broke the Blues had sealed a deal to bring in Emi Martinez to replace Robert Sanchez after the Spaniard’s horror show in the Monday night win at Fulham.

With one Argentinian absent and another not yet arrived, there was still someone for the Luton fans to boo.

Valentin Barco, who earned a clip round the ear from Jude Bellingham after the World Cup semi-final, made his first appearance and his every touch was jeered..

Barco will have to get used to it.



Just as Chelsea fans were becoming accustomed to their team playing in new manager Alonso’s favoured 3-4-2-1 formation, he took the opportunity to experiment.

Palmer and Rogers formed an attacking trident with Estevao behind Welbeck, and at times they were a blur of movement and neat touches.

Palmer forced a double save from Josh Keeley, then backheeled a free kick to Reece James, whose shot was pushed away acrobatically by the Luton ‘keeper.

It was attack against defence for long periods, with the visitors seeing little of the ball or the Chelsea half.



After Luton posed a brief threat which ended with a Benny Benagr shot being blocked, Barco played in Estevao, who sent a good chance well wide.

Shortly before the break, the Brazilian crossed for Rogers but his volley came back off the underside of the crossbar.

But the deadlock was broken within five minutes of the restart. Gusto had too much time to cross and Welbeck was given room to head home from relatively close range.

Luton had to react and they did, even enjoying some possession at last in enemy territory.

Nevertheless the home side were by far the more threatening, and Welbeck fired wide from a Palmer through ball.



The Chelsea No10, oozing confidence in front of watching England boss Thomas Tuchel, then clipped the bar with a 20-yard effort.

Luton’s Palmer, Kasey, was not too far off target from range, but Penders was having very little to do.

After Alonso sent on Pedro for old man Welbeck, Palmer played in teenager Estevao. The shot seemed to be off target but Odoffin could not stop himself helping it into the net.

Keeley saved a stoppage-time effort from Pedro and Jamie Gittens hit the post.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Welbeck will surely be back on the bench for the visit of former club Brighton to Stamford Bridge on Sunday.



But he showed he has more than just experience to add to Alonso’s still-young squad.

Sports.title: Moment fans call Gianni Infantino a ‘f***ing w***er’ as UEFA prepares criminal proceedings against Fifa boss
Sports.content:
UEFA is preparing criminal proceedings against Gianni Infantino, it emerged yesterday — as furious fans called the Fifa boss a “f***ing w***er” while he presented a trophy.

Infantino aborted outrageous plans to sell shares in the World Cup after Uefa threatened a boycott.



It dropped its threat, but legal papers show the European football governing body has now pledged to subpoena Fifa and US financial institutions linked to the plot.

It would be launched in Switzerland, where Fifa has its main HQ.



A legal document said: “Uefa and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other Fifa officials and advisers for criminal mismanagement.”

Meanwhile, fans in Vietnam hurled abuse at Infantino after he turned up at a cup final in Hanoi.

Video showed them calling the Swiss-Italian a “f***ing w***er” in English, while he smiles and waves back.

The toe-curling scenes at the My Dinh National Stadium — where Vietnam beat Thailand to win the ASEAN title — were witnessed by a Brit bar boss.

The 40-year-old Man Utd fan, who asked not to be named, said: “It was absolutely hilarious.

“He obviously thought he could come here and get away from all the scandal about him selling off the World Cup but was badly mistaken.



“It was close enough for him to hear because I saw him look up and he even waved — it was ridiculous. Then more people joined in.”

Infantino, 56, later gushed on Instagram of his visit: “Moments like this embody what Fifa is all about.”

The Fifa president, whose scheme was pulled after a furious backlash, is up for re-election next March.

Sports.title: Jamie Vardy lands shock rights to show Bundesliga in huge broadcasting change as he searches for new club
Sports.content:
JAMIE VARDY is set to take the Bundesliga by storm after his podcast has secured the rights to Germany’s top flight football league.

The ex-England striker, 39, has won the deal from Gary Neville’s The Overlap podcast.



As well as featuring on the Jamie Vardy’s Having A Party podcast show, he has landed a mega TV deal with Samsung TV.

Samsung have created a dedicated channel, which will also be available on Amazon Prime.



The rights focus on live games, which start on Friday evening at 7.30pm UK time.

A source said: “This is a huge move for Jamie as he expands his talents in broadcasting, while still playing football.



“He’s buzzing to reach Bundesliga fans and chat with star guests about action on the pitch.

“He’s hoping to creat a real community with his podcast and is loving getting into the nitty gritty of the sport.”

The ex-Leicester City captain Jamie’s got some brilliant guests planned.

That includes former team-mates, celeb pals and is even going to bring on his wife Becky.



CASINO SPECIAL – BEST CASINO BONUSES FROM £10 DEPOSITS

It comes after entertainment powerhouse Banijay Entertainment unveiled Players Network in June, produced by Workerbee.

Jamie said of the project previously: “I am excited to launch the podcast with one of the major players in the game, Banijay Entertainment.

“I am still an active player.

“But having an opportunity to chat football and have a banter off the pitch is something that I am really looking forward to.”



The Sun reached out to Banijay for comment.

Sports.title: How KSI transformed high-flying Dagenham & Redbridge as he spearheads influencers’ takeover of football
Sports.content:
WE’RE nearly half a year into KSI’s tenure as a non-league football club owner, and it couldn’t have gone better.

Back in March, the YouTuber acquired a 20 per cent stake in National League South’s Dagenham & Redbridge, alongside the Happy Fan Group and former QPR owner Tony Fernandes.





His plans for the club were clear. He declared: “I’m gonna take it to the moon”. And he wasn’t joking.

Since the vlogger, worth an estimated £80million, entered the boardroom at Victoria Road the Daggers have had attendance boosts, as well as commercial growth off the pitch.

While on the pitch, they’re sitting proud at the top of the National League South.

It’s fair to say that KSI has transformed Dagenham & Redbridge with his lofty ambitions.

And, he has spearheaded the influencers’ takeover of football.

He manifested it

FIFA played a huge role in KSI, 33, getting where he is today.

His YouTube series, Race to Division One, where he started in Division 10 in the videos games’ competitive online mode and tried to get a team to the top flight, mirrors his real life now.

It put him on the social media stratosphere, and on the way to an extraordinary number of followers.





Across his YouTube, Instagram, and TikTok accounts he has well over 50 million now.

It’s a huge reach that’s benefitted Dagenham’s popularity.

To give you some context. Just days before KSI announced his involvement with Dagenham, only 1,247 people watched their home defeat to AFC Totton.

Fast-forward a few days and 2,281 fans watched a 1-0 win against Dorking.

Better still, KSI live-streamed himself taking in the game, walking around the stadium, and meeting the fanbase.

In one clip he was sat next to co-investor and player/assistant manager, Andy Carroll.

Astonishingly, the video got more than 300,000 views. When you think the most a non-league club can dream of attendance-wise is around 10,000 bums on seats, it’s a wild scenario to imagine that much interest.

For his next trick, KSI followed messieurs Ryan Reynolds and Rob McElhenney in going down the documentary route.



Instead of appearing on a streaming platform like Disney, though, he kept the production in-house.

The first episode of Race To The Top: The Dagenham & Redbridge Story, released back in June, has been viewed an astonishing 800,000 times.

Again, more eyes are watching this success story unfold in real-time.

How does that boost the coffers?

In terms of revenue, the club have kept mum on their financial figures.

A fake story that they sold over 3.7 million replica shirts last season was quickly rebuffed.

However, thanks to the KSI effect, commercial and broadcast partnerships have been secured.

They have partnered with DAZN to broadcast select fixtures, as well as produce creator-led storytelling – starring the main man himself.

Sponsors Formation Games, Gemini Sports, West and Coe, Brunel Shipping, and Wolf Competitions are onboard, as the club coffers start to swell.



Fashion studio Acid FC were also drafted in to create a special-edition collaborative away kit, designed to bring in fans who just love collecting football shirts.

This summer the club recorded a huge overhaul of their squad, with a whole team of new signings.

Coached by Lee Allinson, who joined in early May, Dagenham have won their first four matches and are looking an early bet for promotion.

A new trend in football

KSI’s involvement with Dagenham has now kickstarted the influencer-led football revolution.

Intriguingly, the East London side kicked off their league campaign this season against another team owned by a man who made his money through a major global influencer marketing company.

Harry Hugo co-founded The Goat Agency, turning it into a major international enterprise, before selling it to WPP for a reported nine-figure sum in 2023.

Soon after, he visited a Ferrari garage with his friends – with his eyes on a 458 Spyder in Black.



Instead, he bought Farnham Town.

He told Sky Sports: “My mate asked me why I was considering buying it.

“My only answer was that it would be fun. That wasn’t a good enough answer, so I challenged my mates to come up with something that would provide as much fun for the money.

“The first suggestion was, why don’t we buy a football club – and I thought that was quite a good idea!”

Up north, Burnley have also welcomed YouTubers onto their board.

The five-man group Dude Perfect became minority owners in 2023.

Their partnership includes front-of-shirt sponsorships for junior and academy kits, brand-building collaborations, and naming rights for the annual youth cup.



In return, Dude Perfect’s posse, Tyler Toney, Garrett Hilbert, Cody Jones, and brothers Coby and Cory Cotton hope to sell the Clarets to a worldwide fanbase, starting with their 60 million plus subscribers.

Forget Hollywood stars, it’s the influencers who are now taking over the game.

Sports.title: Mo Salah endures nightmare as Liverpool icon's manager QUITS after Europa League failure
Sports.content:
Mo Salah endures nightmare as Liverpool icon's manager QUITS after Europa League failure

Trabzonspor signed Mo Salah from Liverpool to help fire them into the Europa League, but the Turkish side have failed to even qualify after losing 5-0 on aggregate to Ferencvaros

View 2 Images Mo Salah was hooked during the heavy defeat (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

Mo Salah's manager at new club Trabzonspor has QUIT immediately after their hopes of qualifying for the Europa League were crushed by Ferencvaros. Salah's side were hammered 4-0 in Hungary, having lost the play-off first leg at home by a single goal.

‌



It was only the Liverpool legend's third start since joining the Turkish side on a free transfer earlier this month. Salah scored his first two goals for Trabzonspor against Istanbul Basaksehir on Sunday, and he hoped to lead their comeback against Ferencvaros.

‌



But things got off to a terrible start when Republic of Ireland international Callum O'Dowda headed the hosts in front on the night, extending their lead on aggregate. Trabzonspor attempted to regroup at half-time, but their slim hopes of making it through were all but dashed when they conceded two more goals and had a man sent off in the space of five minutes.

‌



Trabzonspor boss Fatih Tekke had seen enough and substituted Salah in the 64th minute, presumedly with Monday's game away to Amed Sportif in the Turkish Super Lig in mind. The Egyptian was signed for his ability to deliver on the European stage but won't get a chance to show it following Trabzonspor's abject failure.

‌



Salah, 34, wasn't the only former Premier League star responsible for the heavy defeat. Andre Onana - on loan from Manchester United - was in goal, while ex-Manchester City defender Stefan Savic and former Southampton striker Paul Onuachu were also named in Tekke's starting line-up.

In a bombshell post-match interview, the Trabzonspor manager announced live on air that he was resigning with immediate effect. "I am resigning from a very honourable position," Tekke revealed.

"Today's defeat is unacceptable. Misfortunes and bad luck are all acceptable, but I cannot accept this. I cannot sleep with this feeling. May everyone forgive me. We did our best."

‌



Are Liverpool better off without Mo Salah? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Trabzonspor boss Fatih Tekke announced his resignation in a post-match interview (Image: Hakan Burak Altunoz/Anadolu via Getty Images)

The 48-year-old added: "We had a very sad night. Of course, the reason is me and my team! It was a sad night for both our country and our club.

‌



"Until the red card, it seemed like a match that would go well. As a result, we couldn't qualify for the Europa League. For 18 months, day and night, my team and I have been thinking about how we can do better.

"The team will be much, much better, that's for sure. I won't elaborate further. Nobody knows. As of now, I am resigning from my position after 18 months. I think I have the right to punish myself in this way."

Sports.title: Matteo Guendouzi continues to shine light on Mikel Arteta's shrewdest Arsenal transfer
Sports.content:
Matteo Guendouzi continues to shine light on Mikel Arteta's shrewdest Arsenal transfer

Matteo Guendouzi’s antics in Lyon shone a colourful light on the abrupt end to what had been shaping up to be an Arsenal career that had decent potential

View 2 Images Matteo Guendouzi caused chaos after Fenerbahce beat Lyon (Image: OLIVIER CHASSIGNOLE / AFP via Getty Images)

Of all the contributory factors in Arsenal’s title-winning season of 2025-26, discipline was the one that tended not to get mentioned too much.

‌



Over the course of their triumphant Premier League campaign, none of Mikel Arteta’s players received a red card. Only Manchester City and Brighton could boast the same record. And Arsenal’s collection of 51 yellow cards was the lowest tally in the Premier League by some distance.

‌



They might not be unfamiliar with dark arts but this is currently an Arsenal team that keeps its composure. Which is why Arteta would be allowed a wry smile if he saw the chaos caused by Matteo Guendouzi in Lyon on Wednesday night after he helped Fenerbahce to a 2-1 win that means they are in this season’s Champions League.

‌



Guendouzi made a reasonably compelling case for his defence. “For 90 minutes, even longer with the warm-up, they insulted my family,” he said, referring to the Lyon crowd. “It’s something that gets to you. They insulted my mother and my family, and to me, that was disrespectful. Beyond that, if we can’t celebrate the way we want anymore, I think that is a shame.”

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Fair enough. But look at the footage of Guendouzi’s celebrations and it is clear he is goading the Lyon players and supporters. He has to take his share of the blame for the violent scenes which have gone viral on social media.

‌



And that will not be a surprise to Arteta. After almost eight years in charge, the significance of one decision in 2020 has, understandably, been forgotten. But Guendouzi’s antics in Lyon shone a colourful light on the abrupt end to what had been shaping up to be an Arsenal career that had decent potential.

And it marked Arteta down as a manager who wants no nonsense from his players and is not prepared to indulge nonsense, no matter how talented the player is. Guendouzi certainly caught the eye when he was recruited as a 19-year-old from Lorient by Unai Emery in 2018.

View 2 Images Mikel Arteta never quite gelled with Matteo Guendouzi (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



While Emery indulged the teenager, Arteta was quickly unimpressed when he succeeded his fellow Spaniard. During a mid-season training camp in Dubai, Guendouzi was involved in a bust-up with members of the Gunners staff after having an altercation with a team-mate.

Arteta was deeply unimpressed but Guendouzi managed to convince the new manager he deserved a chance. But his time under Arteta came to an unhappy end after Guendouzi was involved in a fracas after a defeat at Brighton.

Guendouzi actually escaped any official sanction after grabbing Neal Maupay - no stranger to controversy himself - but Arteta had seen enough. He called Guendouzi into a meeting and was said to be unimpressed by the French youngster’s attitude. There was little doubt about his talent but Arteta was clearly not taken by his character.

Article continues below

He spent the next season at Hertha Berlin and another loan arrangement at Marseille was made permanent. Guendouzi then had a couple of seasons at Lazio before Fenerbahce paid £25million for him early this year.

It is clear Guendouzi is a talented operator but his involvement in another bust-up - and a quite spectacular one at that - is a reminder that Arteta did exactly the right thing all that time ago.

Sports.title: UEFA preparing criminal proceedings against FIFA president Gianni Infantino
Sports.content:
UEFA preparing criminal proceedings against FIFA president Gianni Infantino

UEFA are trying everything in their power to oust Gianni Infantino from the FIFA presidency in the wake of the scandal over an attempt to sell shares in the World Cup

View 2 Images Gianni Infantino is under huge pressure from UEFA (Image: Getty Images)

UEFA is considering launching criminal proceedings against FIFA president Gianni Infantino in an audacious attempt to oust him from power.

‌



The scandal in the wake of Infantino's failed attempt to sell shares in FIFA tournaments to external investors has faded in recent weeks. But legal documents filed in the United States shows that UEFA has now stepped up their efforts to topple Infantino.

‌



UEFA is subpoenaing FIFA and the financial institutions involved in the failed plot in an attempt to obtain documents. European football's governing body then plans to launch legal action in Switzerland - the home of FIFA.

‌



As reported by Sky News, the document states: "UEFA and other interested parties are preparing to bring criminal claims in Switzerland against Infantino and possibly other FIFA officials and advisors for criminal mismanagement under Article 158 of the Swiss Criminal Code and such further or alternative charges as the developed factual record may support, arising out of the secretive structuring, valuation, financing, and marketing of a transaction that inflicted direct and concrete injury on FIFA's reputation, governance authority, and commercial relationships to the detriment of FIFA as well as its 211 members, including UEFA's 55 member associations."

As well as Infantino, the application in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York is against JP Morgan Bank, planned lead investor Thrive Capital and its CEO, Joshua Kushner.

‌



The legal document alleges: "It was a vehicle for Infantino and that small circle to acquire a permanent stake in and otherwise profit from FIFA's most valuable assets to the detriment of FIFA, its members, and other parties within the football family."

The news comes just a day after UEFA dropped its threat to boycott FIFA tournaments. European football's governing body feels its two conditions have been met, namely that FIFA drops the idea of selling off stakes in its tournaments and that they receive assurances it doesn't happen again.

UEFA and its president Aleksander Ceferin have been leading the campaign against Infantino this summer. The body's 55 member associations are due to meet on Thursday ahead of the Champions League draw in Monaco, where the situation will be discussed further.

‌



View 2 Images Aleksandr Ceferin is leading the campaign against Gianni Infantino (Image: Nick Potts/PA Wire)

UEFA have received support from Confederation for North America and the Caribbean (CONCACAF) and the Asian Football Confederation (AFC). However, Infantino has managed to claw back support from elsewhere.

African Football Confederation (CAF) and Confederation for South America (Conmebol) have thrown their support behind the Swiss bureaucrat, who will go for re-election next year.

‌



If UEFA fail to oust Infantino, then they will have to support a rival candidate in the FIFA elections next year. "Things are changing every day. Every day, there are different discussions. I didn't speak with him. But there are two options," Ceferin said on The Rest is Politics.

"One option is that he realises that he doesn't have the support, and that's not only a political support of the ones who vote, but the political support of football community, the political support of fans, the political support of the players, former players, coaches.

"And the second option that he goes to the elections in March, but in that case, I think he will have a candidate against him. I don't know yet who."

Sports.title: Bradley Barcola 'farce' continues trend that has transformed Liverpool's reputation
Sports.content:
Bradley Barcola 'farce' continues trend that has transformed Liverpool's reputation

Liverpool once had a reputation of being one of the shrewdest recruitment teams in world football - but a change of approach has led to some very differing results

View 4 Images Bradley Barcola is closing in on a massive transfer to Liverpool (Image: Getty)

Liverpool have long since judged their standards alongside those belonging to bitter rivals Manchester United.

‌



European Cups, league title wins and the talents of managers and footballers alike have been barometers the two English giants like to measure themselves against.

‌



Liverpool have held the upper hand in recent times. The Merseysiders have been English champions twice since United last managed the feat in 2013.

‌



And have also won a sixth Champions League/European Cup, which is now double the amount of times United have lifted club football's biggest trophy.

And it wasn't too long ago Liverpool's owners were sitting back and watching United spend cash like it was going out of fashion, on expensive signings who turned out to be a complete waste of money.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



FOLLOW OUR LIVERPOOL FB PAGE! Latest Reds news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

There is no point listing them. We don't have enough time.

In that same period, Liverpool conducted their own business with ruthless stealth. Big targets were kept under the radar, until a deal was so close to being completed it would be made public.

‌



This happened with the likes of Virgil Van Dijk, Alexis Mac Allister, Alisson and Luis Diaz, to name but a few.

Liverpool resembled a well-oiled machine who got the job done - and on their terms. But times have changed.

View 4 Images Liverpool were once heralded as the transfer kings - but in recent years their crown has slipped (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

‌



Because in recent seasons Liverpool have decided to take a change of tact, not to mention a leaf out of United's soiled book.

We know new investor Jeff Bezos has more dollars than sense, but he's not been around long enough to be blamed for what can only be described as a haphazard approach to luring new talent to Anfield.

Last summer Liverpool broke the British transfer record not once, but twice in a matter of weeks. Florian Wirtz arrived for £116m, before Alexander Isak followed suit at a cost of £125m.

‌



Both have been huge disappointments. And fast forward 12 months and Liverpool could be about to break their own record again.

Negotiations are taking place with PSG about a deal for Bradley Barcola, with a deal likely to come close to the fee paid to Newcastle for Isak.

View 4 Images Florian Wirtz and Alexander Isak both struggled in their first seasons with Liverpool

‌



Under normal circumstances, such a move would leave supporters feeling overwhelmed excitement.

The problem is, Liverpool have turned to Barcola in desperation less than a week before the transfer window closes, having pulled out of the bidding for Brighton's Yankuba Minteh.

Liverpool bid £60m, but Brighton wanted £80m. Brighton's track record of making profit on previously unheralded talent is second to none.

‌



But despite this, Brighton knew on this occasion at least, how desperate Liverpool had become - and looked to take full advantage. This isn't Brighton's fault. It's Liverpool's.

Liverpool have created a situation where every selling club now knows how keen they are to make quick signings. Millions will be added to the value of a target.

‌



What makes the scenario even more baffling is that Liverpool knew in March Mo Salah would be leaving. How has it taken this long for them to attempt to sign another right winger?

The gaps in the squad are clear for all to see. New manager Andoni Iraola needs a new winger, defensive midfielder and forward.

But Liverpool have still not signed a player they've been negotiating for since the end of the World Cup. The situation is farcical.

‌



But perhaps the most negligible aspect of the whole shambles is how owners FSG have allowed sporting director Richard Hughes to continue in charge of signings, despite the fact he's expected to leave in the coming weeks?

View 4 Images Richard Hughes remains in charge, despite the fact he is set to leave Anfield (Image: Liverpool FC via Getty Images)

Should he have not been put on gardening leave instead?

‌



Liverpool finished fifth in the table last season, 25 points behind champions Arsenal. And nothing they've done this summer suggests this gap is going to be closed anytime soon.

Liverpool can change their squad all they like. But it's a change of approach to how this is done, which is needed the most.

Sports.title: Good Good Golf withdraw from sponsoring PGA Tour event after controversial video
Sports.content:
Content creators Good Good Golf pull out of title sponsoring PGA Tour event in November, saying "we recognise that we have work to do as an organisation"; Brand apologised for publishing a video for a Callaway driver last week that has been accused of portraying violence against women

The PGA Tour agrees with Good Good Golf's 'decision to use this time to focus on their organisation and the work ahead'

Good Good Golf has withdrawn from sponsoring a PGA Tour event this autumn following its controversial video promoting a new Callaway driver.

The video published last week by the popular content creators was subsequently deleted after widespread criticism that it portrayed violence against women.

The video showed a man shoving a woman who was reaching for his new Callaway driver to the ground, before warning her not to touch the club as she lay on the ground.

Good Good Golf apologised in a social media statement and Callaway Golf admitted 'mistakes were made' over their handling of the incident.

The company had been due to title sponsor a new PGA Tour event in Austin in November but have now pulled out of doing so.

In a statement on Thursday, Good Good Golf said: "After thoughtful discussion with the PGA Tour and careful reflection, we have decided to step away as sponsor of the tour event in Austin this fall.

"We recognise that we have work to do as an organisation, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we learn from this situation.

Coventry vs Hull, Saturday 3pm

There is something rather appealing about backing goals when two promoted sides meet this early in a Premier League season. For starters, the last 36 fixtures of this nature has seen over 1.5 goals hit on 35 occasions.

Also, the last five newly-promoted teams to play their first home game of the season have won it, so history is certainly pointing towards a positive afternoon for Coventry. But Frank Lampard's side have some defensive issues to iron out after Arsenal exposed them in a 3-0 defeat on the opening weekend before conceding two at Plymouth in the Carabao Cup.

Hull, meanwhile, could hardly have made a better start. They stunned Manchester United 2-0 last weekend, showing the aggression, organisation and set-piece threat that could make them awkward opponents for plenty of teams this season.

There is also a betting-system angle that makes me reluctant to write off the visitors. A one-unit stake on Hull whenever they have started a game bigger than 2/1 since the beginning of last season would have returned a £34.96 profit. That includes away wins at Millwall twice, Middlesbrough and, most impressively, United last weekend.

The safer route is to take the result out of the question and both teams to score and over 2.5 goals at Evens with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-2

Tottenham vs Newcastle United, Saturday 5:30pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

There are times in betting when you have to decide whether a bad performance is a warning sign or a price-making opportunity.

I'm leaning towards the latter with Tottenham.

The 3-0 defeat at Brentford was awful. There is no dressing it up. Spurs looked disjointed, physically behind the game and defensively vulnerable, while Roberto De Zerbi admitted afterwards that his side were "not a team" yet.

But I'm prepared to give them another chance.

De Zerbi has an excellent record in the game immediately following a defeat of three or more goals, winning eight of 11 such matches, with his teams averaging 2.1 goals. That's a big enough sample to make me sit up as Tottenham are available at 6/5 with Sky Bet. It's a bet.

There were mitigating circumstances at Brentford, too.

Spurs had five competitive debutants in their starting XI, while Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were unavailable and several players had either returned late from the World Cup or endured disrupted pre-seasons.

It doesn't excuse the performance, but it does suggest that some of what went wrong is fixable.

And there is now a sense of the cavalry returning.

I'm not suddenly convinced Spurs are back to being the team many expected them to be before a ball was kicked. But the home win price looks quite tasty at odds-against as this feels like a classic reaction game for De Zerbi and Tottenham.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1

Chelsea vs Brighton, Sunday 2pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

Chelsea just might have the best attack in the Premier League. Monday's night win at Fulham got tongues wagging on that front.

It was aggressive. It was vertical. And it was quite chaotic.

Xabi Alonso used Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers operating behind João Pedro. The trio combined for all three Chelsea goals and Alonso subsequently described them as central to what he is building. They were electric.

However, Chelsea conceded twice as Robert Sánchez made another costly error and Fulham had opportunities to punish a defence that looked vulnerable when Chelsea's aggressive shape was exposed. That lack of defensive cohesion stems from the lack of authority from the goalkeeper.

Are Chelsea now structurally a team capable of producing these types of matches regularly? I'd be confident of that answer being yes, meaning there is value in backing their games to be high scoring before the market full adjusts.

Over 2.5 goals and both teams to score should be a staple Chelsea bet to follow in the coming weeks, starting here at 4/5 with Sky Bet.

Leeds vs Brentford, Sunday 2pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

Brentford fired in 26 shots and registered an expected goals total of 3.87 last weekend - it was the highest xG of the opening weekend.

However, the Bees aren't the same animal on the road to the extent they've only averaged 1.15 goals per game under Keith Andrews. One of those was this corresponding fixture last season which ended 0-0 - a game which bored everyone to tears. It was football as a form of punishment for those watching. Neither side created a big chance and the combined xG was just 0.98. The ultimate stalemate.

There is something about this fixture that makes me think we could be in for another game where both managers are more interested in avoiding defeat than throwing bodies forward. The draw and under 2.5 goals is 100/30 with Sky Bet and that's a price worth respecting.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1

Sunderland vs Fulham, Sunday 2pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

Everyone quite rightly came away from Fulham's 3-2 defeat to Chelsea talking about Cole Palmer.

But what about Josh King?

The Fulham teenager was not too far behind Palmer in the wow-factor stakes.

King scored Fulham's first goal at Craven Cottage. He finished the game with three shots, two on target and was a constant threat for a Fulham side that looked dangerous in transition. This wasn't a case of a young player popping up in the right place once and taking advantage. King was Fulham's key man in attack. He looked willing to carry the ball, take responsibility and get shots away.

The market is still treating him like an emerging youngster rather than someone who can genuinely be one of Fulham's primary attacking outlets.

The 9/2 for King to score with Sky Bet therefore looks interesting in what looks a very tough clash to call.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-1

Manchester United vs Ipswich, Sunday 4:30pm, live on Sky Sports - PLAY SUPER 6 HERE!

You don't have to convince me twice to back a set-piece angle.

Manchester United won just 42 per cent of their duels in their 2-0 defeat to Hull - the lowest figure recorded by any Premier League team on the opening weekend. That lack of physical bite is a concern in a league where you simply cannot afford to be second best in the fundamentals.

Since Michael Carrick took charge, United have conceded 20 Premier League goals in 18 matches - 10 of them from set plays. That's an extraordinary ratio. Only Bournemouth and Leeds have conceded a higher proportion of their goals from set-pieces during that period.

And Hull provided the perfect example of how to exploit it, scoring both goals from dead-ball situations in their stunning victory at Old Trafford.

So why should we expect Ipswich to be any different?

Dara O'Shea is the first-contact man on set pieces for Town and averaged 0.95 shots per 90 over the last 12 months. That's a great number for a defender and tells us something about how aggressive Ipswich are in targeting him. He is Evens for at least one shot and 18/1 to score with Sky Bet.

SCORE PREDICTION: 2-1 | JONES KNOWS' BEST BET: Dara O'Shea +1 shots (Evens with Sky Bet)

Aston Villa vs Arsenal, Monday 8pm, live on Sky Sports

Christos Tzolis looks like fun.

The new signing from Club Brugge hit the ground running, producing a direct, fearless performance on his Premier League debut in the win over Coventry. He was constantly looking to attack his man, drive into dangerous areas and get shots away.

He finished with four shots and eight touches in the opposition box - more than any Arsenal player on both counts.

And at 15/8 with Sky Bet to score in a game Arsenal are taken to win, he rates as a player to consider.

Also, Matty Cash is 11/4 to be booked with Sky Bet. That's a great bet. Why? Because he looks likely to have the job of dealing with Tzolis.

And that could be an uncomfortable mission for a player who was carded 12 times last season.

The Greek winger brings an excellent card-drawing record from his time at Club Brugge, drawing a card every 206 minutes. That's a very healthy strike-rate.

SCORE PREDICTION: 1-2

Sports.title: Wigan thump Hull KR to go back top after emotional Boston tributes
Sports.content:
Wigan celebrated the life of the late, great Sir Billy Boston by sweeping aside a weakened Hull KR side 46-0 in their Betfred Super League clash at a sodden Brick Community Stadium.

Boston, who was made rugby league's first knight last year, died on Tuesday morning, four days after the funeral of his wife Lady Joan.

An emotional pre-match tribute saw Boston's son Stephen carry a Wigan shirt bearing his name onto the halfway line, where it was draped over the same throne upon which Boston had sat when the club celebrated his knighthood last July.

Two seats were left vacant in the directors' box in tribute to Boston and his wife, and the home team warmed up in black T-shirts emblazoned with his number two prior to an impeccably-observed minute's silence.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player A tribute to Sir Billy Boston is played out ahead of the Super League game between Wigan Warriors and Hull KR

Image: Sir Billy and Lady Joan Boston's seats were left vacant in the directors' box (SWpix.com image)

Once the action got under way, Matt Peet's men duly racked up a record-extending 13th consecutive Super League win that restored them to the top of the table ahead of Leeds' trip to St Helens on Friday.

Liam Marshall helped himself to a hat-trick, while Zach Eckersley - the latest recipient of the number two jersey that Boston made his own - scored twice in a nine-try show to which Adam Keighran contributed a try and 10 points with the boot.

Rovers head coach Willie Peters, battling injuries and suspensions, named a team featuring three club debutants with an eye on next week's home clash with Huddersfield.

The defending champions are in real danger of slumping out of the top six and while the commitment of their weakened side could not be questioned, they were miles away from posing any kind of threat to a home team clearly hungry to wrest back their title.

Image: Wigan Warriors' Liam Marshall is congratulated after scoring the first try (SWpix.com image)

The visitors held out for 10 minutes with Bill Leyland making a fine try-saving tackle on Jai Field before Marshall crossed for the game's first converted try.

Field zoomed onto Harry Smith's clever kick to double Wigan's lead, then Smith again was the instigator with a perfectly delivered 40-20 kick to set up Eckersley's opener on the right flank.

The half-time damage could have been worse for Rovers, as both Smith and Marshall had further tries disallowed, before Marshall and Eckersley each scored their second amid a torrential downpour just before the break.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Liam Marshall scored this acrobatic try for Wigan Warriors against Hull KR in the Super League

Keighran converted his own try after Eckersley tapped back a Smith kick 12 minute into the second half, but Rovers dug deep and enjoyed a sustained spell of pressure on the Rovers line, forcing a series of drop-outs and bulling close through Arthur Mourgue and Sam Luckley.

Just after the hour mark Rovers thought they had been rewarded for their efforts when one of their debutants, Frankie Dearlove, splashed over in the corner, but replays showed a Wigan arm had prevented the ball being grounded, and the try was chalked off.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Wigan Warriors head coach Matt Peet reflects on their win over Hull KR in the Super League.

Marshall completed his hat-trick by blazing down the left with 12 minutes on the clock, and Wardle also jinked over after fine work from Field as the hosts wrapped up victory in a manner that would have made their late, great hero proud.

Sky Sports will show every game of the Super League live this season, including two matches each round exclusively live. The remaining five matches will be broadcast on Sky Sports+.

Sports.title: Muniz nets first goal in a year as Fulham ease past Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Rodrigo Muniz was finally all smiles again as he ended a year-long goal drought to help earn Alvaro Arbeloa his first win and see Fulham breeze past AFC Wimbledon 3-0 in the Carabao Cup.

The Brazilian netted his first goal since August 16, 2025 with a fine header back across goal from Kenny Tete's cross after Emile Smith Rowe had nodded the Cottagers in front to all-but secure a third-round trip to West Ham even before half-time.

"Goals are very important for strikers, we know that, and Rodrigo is working hard," Arbeloa said after full-time. "We have very good strikers with him and with Gonzalo [Garcia] - different strikers, but we need both, and both will be very important for us.

"They both scored tonight and they are so happy in the dressing room."

Wimbledon had held strong for the opening half-hour at Craven Cottage in the first ever meeting between the two London sides, but never recovered from falling behind.

Fulham created a succession of chances to add to their lead after the break, with half-time debutant Macaulay Zepa a live wire on the right flank and unfortunate not to mark his first appearance with a goal.

The youngster did at least get an assist in added time, freeing big-money summer signing Goncalo Garcia to race past Dan Sweeney and ride a challenge from goalkeeper Nathan Bishop before calmly slotting home his second goal in as many games.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz share the goals as Fulham double their lead against AFC Wimbledon in the Carabao Cup second round.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gonzalo Garcia gives Fulham a three-goal advantage in the dying minutes against Wimbledon to secure them victory in the second round of the Carabao Cup.

The key moments from Craven Cottage

22: CHANCE! Wimbledon's Callum Maycock glances a cross just past the far post as Wimbledon threaten a shock opener.

24: BIGGER CHANCE! Smith Rowe catches a half-volley from the edge of the box but narrowly misses the near post.

37: GOAL! Smith Rowe makes up for his miss by nodding home from Ryan Sessegnon's cut back.

42: GOAL! Muniz makes it two with an excellent header from a Tete cross.

46: SUB! Zepa comes on for Oscar Bobb to make his Fulham debut.

75: NO HANDBALL! Andy Yiadom somehow avoids being penalised for a blatant handball inside his own box when sliding to block a Tete effort.

90+3: GOAL! Substitute Garcia makes it three after racing away from a defender and evading Bishop's attempts to stop him.

90+5: CHANCE! Zepa gets down the outside of his man but is denied a dream debut by Bishop's legs from a tight angle.

Analysis: A perfect night for Arbeloa

Sky Sports' Ron Walker:

"Fulham boss Alvaro Arbeloa could not have asked for much more. Despite making 10 changes his side breezed into the third round, with a number of encouraging individual performances and not an injury in sight.

"Rodrigo Muniz's future may lie away from Craven Cottage but he is at least back in the goals and smiling again, and for the moment offers a valuable back-up to Goncalo Garcia - himself looking full of confidence with another strike.

"The Fulham fans leaving the ground would have undoubtedly been most captivated by the performance of Zepa, though.

"Against admittedly limited opposition, he was direct, lively and most importantly composed from his first touch to his last with his debut only missing a goal - and that wasn't for the want of trying."

Sports.title: Welbeck off the mark for Chelsea in win over Wilshere's Luton
Sports.content:
Danny Welbeck scored on his Chelsea debut as Xabi Alonso's first competitive game at Stamford Bridge as Blues manager ended in a 2-0 win over League One Luton in the Carabao Cup second round.

With transfer news about Enzo Fernandez and Emiliano Martinez swirling through the air at Stamford Bridge before kick-off, Welbeck's 50th-minute header to open his Chelsea account showed that not all signings have to be high profile.

Alonso actually named a strong Chelsea squad for this one, with Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Reece James all starting in a bid to take the game seriously. They dominated the first half but Palmer and Estevao missed good chances, before Rogers hit the bar with the last kick of the half.

But Welbeck broke Luton's resistance with a bullet header from Malo Gusto to open his Chelsea account in his 19th season playing in England's top league.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danny Welbeck scores against Luton on his Chelsea debut in the Carabao Cup to give the Blues the lead.

His achievements are so impressive that it is worth remembering that he and Luton head coach Jack Wilshere were once Arsenal team-mates.

But it was someone 16 years Welbeck's junior who sealed the result as Estevao's silky run and finish ended the contest with 10 minutes to go - though it would go down as a Hakeem Odoffin own goal.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Hakeem Odoffin scores an own goal for Luton as they go 2-0 down against Chelsea

The result sees Chelsea book a Carabao Cup third-round tie against Leeds United in early September, while Wilshere's Luton lost for the first time in 16 matches in all competitions - which was the longest run out of England's top four leagues.

The key moments from Stamford Bridge

11: DOUBLE CHANCE! Chelsea start strongly and Palmer has two quickfire efforts saved by Luton goalkeeper Josh Keeley.

19: GOOD SAVE! The Chelsea onslaught continues as James' free-kick is well-saved by Keeley.

39: WIDE! Estevao gets into a good area but drags his effort well wide of goal.

44: SAVE! Luton's best chance of the first half sees Odoffin head a free-kick at goal, but Mike Penders saves.

45+1: OFF THE BAR! Chelsea's best chance of the game sees Rogers hit the bar from Estevao's run and cross.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Morgan Rogers' shot hit the crossbar as Chelsea were left frustrated by Luton Town in the first half of their Carabao Cup clash.

50: GOAL! Luton's resistance is broken as Welbeck heads home from the middle of the box after Gusto's cross.

67: CHANCE! Kasey Palmer has a good shot from distance but it flies just wide of the near post.

79: GOAL! Estevao seals the win after doing a stepover before finding the opposite corner with a slick finish, which then goes down as a Odoffin own goal.

90+2: CHANCES! Substitute Joao Pedro misses a sitter before fellow replacement Jamie Gittens strikes the foot of the post.

Alonso: We have to prepare for low blocks

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso to Sky Sports:

"We needed to play with patience. Luton were defending with heart, they were solid so we knew that if they defend that low, it's not easy. At half-time, we spoke to be patient and keep going.

"It's the first time we have played against a low block this season, we have to prepare for when teams play in that way.

"We want to have a complete squad in all aspects. In quality, personality, young and experienced players - so the young players get help, that they are still players to develop.

"I'm happy with the energy and attitude of the players. The crowd has been great, we need them for the whole season. We come back here on Sunday."

Chelsea

Brighton and Hove Albion Sunday 30th August 1:00pm Kick off 2:00pm

Analysis: New formation gives Chelsea a Plan B

Sky Sports' Sam Blitz:

On Monday, there was reason for excitement about Alonso's Chelsea. The 3-4-3 formation at Fulham saw some brilliant attacking plays - but in this game we saw something a bit different.

Alonso switched it up with a 4-2-3-1 formation, putting Palmer in as the No 10 behind Welbeck - and it added a different dimension to the Chelsea attack.

Yes, the gulf in class between Chelsea and League One Luton is fairly big but the Blues' attacking players thrived. Estevao and Palmer both ended up with five chances created each - in a Chelsea attack that created 26 shots.

Many saw Alonso's time at Real Madrid and thought a back four wasn't possible. But after this dominant display, Chelsea have a different game plan they can turn to - after years of being accused of not having a Plan B.

Wilshere: We don't like losing

Luton Town head coach Jack Wilshere to Sky Sports:

"Proud is the word that comes to mind the most. We saw things in the team tonight that we don't normally have to do.

"For as long as Chelsea made us do it, I loved it. I loved how focused we were. The first goal is a really good goal that's hard to defend. And then you think can you stay in it still? Towards the end I think we got a bit tired, but really proud of the commitment and the effort.

"We don't like losing, we knew it would be difficult but I'm proud of the players. No-one in that dressing room is happy or sad - I'm proud of them. But we haven't lost in a while and we don't like that losing feeling. We want to create that winning culture and feeling."

Sports.title: McKibbin leads British Masters amid repeated rain suspensions
Sports.content:
Tom McKibbin held a one-shot lead at the Husqvarna British Masters before play was suspended on an opening day at The Belfry already severely hampered by stormy weather.

The first klaxon of the day for lightning came just two minutes after the opening tee shots had been hit at 7.30am, forcing an initial three-hour suspension.

Play resumed at 10.32am before being stopped again just after midday due to flooded bunkers, keeping players off the course for a further four hours.

A final resumption at 4.15pm allowed the early groups to get deep into their back nines before the return of thunder and lightning saw play for the day end at 7.11pm.

None of the groups out on the course had completed their first rounds, with half of the 156-player field yet to tee off at all.
