Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Guéhi versatility crucial as Bouaddi arrives

Enzo Maresca has a shiny new £85m midfielder he could select for a debut but, at 18 years old, he may want Ayyoub Bouaddi to have a bit of time watching on from the bench to learn about the Premier League from his elders. The Moroccan may not have anticipated one of those to be a centre-back by trade. Marc Guéhi will be eager to make a triumphant return to Crystal Palace and may well have the opportunity to do so from central midfield, where he played last weekend in the victory over Bournemouth, scoring the equaliser. The centre-back was a surprise selection in the blocker role next to Elliot Anderson, but equipped himself admirably and was not limited to the dirty work, often being found in more advanced positions in open play and happy to have the ball at his feet. His long-term future is unlikely to be outside of defence but further proof of Guéhi’s adaptability will be a positive for Maresca, as a long season awaits. Will Unwin

Crystal Palace v Manchester City, Friday 8pm (all times BST)

2 Liverpool need to stop Gibbs-White

“It is just not personnel,” insisted Andoni Iraola in response to Liverpool conceding two goals to quick Newcastle transitions in his first Premier League game as the club’s head coach. Some long-term faults can not be rectified overnight – although that did not prevent some hysterical reactions to the performance at St James’ Park – and with Liverpool prioritising wingers in the final days of the transfer window the answer to this particular weakness, as Iraola indicated, lies on the training ground. Morgan Gibbs-White revelled in the spaces behind Liverpool’s midfield last season as he – and set-pieces – helped Nottingham Forest to a second successive league win at Anfield. Iraola does not want to curb Ryan Gravenberch’s attacking instincts but greater tactical discipline and willingness to do the dirty work from the entire Liverpool midfield will be needed to stop Gibbs-White producing a repeat performance. Forest’s new record signing, Liam Delap, has also been registered in time to play. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 12.30pm

3 Everton note Cherries’ set-piece struggles

There were so many encouraging takeaways for Bournemouth despite an agonising late defeat at Manchester City. The catalyst for City’s turnaround was Marc Guéhi’s 84th-minute equaliser, the England defender heading in unmarked at a corner, after wasting a near-identical earlier chance. For Bournemouth, it was a familiar source of pain; only Liverpool conceded more set-piece goals in the top flight last season (20), with the Cherries and Crystal Palace both conceding 18. Bournemouth sought to address their vulnerability in the summer by hiring their first dedicated set-piece coach in Nicolas Gagnon, who worked with Canada at the World Cup and previously at Southampton and in Saudi Arabia. Only Arsenal, Manchester City, Manchester United and Aston Villa claimed more points away from home than Everton last season and David Moyes’s centre-backs, Jarrad Branthwaite and James Tarkowski, will be licking their lips if Bournemouth do not sharpen up their act. Ben Fisher

Bournemouth v Everton, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Bournemouth were again undone by a set-piece goal as they lost 2-1 at Manchester City. Photograph: Darren Staples/AFP/Getty Images

4 Too early for a relegation six-pointer?

Contrasting opening weekends for Coventry and Hull, harsh reality dealt out against the dream scenario lived out. At Arsenal, Coventry were well beaten by the champions, while in East Yorkshire, Manchester United were soundly, deservedly defeated. Despite contrasting starts, both teams remain warm favourites for relegation. Two defeats in a row for Frank Lampard’s team would dim the optimism of a summer of anticipation. Hull seek to extend the reverie of last week though Coventry are unlikely to be caught as cold as United last week, and surely cannot defend set pieces so badly. The last three Championship matches between these two teams ended in draws, last season’s meetings goalless, although both squads have since been upgraded by brisk transfer business. At Hull, much is expected of Lucas Herrington who missed Australia’s fateful penalty against Egypt at the World Cup. The teenage defender shone against Stoke in the Tigers’ successful midweek Carabao Cup assignment. John Brewin

Coventry v Hull, Saturday 3pm

5 Tottenham keen for Tonali to tick

It has not taken long for Sandro Tonali to be reunited with his former teammates. After succumbing 3-0 on the opening weekend at Brentford, a home victory will be the minimum requirement for Tottenham. Roberto De Zerbi and his players will be desperate to show that things have changed after a busy summer in the transfer market. Tonali will be a key part of that; he was the only central midfielder who made it past half-time in west London, so at least has minutes in his legs to build on. The Italian will be eager to not suffer at the hands of a team that served him well after bringing him to England. Tonali is supposed to make his new team tick and a rousing home debut would do a lot for everyone’s confidence, while defeat will bring plenty more questions. WU

Tottenham v Newcastle, Saturday 5.30pm

View image in fullscreen Sandro Tonali (left) faces his old club Newcastle after a difficult debut against Brentford. Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The Guardian

6 Acheampong fights to stay with Blues

This is an important moment in Josh Acheampong’s development. The 20-year-old academy graduate did not have many opportunities last year but he started in Xabi Alonso’s back three when Chelsea beat Fulham on Monday. It was a big vote of confidence from Alonso in the young defender, who played well, and may indicate that Acheampong will stay at Stamford Bridge this season. Several clubs are interested in the England youth international and there is talk of a loan before the transfer window shuts, but Acheampong would strengthen his position further if he is selected again for Sunday’s home game against Brighton. Jacob Steinberg

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Chelsea v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

7

On Monday night, Jamie Carragher told a Sky Sports audience that he thought Sunderland might be relegated this season. The former Liverpool defender compared Régis Le Bris’s team to the Sheffield United side managed by Chris Wilder that went down in 2020-2021 – their second season after promotion – and suggested Sunderland were “arrogant”. How will Le Bris’s players respond against Fulham at the Stadium of Light on Sunday? Has the moment arrived to end a winless Premier League run against the west London side stretching back 12 years? If there are legitimate concerns about the ability of Le Bris’s players to cope with a Europa League campaign, regular Sunderland watchers struggle to buy into the accusations or arrogance, let alone the analogy with a very different Sheffield United side. Nonetheless, last Saturday’s 2-1 defeat at Ipswich has prompted a certain anxiety, leaving Wearsiders hoping Nordi Mukiele is fit enough to raise defensive standards. Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Fulham, Sunday 2pm

View image in fullscreen Sunderland fans have bristled at Jamie Carragher’s prediction for their team’s season. Photograph: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

8 Leeds look to strengthen as Bees buzz

Sub-plots abound at Elland Road as Leeds and Brentford meet after two wins apiece from their first competitive matches of the season. There is the goalkeeping beauty contest between Daniel Farke’s showpiece summer signing, James Trafford – who has registered two clean sheets in his opening games – and Brentford’s Caoimhin Kelleher. Further forward, fans can ponder the question of which centre forward, the Leeds favourite Dominic Calvert-Lewin or his opposite number Igor Thiago will prove the more incisive. Similarly the technical area tactical duel involving Daniel Farke and Keith Andrews looks extremely hard to call. Away from the pitch, Farke is hoping to win a race with Sunderland to sign Marseille winger Igor Paixão for around £30m as the Leeds manager urges his board to strengthen. “I’m happy with my group and my signings so far,” said Farke. “But we know we can definitely improve our squad. That is what Leeds supporters and Leeds United deserve.” LT

Leeds v Brentford, Sunday 2pm

9 Carrick under pressure to deliver

Manchester United are bloody-nosed and Ipswich Town definitely delighted after the tale of each team’s results on the opening weekend. At Hull City, Michael Carrick’s team played with zero cohesion and conviction and went down to a miserable 2-0 loss. At Portman Road Gary O’Neil’s side hosted Sunderland and claimed a rousing late 2-1 win, so arrive at Old Trafford with a bounce in the step. Carrick has to lift his men and get a result – preferably victory. A loss, at home, to another promoted team, would begin the latest inquest into a United No 1: a predicament suffered by every manager post-Sir Alex Ferguson. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Ipswich, Sunday 4.30pm

10 Villa fans bid farewell to Konsa

At a time when the manner of a player’s departure feels particularly pertinent, especially at Aston Villa, Ezri Konsa can expect a warm reception on his return to the club. Konsa could make his Arsenal debut at Villa Park against his former club, where he excelled across seven seasons. A £12m buy from Brentford in 2019, Konsa surely represents one of their finest signings in the Premier League era. He joined fresh from a single season in the Championship with Brentford and left as an England regular and Europa League winner. Konsa’s role in Villa’s recent success should not be overlooked. Unai Emery can be judged by Villa’s extraordinary run of league finishes – seventh, fourth, sixth and fourth – but also his track record of turning promising talents, like Konsa, into fully-fledged internationals. BF

Sports.title: Danny Welbeck leads Chelsea past Luton but Enzo Fernández misses Carabao Cup tie
Sports.content:
Emiliano Martínez is on his way but another high-profile Argentinian is likely to be wearing a different shade of blue soon. Chelsea have dealt with their biggest weakness, satisfying Xabi Alonso’s wish for a new goalkeeper by agreeing a £7.5m deal to sign Martínez from Aston Villa, and it will surely not be long before they have put an end to the Enzo Fernández saga.

Fernández was the most notable absentee as Chelsea eased into the third round of the Carabao Cup with a 2-0 win over Luton. There is a desire to move on from the circus. Manchester City are poised to bid for Fernández and, with the noise around the midfielder becoming a distraction, Alonso and the club decided to leave out Chelsea’s supposed vice-captain.

Alonso explained that he had to think about the team. Chelsea’s manager was diplomatic. Alonso said that Fernández has been training well. He offered political answers but did not douse the sense that Fernández has played his last game for Chelsea, who host Leeds in the next round.

It is for the best. Fernández has been looking for a way out since March and Chelsea need committed players. Alonso wants to improve the squad’s culture and the attitude against Luton was good. Danny Welbeck, still going strong at 35, can be a standard bearer after joining from Brighton. The striker is not here to make up the numbers and played a key role in this win, grabbing his first goal since joining when he opened the scoring early in the second half.

“Danny was the patient player,” Alonso said of Welbeck breaking Luton’s resistance by leaping to head home a fine cross from Malo Gusto. “He did what he does best: score and to be in the right place.”

Welbeck will provide competition for João Pedro in attack this season. He also adds a vital dash of experience to a young squad. Chelsea can cope without Fernández, even though they will need to replace him if he goes to City.

View image in fullscreen Xabi Alonso has seen his Chelsea side win their first two games. Photograph: Ian Stephen/Every Second Media/Shutterstock

The early vibes under Alonso are encouraging. He has been decisive with the goalkeeping position, as exemplified by his ruthless response to Robert Sánchez’s skittish display against Fulham. There is nothing left to see with Sánchez. He is not good enough and Chelsea had to be opportunistic when offered the chance to sign Martínez. Mike Penders made his debut in goal on Thursday night. The 21-year-old Belgian is highly rated but will be behind Martínez in the pecking order.

Alonso is trying to win now. Although Chelsea have no European football this season it was surprising that they named such a strong side three days after their helter-skelter win over Fulham in the Premier League. Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer were part of an exciting attack and were supported by a thrilling display from Estêvão Willian on the right.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Third in League One, Luton battled to stay in contention during a first half in which the shot count was 17-3 in Chelsea’s favour. Rogers crashed an effort against the bar and Jack Wilshere’s side were defiant in defence. Josh Keeley made excellent saves from Palmer and Reece James, starting in midfield for the second time in three days despite his injury problems.

Chelsea stayed patient. Valentin Barco, Jude Bellingham’s Atlanta irritant, had an impressive debut next to James. Chelsea, who were still missing Moisés Caicedo, upped the pace early in the second half. Gusto overlapped and crossed. Welbeck was wily and deadly, creeping off his marker and heading home.

The second goal arrived late. Barco was involved and Palmer found Estêvão, whose shot went in off Hakeem Odoffin for an own goal.

Sports.title: Chelsea agree £7.5m deal to sign Emiliano Martínez from Aston Villa
Sports.content:
Chelsea have agreed a £7.5m deal to sign the Aston Villa goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez and are expecting Manchester City to make an offer for Enzo Fernández in the next 48 hours.

Xabi Alonso identified the signing of a goalkeeper as a priority after Robert Sánchez struggled against Fulham on Monday and the deal for Martínez has gone through quickly. The Argentina international is out of favour at Villa after their acquisition of Zion Suzuki and is due to sign a two-year contract with the option of a further year.

The signing of Martínez, who will be 34 next week, will raise questions over the future of Sánchez. Sources believe the Spaniard is unlikely to accept losing his spot as No 1 and may need to be moved on before the window shuts on Tuesday night.

Quick Guide How do I 

However iIt is unclear whether there is an obvious club for Sánchez to join and another complication for Chelsea will be working out what to do with Mike Penders, who was expected to challenge for the No 1 shirt this season. There is a feeling that Penders could leave on loan. The highly rated 21-year-old Belgian spent last season on loan at Strasbourg.

It is poised to be a busy end to the summer for Chelsea, who are also dealing with City’s attempts to sign Fernández. The Argentina midfielder is desperate to leave and was left out of the side for Thursday night’s Carabao Cup tie against Luton.

Sources at Chelsea insist a deal is not close and that there has yet to be any communication from City. Chelsea are adamant that Fernández will be sold only on their terms. City missed an unofficial deadline to sign the midfielder for £120m this month and there have been suggestions the price could be higher because the end of the window is approaching.

Chelsea also need to be able to strengthen their squad but have little time to act. They are aware Bournemouth do not want to sell Alex Scott and that Crystal Palace are similarly determined to hold on to Adam Wharton, while Monaco midfielder Lamine Camara could be a target. Chelsea may not look for a direct replacement for Fernández, but will not accept weakening their squad by helping out a rival.

View image in fullscreen Leon Goretzka has joined Aston Villa after leaving Bayern Munich earlier this summer. Photograph: Neville Williams/Aston Villa FC/Getty Images

Aston Villa, meanwhile, have signed the Germany midfielder Leon Goretzka on a free after his departure from Bayern Munich. The 31-year-old spent eight seasons at ​Bayern, making ‌312 appearances, and has played 73 times for his country.

“I had a bit of long vacation, and it was a process to find out what I really wanted. From the first moment, I had a really good feeling, and I’m really happy to be here,” Goretzka said after completing the move.“I had a good feeling from the first conversation with the coach. Aston Villa is a really big club. I want to help the team to achieve their goals and to bring my experience that I have from my whole career.”

“I’m really looking forward to playing in these kinds of big games every few days,” he added. “This is probably the biggest difference to the Bundesliga, where you have only several great games with big opponents.”

Sports.title: Champions League draw: Arsenal face Real Madrid, Man City get Barcelona and PSG
Sports.content:
Arsenal face mouthwatering assignments against Real Madrid and Bayern Munich as they bid to go one better than last season’s agonising near miss and win a first Champions League title.

Mikel Arteta’s side were pipped on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain in the final three months ago and will be expected to cruise through this season’s league phase. The bulk of their draw appears kind but they are tasked with a visit to the Allianz Arena to play Bayern, whom they beat 3-1 at the Emirates Stadium last November, and host Real, who are once again under the charge of José Mourinho. Two seasons ago, Arsenal beat the Spanish giants 3-0 at home in a quarter-final first leg, Declan Rice scoring two memorable free-kicks.

Arsenal will also welcome Borussia Dortmund, Lille and the Azerbaijani debutants Sabah to north London. Their other away fixtures involve trips to Napoli, Slavia Prague and a reunion with their ex-player Héctor Bellerin at Real Betis.

Manchester City will swiftly renew acquaintances with Rodri when they visit Barcelona during Enzo Maresca’s first Champions League campaign in charge. They will greet Kevin De Bruyne and Napoli at the Etihad Stadium, just as they did last season in cruising to a 2-0 win. Their other home ties bring an enticing meeting with the reigning champions, PSG, a tie against Sporting and a visit by AEK Athens. Trips to Porto, RB Leipzig and Lens will round off their schedule.

The return of Manchester United to Europe’s elite competition throws up home games with Bayern, Roma, RB Leipzig and Sabah. Michael Carrick’s team will travel to Como, who are managed by Cesc Fàbregas, along with Atlético Madrid, Sporting and Villarreal.

Liverpool will host Atlético, Porto, Villarreal and Lens. They visit Lask, the newcomers who sensationally beat Celtic on Tuesday, along with Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and Inter in a relatively kind-looking set of games.

Aston Villa, ravaged in recent weeks by the departures of key players, will hope to have strengthened sufficiently for a home tie with PSG and a visit to Barcelona. They will be heartened by a stirring performance in their recent Super Cup defeat to Luis Enrique’s side in Salzburg. Borussia Dortmund, Fenerbahce and the Norwegian new boys Viking Stavanger will also visit Villa Park. Unai Emery will also take his team to Club Brugge, Galatasaray and Slavia Prague.

Liverpool: Atlético Madrid (h), Inter (a), Porto (h), Club Brugge (a), Villarreal (h), Fenerbahce (a), Lens (h), Lask (a). Aston Villa: PSG (h), Barcelona (a), Dortmund (h), Club Brugge (a), Fenerbahce (h), Galatasaray (a), Viking (h), Slavia Prague (a). Thank you for your feedback.

While Chelsea did not qualify for European competition this season, their home will still host Champions League football. The Ukrainian champions, Shakhtar Donetsk, still unable to play continental matches in their homeland, will stage home games there. Real Madrid are the most high-profile of their four visitors, meaning Mourinho will return to his old stomping ground.

PSG’s bid to win a third successive Champions League title involves home league games against Barcelona, Roma, Galatasaray and Slovan Bratislava, as well as trips to Villarreal, Como, City and Villa.

The first set of fixtures will be played on 8 and 9 September. The schedule and dates for all eight match weeks will be announced on Saturday.

Sports.title: Muniz and García on target in Fulham’s Carabao Cup cruise past Wimbledon
Sports.content:
Fulham’s second London derby this week, a first competitive win for Álvaro Arbeloa. If AFC Wimbledon represent a different echelon to Chelsea, Monday’s visitors, Thursday’s easy progress past League One opponents supplied several reasons for optimism in the new Fulham.

Marco Silva, Arbeloa’s predecessor, frequently offered sullen dismissal of the depth of his Fulham squad and yet left behind plenty of talent on departing for Benfica. Getting a better tune from Emile Smith Rowe and Rodrigo Muniz than Silva managed last season will help. The pair scored first-half goals to take the tie from Wimbledon’s reach, making for a second half of comfort and experimentation, glimpses of a different Fulham, teenage talent handed its chance to shine. Gonzalo García’s late strike, rounding Wimbledon goalkeeper Nathan Bishop for a second goal of the week, increased the excitement surrounding one of the summer’s most eye-catching signings.

“You need the energy and different qualities,” said Arbeloa of an evening where squad rotation had paid dividends. “They need to feel they are important.”

A muggy riverside evening attracted a decent crowd. More than enough to disrupt the dog walkers and evening strollers of a genteel locale, the Wimbledon contingent boisterous. The first meeting between the clubs since 2001, before the old Wimbledon was franchised to Milton Keynes and a phoenix club rose from that rotten affair.

The respective team selections revealed priorities; 10 changes for Arbeloa, only Oscar Bobb remained from Chelsea; six for Johnnie Jackson, the Wimbledon manager. Shea Charles, the summer’s other headline signing, made his first start and played well. “He’s ready,” said Arbeloa of the young Northern Ireland midfielder.

Luc De Fougerolles, fresh from the summer’s World Cup with Canada, made only his second Fulham appearance. Down each team’s left, a Sessegnon brother, Ryan for Fulham and Steven, formerly of Fulham, for Wimbledon.

“A good night for the club because we get to test ourselves against the very best,” said Jackson. “And 5,000 fans got to enjoy themselves. They were a credit to the club.”

Wimbledon, maintaining Crazy Gang traditions, were dangerous from set pieces. When De Fougerolles could only head away a corner, the ball fell to the Wimbledon captain, Alistair Smith. The shot was straight at Benjamin Lecomte, the best chance on offer to the visitors all evening.

Thereafter, Fulham piled up opportunities. Goals soon followed. Smith Rowe was furious after a sliced miss. Muniz was just as self-flagellating when ballooning a Smith Rowe flick.

View image in fullscreen Gonzalo García completes Fulham’s 3-0 victory to set up a London derby with West Ham. Photograph: Dennis Goodwin/ProSports/Shutterstock

His redemption came swiftly, from close range after Dons defender James Tilley deflected the ball into his path. The celebration was minimal from a player Arbeloa said “deserves more minutes”.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Muniz was far more rapturous after nodding in Kenny Tete’s cross. Small wonder. This was his first goal since the opening game of last season. “Goals are very important for strikers,” said Arbeloa, stating the clear and obvious.

At half-time Macaulay Zepa, 18, arrived. Arbeloa’s appointment was accompanied by heralding of his youth development work at Real Madrid, a departure from Silva’s preference for hard-bitten pros. Zepa, a speedy and direct winger, showed real promise, as did fellow youth team graduate Chibby Nwoko. “One of the best news today,” said Arbeloa. “We know very well that academy players are very important.”

Fulham featured an assured youth-and-experience central defensive combination of De Fougerolles and Joachim Andersen. Calvin Bassey replaced the senior partner on the hour and the youngster did not last much longer, pulling up after a block tackle. “Nothing to worry about,” said Arbeloa, soothingly.

The arrivals of García and César Palacios, young Madrilenos who accompanied Arbeloa, supplied further excitement, the former’s goal another taste of a new Fulham.

Sports.title: Uefa raises stakes with criminal complaint in battle to unseat Infantino | Matt Hughes
Sports.content:
Anyone who interpreted Uefa’s decision to withdraw a proposed boycott of Fifa competitions, revealed by the Guardian on Wednesday, as a backward step in the attempt to remove Gianni Infantino as Fifa’s president has been quickly disabused of that notion.

In a stunning development that overshadowed one of the biggest days in the European football calendar as national football federation and club executives gathered for the Champions League draw in Monte Carlo, Uefa announced it was preparing to make a legal complaint against Infantino in Switzerland alleging “criminal mismanagement” for his role in the failed World Cup sell-off plan.

Uefa, having removed the immediate pressure on Fifa on one front by permitting European teams to play in next month’s Under-20 Women’s World Cup and October’s senior Women’s World Cup qualifiers, has dramatically increased the stakes on another.

The first step in that legal process is seeking disclosure in the United States of documents relating to the abandoned Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, which Uefa described in a 56-page document sent to three US courts as having an “absurdly low enterprise value of only approximately $20bn” (£14.7bn).

From the moment it became clear Infantino would not resign after withdrawing the FFE plan four days after it became public, Uefa has been pursuing the valuation issue, which if the sale had progressed would have enabled Joshua Kushner’s Thrive Capital to buy 21% of future Fifa revenues in perpetuity for $4.2bn.

The Guardian revealed on 6 August that Uefa was commissioning an independent valuation of FFE amid concerns Infantino was planning to sell off football’s crown jewel on the cheap, a feeling exacerbated by the fact Fifa’s sales deck did not contain any information on the valuation process or evidence of a competitive tender.

As one source who questioned Fifa’s valuation said this month: “We need to find out if they were selling the World Cup at a knockdown price.” The intention to bring a criminal complaint is the logical extension of this process.

View image in fullscreen The four-year cycle leading to this summer’s World Cup yielded $15bn in revenue for Fifa. Photograph: Claudio Thoma/EPA

Even the most cursory of inquiries over the past few weeks vindicated Uefa’s concerns. Fifa’s revenue for the four-year cycle that culminated in this summer’s World Cup was $15bn, leading market analysts to suggest that $20bn was a low valuation, particularly as the proposal did not appear to include provisions to prevent expansion and the creation of new tournaments.

Kushner’s subsequent purchase of the LA Lakers with the former Disney chief Bob Iger for $12.5bn further convinced Uefa that Thrive Capital had been given a sweetheart deal by Infantino, a conviction underlined by its suspicion that Infantino was lining up a lucrative role worth tens of millions of pounds a year as FFE’s chair after standing down as Fifa’s president, which he plans to do in 2031 if he wins a further, final term.

Infantino’s determination to cling to office – demonstrated by his decision to enter campaign mode by attending a meeting of the Caribbean Football Union last weekend in the Dominican Republic where, as the Guardian revealed, he suddenly approved several funding projects – emboldened Uefa further.

Uefa has taken the legal route after being thwarted in numerous requests to Fifa to disclose documents. It has made court filings in New York, Florida and Colorado to obtain papers it may submit to Swiss courts seeking criminal charges.

Just as significant as the attempt to take Infantino to court in his adopted country is Uefa’s attempt to rally Fifa members behind it in its attempt to unseat him via March’s presidential election.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

For all Uefa’s public bullishness that Infantino’s race is run, several senior figures there and among its allies at Concacaf – the North and Central American and Caribbean confederation – have admitted concerns to the Guardian that they are struggling to get many member associations outside Europe to turn against him.

Over the past few weeks several FAs have privately indicated it may take evidence of criminal activity, or at least proof that Infantino would have been personally enriched by the FFE venture, for them to abandon him.

Even those with a brief knowledge of Fifa’s history would agree that the rebels concerned about momentum to unseat Infantino stalling have a point. Although he loves to paint the world governing body as the ultimate democracy underpinned by a one-member, one-vote system, the reality is anything but. Although elections are held every four years there have been only three permanent presidents in the past 52 years, and the last to leave office after a vote was England’s Sir Stanley Rous in 1974.

Rous’s conqueror, the Brazilian João Havelange, resigned after 24 years and was later found to have accepted bribes related to the sale of media rights by a Fifa ethics committee. His successor, Sepp Blatter, stood down after winning five elections in the midst of an FBI investigation in 2015, which has resulted in more than 20 criminal convictions in the US and could lead to more.

Any hope among the rebels that the Swiss authorities will come to their aid and bring Infantino to court should be tempered by those authorities’ long history of turning a blind eye to Fifa corruption, which meant intervention from the FBI was required to expose and punish it.

Sports.title: Atlético Madrid chief insists Júlian Alvarez will ‘never, ever’ be sold to Barcelona
Sports.content:
Atlético Madrid’s chief executive appeared to slam the door on Barcelona’s pursuit of Júlian Alvarez on Thursday. Miguel Ángel Gil Marín accused the Catalan club of dishonesty and insisted the Argentina forward would “never, ever” be sold to them.

Speaking to Spanish broadcaster Movistar Plus, Gil Marín delivered a blistering response to ⁠Barcelona’s president, Joan Laporta, who had said on Wednesday that ​his club remained “very interested” in signing Alvarez.

Gil Marín said Atlético were united from top to bottom in refusing to negotiate with Barcelona over a deal for a player they insists is not for sale to their La Liga rivals.

“The truth is that it outrages ⁠us even more; we are repulsed by the dishonesty, the lack of ethics, transparency and professionalism, and ​we can only insist that we will not ‌negotiate with Barcelona under any ‌circumstances,” Gil Marín said.

“I have the support of everyone working with me, from shareholders to directors, and ‌the only certain and firm decision is that we will not negotiate with Barcelona under any circumstances,” he added. “You have my word – the player [Alvarez] will most certainly not be transferred to Barcelona.“

The Barcelona vice-president, Rafa Yuste, reacted angrily to Gil Marín’s remarks. “It is a lack of manners and respect,” Yuste told Movistar. “With those words, they’ve crossed a red ‌line.”

Earlier on Thursday, Atlético’s board of directors unanimously backed the club’s stance on Alvarez, ruling out talks with Barcelona and saying there was “zero consideration” of a transfer before the summer transfer window closes.

Gil Marín said the situation had affected Alvarez. “Júlian is really struggling; there have been people who have set out to deceive and confuse him, and I’m very sorry about that,” Gil Marín said.

Alvarez was booed by Atleti fans during their 2-2 home draw with Villarreal on Sunday, having stated his desire to leave. While on World Cup duty with Argentina this summer, the 26-year-old revealed he wanted to “fulfil my dream” by departing the club.

“I know him and we’ve been working with him for ⁠some time,” Gil Marín added. “He’s a great professional and footballer, but he’s very confused and going ​through a very difficult time, ​both personally and professionally.“

Arsenal have also been linked with a move for the former Manchester City forward, but Gil Marín said his preference was ​for the player to ‌remain in Madrid beyond Tuesday’s deadline.

“Our intention ​and my personal dream ​is for him to stay with us, to remain at Atlético,” he said. “To compete amongst the greats, you need great players, and Júlian is one. If he believes that staying at Atlético is no longer feasible, we will look for an alternative, but it will never, ever be Barcelona.”
