Rodri makes Barça debut in win over Athletic

Raphinha and Fermin López scored in either half and Rodri made his debut off the bench as Barcelona beat Athletic Club 2-0 at Camp Nou in their first home match of the new La Liga season.

View image in fullscreen Barcelona midfielder Rodri applauds the Camp Nou crowd after making his debut. Photograph: Quique García/EPA

Barça opened the scoring in the 37th minute, Raphinga rounding goalkeeper Unai Simón after Pedri’s through ball split the Athletic defence. ⁠Fermin sealed the win ⁠in the 82nd ​when he pounced on Aymeric Laporte’s defensive error from Karim Adeyemi’s low cross and finished from inside the penalty box.

Hansi Flick’s side controlled most of the ⁠game and created the better chances, although Simon kept the visitors in contention with several important saves. Flick also handed winger Anthony Gordon his full debut, with Rodri coming on for Raphinha to make his first appearance for Barça.

Flick made three changes from the team that began the campaign ⁠with a 5-0 win at Elche, handing Anthony Gordon his full debut and bringing in Pau Cubarsi and ​Pedri. New signing Rodri started on the bench.

“Happy to play my first match,” Rodri told Dazn after the game. “It is important for me to regain my rhythm and adapt to this great team. It has been a long summer … I’m very happy, I am where I wanted to be. Now we have to work.”

Sports.title: Rangers crash out of Conference League in shootout loss to Czech side Jablonec
Sports.content:
Rangers crashed out of the Uefa Conference League playoffs with a 4-3 penalty shootout defeat by Jablonec.

Leading 1-0 from the first leg at Ibrox last week, Derek McInnes’s side turned in a turgid performance in Czechia which lacked creativity and invention. It proved costly as they fell to a 1-0 defeat at Stadion Strelnice, drawing 1-1 on aggregate after extra time to set up the final shootout.

Despite McInnes introducing Lawrence Shankland, Connor Barron and Findlay Curtis in the second half, Rangers could not get a foothold in the game. The Jablonec midfielder Vakhtang Chanturishvili deservedly levelled the tie in the 73rd minute with a low drive to beat Rangers keeper Ivor Pandur.

There were no more goals which brought penalties, and although Pandur saved from Filip Zorvan, Curtis fired his spot-kick over the bar. James Penrice was then thwarted by Jablonec keeper Jan Hanus, leaving Jan Chramosta to fire in the decisive kick.

The defeat is a huge blow to Rangers, who were knocked out of the Europa League qualifiers by Polish side Jagiellonia Bialystok, losing 3-2 on aggregate. The club’s massive rebuild under McInnes is struggling to get off the ground, and now their European campaign is over in August.

“I’m embarrassed with the performance,” McInnes admitted. “It wasn’t a good performance at any stretch of the imagination. I’m not going to sit here and make any excuses whatsoever. It wasn’t good enough.”

“I thought the opposition were better than us in most aspects of the game so we got what we deserved,” he added. “If we’d won it on penalties, we’d have taken it … but we’d have covered over the cracks, to be honest. I’m mortified by the performance.”

Brighton booked their place in the Conference League’s league phase with a comfortable 4-0 play-off victory over Tromsø at the Amex Stadium. Albion had work to do in Thursday evening’s second leg after failing to capitalise on 25 attempts at goal during last week’s goalless first-leg draw in Norway.

Fabian Hürzeler’s side were far more ruthless on home soil, with first-half finishes from Charalampos Kostoulas, Maxim De Cuyper and Mats Wieffer putting them firmly in control of the tie. Olivier Boscagli added a deflected fourth late on to seal a place in Friday’s draw.

View image in fullscreen Charalambos Kostoulas beats Jakob Haugaard in the Tromsø goal to put Brighton ahead. Photograph: Andrew Boyers/Action Images/Reuters

Motherwell were left to rue another costly red card as their European adventure ended with a 4-1 defeat away to Freiburg in the Conference League playoffs.

A week after Martin Moormann’s sending off paved the way for last season’s Europa League finalists to win 3-1 in the first leg, Well had Jake Girdwood-Reich dismissed just before the hour mark with the second leg in Germany still level at 1-1.

Emmanuel Longelo’s equaliser, following a blunder from home goalkeeper Mio Backhaus, cancelled out an early opener from Derry Scherhant. The visitors’ hopes of emerging unscathed from a formidable away trip were dashed as goals from Igor Matanovic, Cyriaque Irie and Keisuke Goto secured a 7-2 aggregate win.

Miguel Chaiwa scored a stoppage-time own goal as Hibernian suffered Conference League playoff despair for the second year running in a 3-2 home defeat by Gent.

After a goalless first leg in Belgium last week, Hibs looked on course to make it to the league phase for the first time after second-half goals from Jason Kerr and Felix Passlack overturned a stunning first-half opener from Gent’s teenage forward Josue Vergara.

But Christian Burgess equalised in the 84th minute for the visitors, before Hibs midfielder Chaiwa slid the ball into his own net in stoppage time. That confirmed another agonising European exit after a 4-3 aggregate defeat by Legia Warsaw at the same stage last season.

View image in fullscreen Manuel Toledano’s late extra-time penalty condemned Larne to playoff defeat against Gibraltar’s Lincoln Red Imps. Photograph: Liam McBurney/PA

There was also late agony for Northern Ireland’s Larne, who let a two-goal aggregate lead slip in the last 10 minutes at home to Gibraltar’s Lincoln Red Imps. Leading 2-0 from the first leg, Larne kept the visitors at bay until the 82nd minute, but Kike Gómez and Manu Toledano struck in quick succession to level the tie at 2-2 overall.

Montel Gibson was sent off for the hosts in the 87th minute, and although Larne came close to taking the tie to a penalty shootout, Toledano scored a spot-kick in the 121st minute to seal their fate. Shamrock Rovers also missed out on the Conference League’s main phase as they lost 1-0 at Finnish side KuPS to seal a 2-1 aggregate loss.

Sports.title: Man City handed nightmare Champions League draw with Arsenal also given tricky fixtures as Man United face old foes on return to competition - and Jose's back at the Bridge!
Sports.content:
Man City handed nightmare Champions League draw with Arsenal also given tricky fixtures as Man United face old foes on return to competition - and Jose's back at the Bridge!

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Jude Bellingham, Jose Mourinho and Harry Kane all stand in Arsenal's way as they seek to go one better than last season's Champions League final defeat.

The Premier League winners have been handed a tricky looking path to the knockout stages - along with rivals Manchester City - following a draw overseen by Gunners legend Thierry Henry in Monaco which could also prompt a return to England for Mason Greenwood.

Mikel Arteta's side will be keen to dispel the heartbreaking penalty shoot-out defeat to Paris Saint-Germain however, there will no be no easy route to the final at the home of Atletico Madrid.

While 24 out of the 36 sides will qualify from the league format, Arsenal will need to acquire the required points from a tricky looking list.

Bellingham and Mourinho's Real Madrid will head to north London, along with the transfer target they missed out on in Vinicius Junior. Declan Rice and Co will jet to Bavaria to face prolific former Tottenham striker Kane's Bayern Munich. Clashes against Borussia Dortmund, Real Betis, Lille and Napoli will also provide a stiff test while relatively more straightforward challenges await in the shape of Azerbaijan minnows Sabah and Slavia Prague.

Manchester City, entering the tournament without Pep Guardiola at the helm for the first time in a decade, may also be cursing UEFA's computer.

Last season's runners-up Arsenal (left) will face Real Madrid in one their Champions League eight fixtures to reach the knockouts

Enzo Maresca's (right) Man City have been dealt tough games including vs PSG and Barcelona

Enzo Maresca's side will take on champions Paris Saint-Germain at the Etihad and make a trip to the Nou Camp to face Barcelona.

Portuguese duo Sporting Lisbon and Porto also feature, along with Napoli and Leipzig. AEK Athens and Lens complete a what is a seriously daunting-looking list.

It will be a trip down memory lane for neighbours United, who return to the competition following a two-year absence. Michael Carrick's side will entertain Bayern Munich, in a repeat of the epic 1999 final, while Roma - memorably crushed 7-1 in 2007 - will also visit Old Trafford.

There may well be some away days to relish for the club's supporters, with their list featuring trips to Sporting Lisbon, Atletico Madrid and Cesc Fabregas' Como. United, currently on 293, will become the first English team to play more than 300 games in the competition, with Villarreal, Leipzig and Sabah completing their schedule.

Andoni Iraola's Liverpool may well be pleased with how things played out in Monte Carlo. They will host Atletico Madrid, Porto, Villareal and Lens and travel to Inter Milan, Club Brugge, Fenerbahce and LASK.

Europa League champions Aston Villa, who started their season with a 4-0 pasting at Brighton and Hove Albion, will also host PSG and travel to Barcelona, like City. Borussia Dortmund, and Greenwood's Fenerbahce and Viking will travel to Birmingham while Emery's side will go to Club Brugge, Galatasaray and Slavia Prague.

Bradford-born Greenwood's last appearance in England was in January 2022 for Manchester United. He was subsequently suspended after being arrested on suspicion of rape and did not play for the club again. After charges were dropped a year later, he was loaned to Getafe before joining Marseille on a permanent deal. The 24-year-old moved to the Turkish club this summer. Greenwood may also head to London to face Shakhtar Donetsk, who are playing their home matches at Stamford Bridge thanks to the ongoing war in Ukraine.

Mourinho, Bellingham and Co will also be due at Chelsea's home, along with Sporting Lisbon and AEK Athens. UEFA rules dictate a minimum of five per cent of tickets should go to away supporters but there is no maximum, meaning the Ukrainians could secure much-needed funds from their stint at their temporary residence.

Liverpool will be happier than Arsenal and City with their Champions League fixtures

Fenerbahce's Mason Greenwood will play on English soil for the first time since January 2022

Elsewhere, Fabregas will return to Barcelona with Como, while Mourinho will head back to Roma, where he was sacked after two years in 2024.

Fans of Celtic may well have been left wondering what might have been following their spectacular second-leg collapse to LASK. The Austrians, who overcame a four-goal deficit against the Glaswegians in a disastrous play-off for Martin O'Neill's side, will host Liverpool and travel to the Bernebeu to face Real Madrid.

Following the completion of the League Stage, those in 25th to 36th place will be eliminated, while those from ninth to 24th will play two-legged knockout play-offs in February. The top eight automatically progress to the Round of 16, which will take place in March.

Bournemouth, Sunderland, Crystal Palace and Brighton and Hove Albion will learn their opponents in Friday's Europa League and Europa Conference draws.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez being axed from Chelsea squad signals he is Man City bound: Why wantaway star's absence from squad spoke volumes as Xabi Alonso reveals why he decided to leave him out against Luton
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez being axed from Chelsea squad signals he is Man City bound: Why wantaway star's absence from squad spoke volumes as Xabi Alonso reveals why he decided to leave him out against Luton

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

We love a transfer update in today's world of club-to-club talks and verbal agreements and sources whispering this and that, but there is nothing quite as clear as a surprise absentee on a match day.

It smacks of something happening behind the scenes, and Manchester City target Enzo Fernandez was nowhere to be seen at Stamford Bridge, neither in the team nor on the bench nor in the stands supporting his team-mates in this Carabao Cup second-round victory.

That was despite Xabi Alonso telling us a day previous that he intended on using him against League One visitors Luton. Chelsea did not need him. They won by two goals, with Danny Welbeck scoring and Hakeem Odoffin sending Estevao Willian's shot into his own net. They arguably should have won by six with the chances that Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers had.

We will never know whether Chelsea's home fans would have embraced Fernandez as warmly as their away counterparts did in their Premier League win at Fulham earlier this week.

Those supporters at Craven Cottage applauded him, sang his name, showed why they would like him to stay. They showered him with more love than he arguably deserved after a summer of such noise. Fernandez has millions of followers on social media. It would take only a single post for him to reaffirm his commitment to Chelsea and quieten that commotion if he wanted.

He has not done that, and now he has been left out of a squad for a match that his manager said he wanted to use him in. When asked about his absence at his post-match press conference, Alonso said it was his decision after speaking with his player.

Enzo Fernandez looks set to join Manchester City after being omitted from Chelsea's squad

In his absence, Danny Welbeck scored Chelsea's opener as they beat Luton 2-0 on Thursday

Estevao thought he scored Chelsea's second but it went down as a Hakeem Odoffin own goal

'It was a decision from myself and from the club,' Alonso said. 'We had other players that needed minutes and it was that way. It's a decision that I took. He's a good professional. He's training well. I have nothing to say about him. It was just a decision that we had to take, thinking about the game that we're playing tonight and we'll see for (Brighton on) Sunday.'

City want Fernandez, and Fernandez wants City. We are 74 days into this summer window and he has not yet been reunited with his former head coach, Enzo Maresca. That is largely because City left it so late to make a serious play for him with his £120million valuation. But as we approach September 1, it is looking increasingly likely that he will be City's and Maresca's soon.

Fernandez's Argentinian team-mate Valentin Barco started here – and was booed by Luton fans for his behaviour at the World Cup – but Chelsea would still need to replace Fernandez. Whether that is with an Alex Scott from Bournemouth or an Adam Wharton from Crystal Palace, we will see.

Mike Penders is Chelsea's future, but Emi Martinez is what the Blues need now to be elite

All summer, Chelsea insisted they were not interested in signing a new goalkeeper and that they were perfectly happy with Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders as their one-two.

When linked with Mike Maignan of AC Milan, you would hear the above. When linked with Diogo Costa of Porto, the above again. However, it was while Sanchez and Penders were warming up for this Carabao Cup clash that we received word how Emiliano Martinez was signing from Aston Villa, a fee of £7.5million having been agreed for the Argentinian who turns 34 next week.

Martinez is viewed by many as an upgrade on Sanchez, who may now leave this summer as a consequence. This news follows the 28-year-old Spaniard's substandard performance away at Fulham. While Chelsea won 3-2, the two goals he leaked were avoidable, and arguably his fault.

It may be a knee-jerk reaction entering into the window's final week - and just the latest example of Chelsea and Villa conducting business after Morgan Rogers, Alejandro Garnacho and, soon, Nicolas Jackson - but Stamford Bridge's supporters will have been glad to hear it.

They know Sanchez is a good goalkeeper, but not enough to help them become an elite side, and the Matthew Harding Stand backed Penders on his Chelsea debut. The 21-year-old Belgian's potential is high. He was good with his feet, and strong when clawing away and catching crosses.

Mike Penders (right) demonstrated his potential by keeping a clean sheet for the Blues

Pedro Neto's defensive work impresses Chelsea fans

Pedro Neto was brought on as a substitute here, and after Reece James gave him a rollicking for not tracking back at Fulham, he made a point of doing so here against Luton.

Neto earned a round of an applause from Stamford Bridge's supporters when he performed those defensive duties.

Sports.title: Pakistan threatened refusing to play after lunch against England after complaining to Sky Sports over interview with sons of imprisoned ex-captain and prime minister Imran Khan
Sports.content:
The first day of the second Test was almost derailed after it emerged that the Pakistan Cricket Board were unhappy with Sky Sports' decision to broadcast an interview with the two sons of the imprisoned former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan.

Cricinfo reported that the PCB briefly threatened to delay the resumption after the lunch break, during which Sky broadcast Mike Atherton's interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, who said they feared for their father's life following three years in jail on corruption charges.

Sky delayed broadcasting the 18-minute interview, and the Pakistan team eventually took the field as planned - avoiding a repeat of the 2006 Test at The Oval, where captain Inzamam-ul-Haq detained his players in the dressing-room after umpire Darrell Hair accused them of ball-tampering. That Test was ultimately forfeited.

The heavily politicised PCB are sensitive to any criticism of government policy, and have denied mistreating the 73-year-old Imran, who was Pakistan prime minister for nearly four years until April 2022, or of forbidding prison visits by his family and lawyers.

Pakistan Cricket Board were unhappy with Sky Sports' decision to broadcast an interview with the two sons of the imprisoned ex-Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran Khan (pictured)

Khan has been in jail for three years on corruption charges and there are concerns about his health

The latest tension follows a letter sent last week to Shehbaz Sharif, the current PM, and signed by 21 former cricket captains - Atherton included - from England, Australia, India, New Zealand and West Indies, calling for Imran to receive proper medical care while behind bars.

Imran, who remains a folk hero for many millions in his home country, captained Pakistan for 48 Tests between 1982 and 1992, and most famously lifted the 1992 World Cup after beating England in the final at Melbourne.

Sports.title: JABLONEC 1 RANGERS 0 (1-1 on agg, Jablonec win 4-3 on penalties): Rangers crash to a new low with humiliating European exit
Sports.content:
A night of abject humiliation for Derek McInnes and his Rangers team. A night of total ineptitude and failure against a team of no-marks from the Czech Republic.

A night where Rangers produced 120 minutes of the most wretched football imaginable. In the end, this was a night which shortens the lifespan of managers.

McInnes cannot hide from this. He should not be spared once the inquest begins. If the failure to overcome Jagiellonia Bialystok in the Europa League qualifiers was bad enough, this was on a whole different level.

Jablonec were third-rate opposition in a third-rate competition. Yet, still, Rangers could not secure a place in the UEFA Conference League.

They will now have no European group-stage football for the season ahead, the first time that has happened since they were dumped out against Progres Niederkorn back in 2017.

This result belongs in the same bracket as Progres. Make no mistake about it, in the hall of shame, this embarrassment ranks right up there.

Rangers players don't know where to look as they crash out of Europe on penalties

The performance Rangers served up would have made your eyes bleed. Leading 1-0 from the first leg, Jablonec took the tie to extra-time thanks to a goal from Vakhtang Tchanturishvili.

Rangers offered nothing. Zilch. The game plan looked nothing more than to try and scrape through by the skin of their teeth.

When the tie went to penalties, it was James Penrice and Findlay Curtis who missed. But only a fool would hold them responsible.

The very fact this tie went to penalties should illustrate the problems facing Rangers right now. McInnes is already under major pressure – and rightly so.

He has signed a dozen new players; six of them were in the starting line-up last night, and another two came off the bench.

This is his team. This result is on him as manager. How ironic that his old club, Hearts, are safely through to the group-stage of this competition after an excellent victory over Rapid Vienna.

Rapid Vienna are miles better than Jablonec. That didn’t stop Wouter Vrancken, another new manager piecing together a team with several new players, from leading Hearts to a terrific result.

The excuse about new players needing time to bed in is routinely the excuse of a manager who has made a poor start. For McInnes, there can be no such excuse.

Rangers should have had more than enough to get the job done against this level of opposition. But they failed. Plain and simple.

The strain on Derek McInnes is all too clear as his woeful start at the club reached a new low

McInnes stuck with the same 4-3-3 system that he had deployed over the last few matches, with Ryan Naderi once again getting the nod up front.

It was Naderi’s goal at Ibrox last week that ensured Rangers would take a 1-0 lead with them as they travelled to the Czech Republic for the second leg.

Lawrence Shankland once again started the match on the bench. We may only be at the end of August, but it is already clear that the newly appointed club captain is not a guaranteed first-pick.

With the £9million arrival of Kevin Kelsy from Portland Timbers now understood to be imminent, Shankland will face even stiffer competition for a place in the team from the Venezuelan international striker.

Much of the pitch at the Stadion Strelnice was still bathed in sunshine as kick-off approached. A small arena housing just shy of 6,000 fans, it almost looked like a pre-season friendly.

The start of the match certainly lacked intensity as both teams struggled to find any sort of rhythm or assert their authority on proceedings.

Dan Neil captained Rangers from the base of the midfield three and he soon cut a frustrated figure at the lack of movement and options ahead of him.

It was Jablonec who had the first clear sight of goal on 13 minutes when a neat through ball from Jan Suchan released Lamin Jawo in behind the Rangers defence.

Jawo only had Ivor Pandur to beat but he drilled his shot low into the side netting at the near post when he really ought to have gone across the goalkeeper.

Rangers continued to show no creativity in midfield or out wide. Starved of service, Naderi was no more than a passenger for the majority of the first half.

Given the paucity of what Rangers had served up during those opening 45 minutes, it was no surprise that McInnes made a triple substitution at half-time and changed the shape of the team.

Findlay Curtis reacts to his missed penalty as Rangers throw away their shoot-out advantage

On came Shankland, Findlay Curtis and Connor Barron; off went Neil, Daisuke Yokota and Djeidi Gassama. Given that Neil was captain, being hooked at half-time was a damning indictment on his performance.

Rangers initially looked brighter, with Curtis showing some pace and trickery to get at his full-back down the right flank.

There was a half-chance for Shankland early in the second half but his shot was quickly shut down by a couple of Jablonec defenders.

Rangers continued to live dangerously. They were cut wide open on the counter-attack on 53 minutes, with Richard Sedlacek racing clean through on goal. He fired his shot wide of target, only for the whistle to be blown for a marginal offside call. Regardless of being spared by the assistant’s flag, it was alarming just how easily Rangers had been exposed.

A one-goal lead always looked fragile and it was Jablonec who grew stronger as the match wore on. When the Czechs scored on 73 minutes, nobody could argue it hadn’t been coming.

The goal came down the left side of the Rangers defence, with Chanturishvili doing a Cruyff turn and selling a dummy to Penrice.

Chanturishvili drove forward inside the penalty area and fired a low shot towards goal, the ball taking a deflection as it flew past Pandur and into the net.

Plainly, Rangers could have no complaints. It had been an awful performance, completely devoid of any guile or artistry in midfield and forward areas.

Standing on the touchline in his collar and tie, the suit jacket had long since been removed for McInnes given the heat. He cut an animated figure, even exasperated at times.

Rangers had 15 minutes to try and find a response but they never even came remotely close. The fact they finished the 90 minutes with only one shot on target spoke volumes about the performance.

McInnes had made five substitutions, desperately seeking to find some kind of positive formula, but none of them really worked.

Substitute Connor Barron closes down Jiri Slama of Jablonec in his side's awful defeat

It was just chopping and changing, throwing mud at a board and hoping that something would eventually stick. Even more galling was the fact that Jablonec themselves looked bang-average.

Rangers were a rabble, no plan whatsoever on the ball, no patterns of play. All of the brighter moments came from the home side as the game progressed into extra-time.

One last roll of the dice came with the introduction of Bojan Miovski at half-time in extra-time. Given that McInnes clearly hasn’t fancied Miovski thus far, that in itself spoke of the sheer desperation of it all.

Jablonec had another good chance when Filip Novak was allowed to turn and shoot inside the area, but Pandur got them out of jail by making a decent low save.

When the penalty shootout came around, Rangers had the initiative when Pandur saved Jablonec’s third spot-kick from Filip Zorvan. But Curtis and Penrice then missed successive spot-kicks; Curtis blazing his high over the bar and Penrice seeing his saved by Jan Hanus.

That left Jan Chramosta with the chance to win it for the Czechs – and he made absolutely no mistake as he blasted the ball past Pandur.

This was humiliation for Rangers, on a par with anything you’d care to mention over their recent history. Progres Niederkorn, Club Brugge, now Jablonec.

With a trip to face Aberdeen at Pittodrie on Sunday, and back-to-back Old Firm games against Celtic in September, McInnes is already under serious pressure.

Sports.title: Enzo Fernandez LEFT OUT of Chelsea squad to face Luton: Wantaway Blues star 'available' but dropped by Xabi Alonso with club braced for £100m Man City bid
Sports.content:
Enzo Fernandez LEFT OUT of Chelsea squad to face Luton: Wantaway Blues star 'available' but dropped by Xabi Alonso with club braced for £100m Man City bid

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Enzo Fernandez has been omitted from Chelsea's matchday squad for their League Cup second-round 2-0 win over Luton Town, as speculation over his future at the club intensifies amid Manchester City's interest.

The 25-year-old is wanted by City before the transfer window closes on September 1 - with the Etihad outfit preparing a £100million bid, as reported by Daily Mail Sport. Even if that offer does come it is set to be rejected, with Chelsea wanting £120m.

Despite Fernandez's uncertain future, Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso insisted that the Argentine would be part of his squad for Thursday's Carabao Cup second-round tie at home to Luton.

However, when the team news came out on Thursday evening, Fernandez's name was nowhere to be seen in the 20-man squad.

Asked about Fernandez's absence from the squad against Luton, Alonso said pre-match: 'We assessed situations, individual and collective and we have decided he is not in the squad for today.'

However, speaking post-match the Spaniard was a lot more open, revealing that the decision was made by himself and the club hierarchy.

Manchester City target Enzo Fernandez was left out of Chelsea's squad that beat Luton 2-0

Xabi Alonso insisted ahead of the game Fernandez would be involved in the Carabao Cup tie

'It was a decision from myself and from the club,' Alonso said. 'We had other players that needed minutes and it was that way. It's a decision that I took. He's a good professional. He's training well. I have nothing to say about him.

'It was just a decision that we had to take, thinking about the game that we're playing tonight and we'll see for (Brighton on) Sunday.'

Speaking on Wednesday, Alonso was adamant to see his No 8 involved, saying: 'Yes, so we expect that he's involved.

'He's trained, he's training really well, he's a good professional and he will be involved.'

When pressed on whether he wants Fernandez to remain a Chelsea player after this window, Alonso added: 'We want to have the best team possible. We know his qualities. He has shown it. We have to wait, but we will think about tomorrow and let's see how things develop.

'We assess the whole squad as a unit and in that squad, we want good balance in terms of quality, in terms of positions, in terms of personalities, so we are aware of everything and we are prepared for whatever.'

Danny Welbeck and a Hakeem Odoffin own goal saw Chelsea beat their League One opponents and set up a third-round home showdown with fierce rivals Leeds United next month.

Sports.title: Fulham 2-0 Wimbledon:
Sports.content:
With season tickets in the Riverside Stand costing £3,192, Fulham’s fans have come to expect a certain level of comfort with their scallops and risotto.

But for nearly a full half here, the Cottagers were left groaning at the hospitality on show - until the Wimbledon dam burst to lighten the mood for Alvaro Arbeloa.

The Spaniard can sleep easily after securing his first competitive win on the back of a long summer where his suitability to replace Marco Silva has been relentlessly questioned.

It was not marquee opposition - Wimbledon are tipped to struggle in League One - but Arbeloa will be pleased that his second string had enough persistence to overcome a stubborn rearguard action against their noisy neighbours.

For a while, it felt as if Fulham would be left frustrated. You know things are getting desperate when, as the relative giants, your fans start encouraging defenders to shoot from the back end of nowhere.

Whatever the attack, Wimbledon had an answer; Andy Yiadom or Dan Sweeney would somehow materialise to defuse whatever Kevin or Rodrigo Muniz were plotting.

Alvaro Arbeloa secured his first victory as Fulham boss with a 3-0 win over Wimbledon

Emile Smith Rowe opened the scoring late on in frustrating a frustrating first half for the hosts

Rodrigo Muniz (above) doubled the lead before the break, and Gonzalo Garcia bagged late on

All empires crumble eventually, though, and the breakthrough came with a tactile sense of relief when Emile Smith Rowe finally turned in a scruffy header after a 37-minute toil which had felt like two hours.

Muniz then doubled the lead with another header minutes before half-time to make the rest of the night feel rather academic.

The second half largely mirrored how the first had gone, with Fulham pushing but often being thwarted. Smith Rowe, who could have had a hat-trick, crashed a half-volley over the bar as Fulham pressed for a third.

Gonzalo Garcia finally gave those who had stayed until the end a final hurrah, as he came off the bench and rounded goalkeeper Nathan Bishop to score his second Fulham goal since joining for £34m from Real Madrid.

Wimbledon had their chances - Callum Maycock missed by molecules with one flicked effort, while Myles Hippolyte went for the spectacular from range - and the packed away end stayed boisterous throughout despite losing this first derby against Fulham since the club’s rebirth.

Fulham's busy week continues with a trip to Sunderland on Sunday, a match which could be very consequential come the end of the season, and they have booked a visit to West Ham in the third round of the Carabao Cup.

'The players did a good job with energy and effort,' said Arbeloa. 'We moved the ball really well, tried to attack, score goals. We controlled Wimbledon’s counter-attacks. I’m happy with the performance and attitude.

'Of course we have a lot of things to work on but it’s a long journey. I saw a team with clear ideas.'

Arbeloa knows sterner tasks lie ahead, but the man inspired by the Spartan army will bite your hand off for any battling victory in these early days.

Sports.title: Chelsea agree £7.5m deal for Emiliano Martinez: Argentina No 1 is finally set to leave Aston Villa - and fix Xabi Alonso's goalkeeper problem
Sports.content:
Emi Martinez is poised to join Chelsea from Aston Villa for £7.5million - the fourth deal involving the clubs this summer.

The Argentina goalkeeper has been surplus to requirements at Villa Park since the club signed Zion Suzuki from Parma earlier this month.

It means Martinez, Lucas Digne, Ollie Watkins and Youri Tielemans should all have left by the end of the transfer window - and they were four of Villa’s highest earners.

That creates space in the wage bill for Nicolas Jackson, Leon Goretzka and - perhaps - Rafael Leao.

Villa’s financial offer to Leao is considerably lower than that offered by Galatasaray, but Villa hope the chance to play in the Premier League will sway it for the AC Milan forward.

Emi Martinez is poised to join Chelsea from Aston Villa for £7.5million - the fourth deal involving the clubs this summer

Martinez saw a move to Juventus collapse earlier this month despite an initial £6million offer, with Unai Emery happy to press ahead with Suzuki and Marco Bizot as his goalkeeping options.

Earlier in the summer, Chelsea boss Xabi Alonso indicated he was happy with keepers Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders.

But Sanchez's shaky display in Chelsea's 3-2 win at Fulham raised more question marks about the Spaniard.

Asked about Sanchez on Wednesday, Alonso said: 'Normal conversations. We have talked more about the team thing, about what we did well and what we have to do better. It was more about understanding the context.

'Every game is going to be important because we are in this process that we still need to develop things, we need to make adjustments that are more team-related.'

Sports.title: Good Good's golf empire crumbles in dramatic fashion as PGA Tour deal is scrapped in latest blow for YouTube stars after 'tone deaf' Callaway ad
Sports.content:
Good Good's golf media empire took another hit on Thursday afternoon in the wake of the backlash to its now-deleted Callaway advert.

Good Good, a YouTube channel that has become a booming business empire, came under fire over clip that showed co-founder Garrett Clark shoving a female co-host to the ground.

Both Callaway and Good Good pulled the commercial from all platforms and posted groveling apologies.

But the repercussions kept coming for the YouTube channel as its sponsorship of a PGA Tour has been pulled.

Good Good had set to be the title sponsor of a PGA Tour event in Austin in November, but is now walking away from the $6 million sponsorship.

'The PGA TOUR has been informed of Good Good Golf's decision to step away as sponsor of the event in Austin, Texas, this fall,' the Tour announced in a statement.

Good Good, a YouTube channel that has become a booming business empire, came under fire over clip that showed co-founder Garrett Clark shoving a female co-host to the ground

The popular golf social media brand has seen backlash from fans and sponsors over the ad

'We agree with their decision to use this time to focus on their organization and the work ahead.

'The PGA TOUR believes in golf's ability to bring people together and create a welcoming environment for all.'

The Tour confirmed that the tournament would continue as scheduled from November 12-15, 2026, with plans on a new sponsor to come.

Good Good also announced the decision to step away as a sponsor, saying that it came after 'thoughtful discussions' and 'careful reflection.'

'We recognize that we have work to do as an organization, and our focus right now is on our team, our culture and ensuring we learn from this situation,' a statement read.

The news came just hours after Callaway, the golf club manufacturer, cut ties with th embattled content creators.

On Thursday, Callaway released a statement confirming it had 'ended its relationship with Good Good, effective immediately.'

The golf giant said: 'Over the last several days, we have listened and reflected deeply on the hurt and disappointment caused by the video we reposted.

The PGA Tour announced that Good Good has stepped away from its sponsorship of an event

The video depicts Good Good co-founder Garrett Clark body-checking collaborator Alexis Miestowski to the ground as she attempted to reach for a branded driver

'We heard from individuals who shared personal experiences related to violence against women, and their stories were powerful reminders that this issue touches the lives of far too many people.

'Unequivocally, violence against women is unacceptable and should never be trivialized, normalized, or used as entertainment.'

Callaway revealed that it had completed a 'review' of the saga and would take several steps beyond cutting ties with Good Good.

'In this instance, our content review process was not comprehensive enough. We have taken appropriate internal corrective actions and significantly strengthened our approval procedures to help ensure this doesn't happen again,' the statement continued.

'We are committing $1million to support organizations working to prevent violence against women, provide resources to survivors, and advance education and awareness efforts.

'These actions do not undo the harm caused or excuse our role in it. We sincerely apologize to everyone who was hurt, disappointed, or offended by this incident.

'One of Callaway Golf's core values is to be a positive influence, both in the game of golf and in our communities. We are further strengthening our commitment to these initiatives, and this will be an ongoing focus in our company. We are committed to learning from this incident and helping ensure that golf is a place where everyone feels respected, valued, and welcome.'

The full-60 second ad - for the Good Good-branded Callaway Quantum driver - was supposed to be a spoof of the popular horror movie 'Obsession.'

The full Good Good driver video was actually 60 seconds long, and it seems like it was meant to be some sort of horror-movie spoof? It’s still viewable in some posts. (Here’s most of it:) pic.twitter.com/UBhUmKBQZY — Stina Sternberg (@StinaSternberg) August 24, 2026

The ad shows Clark standing over Miestowski and telling her not to touch his club

But the opening of the  shows Clark rushing over and body-checking Good Good member Alexis Miestowski as she reached for the golf club.

As Miestowski lay flat on her back on the ground, Clark is seen standing over before angrily saying: 'Do not touch my new driver.'

The rest of the ad shows other members of the content team somehow becoming possessed by the golf club before the video ends.

In a video released following the backlash, Clark apologized and even called the commercial the 'worst ad known to man' - despite being the person at the center of the controversy.

'I wanted to first start by saying, I personally want to apologize for playing the role in this skit, in this ad, at the magnitude that I did, and then on Good Good's behalf and Good Good marketing team's behalf, I wanted to say an apology as well because this is not at all what we stand for,' he began.

'Once again, I want everyone to know that I do not support DV [domestic violence] abuse or any of that, of any kind. So that's the first thing I want to say, and I also wanted to offer you guys some clarity on the situation, if you guys are willing to hear.'

Clark added that the ad was supposed to draw inspiration from the popular horror movie but clearly missed the mark.

'Looking back, super dumb ad concept,' he admitted. 'Terrible ad in general, not the greatest idea.'

Garrett Clark posted his own apology video after the disastrous Callaway advert was pulled

He was also keen to drive home the point that it was a 'complete skit' and 'I didn't actually tackle a woman', adding: 'I never would, and I didn't.'

Clark went on to tell his followers: 'Once I watched it back and it got posted, my skin was crawling. I was cringing.

'I mean, just even minutes after I saw it get posted, before this surfaced everywhere online, I thought it was the worst ad known to man.

'The beginning of the ad was very intense with the way that that was pushed out there, and just not good all around. Not good. So I wanted to say that.'

He then went on to defend Miestowski - the woman pushed to the ground in the clip - and asked for abuse to be directed at him rather than her.

' Her DMs have been, I think, completely unacceptable,' he said. ' I know Alexis is struggling with a lot of this... put it towards me personally. I can handle it. If you want to leave them in these these comments, you're welcome to.

'If you got any left in the tank, give Good Good some hate. You can give me some hate in the comments down below.

'I do sincerely apologize for playing the role that I did in that ad, and I want you guys to know that I in no way, shape, or form support DV abuse or anything of the sort.'

Clark also defended Miestowski, saying her social media had been flooded with 'unacceptable' messages and instead told commenters to direct their anger toward himself and the brand

The  was created to promote a branded version of the Callaway Quantum driver

Backlash against the video was swift and came not only from golf fans but also by other brands that carried the products of the content creators - or those who collaborated with them.

On Tuesday, the Golf Channel posted a statement to reveal that the premiere of 'Big Break x Good Good' was being pushed back a week , after one of the show's sponsors requested that its branding be removed from the series.

Although Golf Channel did not identify the sponsor, multiple reports said it was retailer Golf Galaxy, which had been listed as a presenting sponsor of the show.

Hours later, images and reports began surfacing showing that Golf Galaxy and Dick's Sporting Goods had begun pulling all Good Good products from their shelves.

As criticism began to spiral, Good Good released a statement which read: 'We posted a video to our channels that ultimately depicted actions that are not aligned with our values as a brand. We have since taken that content down and sincerely apologize.'

The statement added: 'Good Good has always stood for making the game of golf more inclusive to all, and we will continue to ensure that is our mission moving forward.'

Good Good rose from the Covid-era golf boom and is one of the sport's most popular content creators, boasting over two million subscribers on YouTube. The cast of the group has changed since inception, but formerly included the likes of pro golfer Luke Kwon and YouTube golfer Grant Horvat.

Their stock rose so much that Good Good was named the title sponsor of the new PGA Tour event in Austin, Texas, this fall. That, however, has now also collapsed amid their crumbling empire.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
