Sports.title: Stats: McLaren win Formula 1’s last Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort – again | 2026 Dutch Grand Prix stats and facts
Sports.content:
The Dutch Grand Prix became a Max Verstappen stronghold when it returned to the calendar six years ago. The Red Bull driver won each of the first three grands prix at his home track.

However the final three editions of the race were all won by McLaren. Lando Norris claimed back-to-back wins either side of the summer break.

This was the last Dutch Grand Prix for the foreseeable future as Zandvoort does not have a deal for F1 to return. Just as when it hosted the last race of its previous stint as an F1 venue in 1985, McLaren won the final race.

On that occasion Niki Lauda claimed his 25th and, as it turned out, final victory. He had announced his retirement plans at his home event one week earlier.

Norris’s win was his 13th, giving him as many as two-times world champion Alberto Ascari and David Coulthard. He also took his 18th pole position, giving him as many as Mario Andretti, Kimi Raikkonen and Rene Arnoux.

Although Ferrari failed to win on the modern Zandvoort layout, they remain the most successful team at the track with eight wins to McLaren’s six. Ferrari’s last win came courtesy of Arnoux in 1983. Mercedes also did not manage to win at Zandvoort during its return; their only victory at the track remains Juan Manuel Fangio’s 1955 triumph.

Charles Leclerc denied Norris a hat-trick by recording the 13th fastest lap of his career. He now has as many as 1983 world champion Alan Jones, plus Jacky Ickx and Riccardo Patrese.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Regardless of how the weekend turned out, Andrea Kimi Antonelli was always going to go to his home race next week as the world championship leader. With a 59-point lead, he is now guaranteed to head the standings when F1 departs Europe for the final nine ‘flyaway’ rounds.

George Russell claimed his fourth sprint race victory but failed to make any inroads on Antonelli’s points lead after following his team mate home in the grand prix.

Liam Lawson made his 50th appearance at a grand prix weekend back at the team he made his 15th and 16th participations with at the beginning of last year. His second stint at Red Bull was much more successful than his first as he finished seventh, despite a 10-second time penalty.

His return to Red Bull came about due to Isack Hadjar’s unfortunate injury. This also prevented Hadjar extending his run of seven consecutive points-scoring finishes.

Verstappen’s first-lap retirement meant Lawson was the only driver to score points for Red Bull. Prior to that Verstappen had never failed to finish outside the top two places at Zandvoort.

He has now gone 12 rounds without a grand prix victory. This is the second-longest win-less streak of his career, only behind the 30-race spell between his first and second grand prix victories in 2016 and 2017.

Advert | Become a RaceFans supporter and go ad-free

Yuki Tsunoda returned and finished one place outside of the points. Had he reached 10th he would have tied Kamui Kobayashi as Japan’s all-time top points-scorer.

The second half of 2026 ha begun much more brightly for Aston Martin following their upgrades in the last two races. Fernando Alonso took ninth place, their best result of the season so far. Team mate Lance Stroll remains one of only three drivers yet to score this year, along with the Cadillac duo, but he must fancy his chances now.

Sports.title: Domenicali hopeful Verstappen’s new deal will end talk of F1 exit | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Stefano Domenicali hopes Max Verstappen’s new Red Bull contract will put an end to claims he could leave Formula 1.

The Red Bull driver, who is one of the strongest critics of F1’s current regulations, said his uncertainty over agreeing a new deal with his team had been “mainly about actually continuing in Formula 1.”

Speaking ahead of Sunday’s Dutch Grand Prix, Domenicali said “the news of Max staying in Red Bull for the next couple of years is a cherry on the cake for this weekend.”

“It’s great news, [I’m] very proud and happy because Max is a world champion, world class person that has a great personality in the sport and I cannot see [imagine] Formula 1 without him.”

In May, Verstappen said it was “mentally not doable for me to stay” if F1 did not alter the power balance between the combustion and electrical parts of its engines next year. It subsequently announced changes will be introduced over the next two years.

“The rules are slowly getting a bit better and, let’s say, I’m willing to live with it,” said Verstappen. “Hopefully by 2030 it opens up another opportunity, potentially with V8 engines coming in, to look again.”

Domenicali hopes Verstappen’s new deal will quieten speculation the popular four-times champion will leave F1. “[I’m] very happy that this news now is official and all these talks that have been happening so far will be out of place,” he said. “Now I’m sure that the focus [will be] for the team to be as good as possible to give Max the best car that he can.”

Doubt continues to hang over the status of F1’s final two rounds this season, which will be held in the Middle East. The conflict in the region has already led F1 to abandon its plans to race in Saudi Arabia in Bahrain this year and arranged for the latter event to take place in Malaysia instead.

Domenicali indicated no decision has yet been taken to cancel the final two rounds in Qatar and the United Arab Emirates. “The calendar, as I said, is confirmed, so there are still a few tickets to be sold in Abu Dhabi,” he said. “Everything is progressing well, and we stay focused on delivering the calendar we promised at the beginning of the year.”

Sports.title: Featured Comment: Lenient response to drivers passing red light sets bad precedent | Brief
Sports.content:
Formula 1’s stewarding guidelines state drivers should receive 10-second stop-and-go penalties if they pass a red light at the pit lane exit during the grand prix.

However the stewards opted for much more lenient penalties when Oliver Bearman and Gabriel Bortoleto broke the rule at Zandvoort last weekend. Reader @Alianora-La-Canta says this sets a bad precedent:

The drivers had no way to know that no dangerous situations would be created by ignoring the red light. Therefore a penalty should have been issued that involved a sporting disadvantage. Even mitigating the penalty would be risky, if understandable (due to the point of the procedure, I recognise the risk should have been much lower than usual). Now people are going to ignore the red light if they think it’s under a red flag and they think there’s an advantage in doing so, which is dangerous because the drivers do not have the information the FIA does.

Sports.title: Verstappen to race 100 drivers at once in karts at Silverstone | Formula 1
Sports.content:
Max Verstappen will take on 100 drivers in a special go-kart race at Silverstone, Red Bull has announced.

The four-times world champion will start at the back of the grid with 100 rivals ahead of him.

“In go-karts you learn all the basics: starts, defending, overtaking,” said Verstappen. “Of course, I spent a long period of my life go-karting, so it’s always nice to return.

“It’s about understanding the grip of the go-kart. I’ve done so many years in go-karting that you quite naturally get back into things. I will be looking forward to just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me.”

Red Bull say Verstappen’s rivals will be drawn “from every corner of sport and culture: from Red Bull athletes and celebrities to content creators, personalities and everyday fans invited from around the world.”

The event will take place on September 16th, three days after the Spanish Grand Prix, at a specially designed track at the home of the British Grand Prix.

“Creating a track for 100 drivers at the same time has never been done, never been seen,” said circuit designer and race director David Terrien. “So it’s very exciting.

“When you have Max Verstappen chasing everyone, I think that’s going to be the experience of a lifetime for all the drivers. You’re going to have Max showcasing all these skills of looking through the traffic, trying to prepare and plan where he can overtake people, and going through the traffic at the fastest speed he can because he doesn’t want to let the drivers at the front pull away.”

The event will be broadcast in some territories on Disney Plus and the ESPN app.

Sports.title: Tyson Fury Has Replacements Ready If Joshua Fight Fails
Sports.content:
Netflix signed up for an international event driven by two famous British heavyweights and a rivalry years in the making. Its return comes through worldwide viewing, subscriber activity and interest beyond boxing’s regular audience, not individual pay-per-view sales alone. Remove Joshua, and that cultural event becomes a standard Fury broadcast against an unfamiliar opponent. Refusing to name either alternative also makes Brown’s announcement sound like pressure on Joshua’s side.

Fury’s camp is publicly presenting New York as a plan that can continue without him, but Brown still expects the original fight to be completed. Until Netflix confirms its involvement with another opponent, the alternatives provide Fury’s team with negotiating leverage more than certainty.

Netflix Faces A Difficult Replacement Decision

The available options leave Fury’s side trapped between commercial value and competitive danger. A soft opponent may not give Netflix enough reason to retain the date, venue and promotional budget. Madison Square Garden also becomes harder to fill once Joshua’s name is removed.

Selecting a leading heavyweight brings a different risk. Fury struggled badly against boxing newcomer Francis Ngannou before losing consecutive fights to Oleksandr Usyk. He looked heavy and slow in the second Usyk fight, with his movement and timing far removed from the fighter who controlled the heavyweight division earlier in his career.

Since then, Fury has beaten Arslanbek Makhmudov by a wide decision and stopped 46-year-old Mariusz Wach after seven rounds. Neither result proved that he is ready to defeat one of the division’s leading fighters. Makhmudov had already been stopped by Agit Kabayel and Guido Vianello, while Wach had lost 12 of his previous 18 fights. The last opponent Fury looked good against at championship level was Derek Chisora in December 2022, almost four years ago. Comfortable wins over carefully selected opposition do not erase what happened against Ngannou and Usyk.

Losing in November would damage the Joshua fight far more than another postponement. Yet selecting an opponent who offers little resistance may leave Netflix paying heavily for another tune-up.

Brown’s announcement shows that Fury’s camp has prepared for the Joshua negotiations to fail. It provides no assurance that Netflix will support the substitute plan or Madison Square Garden will remain the venue. Having two names available is the easy part. Finding someone credible enough for Netflix, manageable enough for Fury, and marketable enough for New York is the real difficulty.

Sports.title: WBA President Undercuts Teofimo Lopez’s Catterall Claim
Sports.content:
The timing and wording weaken Lopez’s argument that the requirement belonged only to Romero. Mendoza made the statement six weeks before Lopez captured the WBA welterweight title by majority decision on August 22. The obligation was described as applying to the winner rather than Romero alone.

Teofimo recently argued that he was not involved in the agreement requiring Romero to face Catterall within 180 days. His position was that beating Romero created a new championship situation because the original paperwork carried Romero’s name.

That contractual distinction does not answer Mendoza’s July 9 declaration. The WBA president knew Lopez was the challenger and publicly connected Catterall to the outcome. Lopez may not have signed Romero’s agreement, but he accepted the bout with that condition already stated.

The matchup also carries more danger than Catterall’s limited recognition in the United States might suggest. His patient southpaw counterpunching would require Lopez to lead and create openings without becoming reckless. Sandor Martin used movement, timing and the left-handed stance to disrupt Lopez in their disputed 2022 fight. Catterall would present some of the same complications while bringing greater experience at the championship level.

A step-aside payment offers one possible escape if Lopez pursues the Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn winner, but Catterall has already said he will not accept even “$1” to surrender his opportunity. If he maintains that stance, Lopez may eventually have to defend, persuade the WBA to approve another fight or vacate the belt.

Vacating would preserve Lopez’s freedom at the cost of weakening his claim to control the welterweight division. He has talked about pursuing three unifications without making a defense. Giving up the title to avoid the first opponent connected to it would turn that ambition into promotional language rather than a championship plan.

Mendoza’s post is not the same as a published ruling from the WBA Championships Committee ordering Lopez to make the defense. The organization still needs to state how it will enforce Catterall’s status now that the championship has changed hands.

However, Teofimo can no longer characterize Catterall as Romero’s obligation alone. The WBA president’s own words support the British fighter’s demand for the next opportunity.

Teofimo Lopez Claims Catterall Deadline No Longer Applies

Teofimo Lopez is attempting to separate himself from the WBA order requiring Rolando Romero to face Jack Catterall within 180 days. Lopez argues that defeating Romero changed the championship situation, but the WBA Championships Committee, not his legal team, will decide if the obligation carries over.

Teofimo Lopez Sends WBA Dispute to Legal Team

“The contract they signed, I was never involved in that contract or that agreement,” Lopez told Ariel Helwani. “It’ll go to my legal team, and we’ll talk. I don’t duck anybody. We’ll fight. “That contract they signed for an extension, for whatever it was, 180 days, was with the name Rolando ‘Rolly’ Romero, not Teofimo Lopez. That means the whole situation with the mandatory changes now. It’s a reset, and I think people are forgetting that.”

Lopez is free to offer that interpretation, but the WBA has not publicly ruled that Catterall’s position or the November 19 deadline disappeared when the title changed hands.

Catterall defeated Shakhram Giyasov on May 23 to get the WBA’s secondary welterweight belt. The organization then required Romero to face the winner within 180 days. Catterall maintains that the WBA has told him he is next and that promoter Eddie Hearn has written to WBA president Gilberto Mendoza requesting an immediate order.

Lopez’s legal team can argue that the original directive named Romero, but a mandatory requirement issued by a sanctioning body is not simply a private contract that binds only the two fighters named in it. The WBA committee can transfer the obligation, modify the deadline, or grant Lopez another fight. Until it makes that decision, Lopez cannot declare on his own that the process has restarted.

The new champion also cited the cut over his right eyebrow and his resulting medical suspension.

“I’m suspended by all commissions right now due to the cut over my right eye. Until I get my license back from the commission, we don’t need to talk about any mandatories at this particular time.”

That suspension prevents Teofimo from returning to the ring until he receives medical clearance. It does not prevent the WBA from confirming Catterall’s status or ordering negotiations for a later date.

Nobody is asking Lopez to defend the belt before the cut heals. The dispute concerns who receives his next defense after he is cleared. Catterall says the WBA has already given him that answer, while Lopez is trying to persuade the committee to give him a different one.

Mannix: Teofimo Lopez Knows Ryan Garcia Is Next

Chris Mannix says Teofimo Lopez and his team already know Ryan Garcia is likely to be his next opponent. Their confidence suggests they do not regard Jack Catterall’s mandatory WBA title consolidation as an obstacle that will stop the fight.

“Ryan Garcia is the name that is at the top of everybody’s list. Ryan Garcia is the name that Teofimo Lopez and his team know that they’re likely going to face,” Mannix said on his DAZN show with Sergio Mora. “In fact, win or lose this fight against Conor Benn, I think Ryan Garcia is going to be next for Teofimo.”

A Garcia victory over Benn on September 12 would allow Lopez to request permission for a WBA-WBC unification. The organization could authorize that fight, give Catterall another deadline and argue that consolidating championships took priority over immediately eliminating its own secondary title.

Losing to Benn would remove that justification. Garcia would no longer bring the WBC belt, leaving Lopez to choose a commercially valuable voluntary defense over a mandated consolidation. Allowing it would amount to the WBA discarding its order because Lopez found a more profitable opponent.

Catterall is not merely a contender waiting after winning an eliminator. He captured the WBA Regular welterweight title by defeating Shakhram Giyasov and was promised a fight against the primary champion within 180 days. Lopez inherited that obligation when he took the WBA title from Rolando Romero.

The sanctioning body must now decide how much its own order is worth. A Garcia unification would produce greater attention and a larger sanctioning fee, but another postponement would further reduce the value of holding its Regular title. Fighters are asked to compete for that belt, pay sanctioning fees and trust that victory will lead to the primary champion.

Lopez’s apparent freedom to plan around Catterall shows that commercial appeal may defeat enforcement. If the WBA permits Garcia to go first, especially after a loss to Benn, it will make itself look second-rate by showing that its orders apply only when champions have nothing richer available.

Matchroom Presses WBA To Force Teofimo Lopez vs. Jack Catterall

Jack Catterall confirmed Tuesday that Eddie Hearn and Matchroom sent a letter to the WBA in an attempt to get his title fight with Teofimo Lopez enforced.

“Letter was sent to them yesterday by Eddie and Matchroom,” Catterall posted on X in response to a supporter asking his team to act.

Catterall also revealed that WBA president Gilberto Mendoza personally promised him that the 180-day commitment would remain in place regardless of who held the Super title.

“When I met Gilberto Mendoza in Egypt, I shook his hand and he gave me his word if I beat Giyasov, someone who was avoided and waited for his shot for two years, I will get my shot within 180 days regardless who has the belt. So I believe the WBA will do the correct thing,” Catterall posted.

That account removes much of the uncertainty about what the WBA intended. Its published resolution named Rolando Romero, but its president allegedly told Catterall that the commitment followed the title. Lopez still has a technical argument based on the written wording, yet the WBA would have to break Mendoza’s personal promise to let him move on.

The dispute began after Lopez openly denied that Catterall was his mandatory during Monday’s Inside the Ring show. Lopez plans to pursue the three additional titles he needs to become the undisputed welterweight champion, beginning with the winner of Ryan Garcia versus Conor Benn on September 12.

That pursuit leaves no place for Catterall, but the secondary WBA champion has rejected the easiest negotiated solution.

“There’s not $1 that can persuade me to step aside to allow a unification bout to happen. I’m here to fight,” Catterall said.

His refusal means Matchroom cannot be paid to wait while Lopez pursues the Garcia vs. Benn winner. The WBA must enforce the consolidation fight, permit a unification first, or allow its two welterweight champions to remain separated.

The 180-day period expires on November 19, based on Catterall’s May 23 victory over Shakhram Giyasov. That leaves less than three months to settle the dispute. The cut Lopez suffered over his right eyebrow against Rolando Romero places more strain on the schedule, although there has been no indication that it will keep him out for an extended period.

Teofimo may believe the WBA will permit a unification to take priority over its internal consolidation fight. Sanctioning bodies regularly move mandatory obligations aside when champions pursue another belt, giving his team a stronger argument than the wording omission alone.

Catterall brings tactical risk with little financial reward. His awkward southpaw style and sharp counterpunching deny opponents clean offensive opportunities. Ryan Garcia, Conor Benn and Devin Haney generate massive paydays. Catterall brings no comparable commercial appeal, only a genuine threat to expose Lopez inside the ring.

WBA Loophole Gives Teofimo Lopez Easy Out On Jack Catterall

A review of the WBA’s published rulings supports part of Teofimo Lopez’s argument. No public order currently names Jack Catterall as the mandatory challenger for Lopez’s newly acquired Super welterweight title.

The May 21 ruling required Rolando Romero to face the Catterall-Shakhram Giyasov winner within 180 days. Its language named Romero specifically. It did not say the obligation would transfer to Romero’s successor if the title changed hands.

That omission gives Lopez a technical basis for denying that Catterall has been formally assigned to him. The WBA would need to issue another ruling, clarify that the original order followed the championship, or designate Catterall as Lopez’s challenger.

Teofimo still goes too far by claiming Catterall was lied to. The WBA sanctioned the Giyasov bout and publicly stated that its winner would receive Romero within 180 days. Catterall’s expectation came directly from the organization, not from an invented promise by his team.

The real issue is poor wording from the WBA. It created two champions and ordered them to meet, yet attached the obligation to Romero by name rather than clearly attaching it to the Super title. Lopez is now using that opening to pursue the Garcia-Benn winner while Catterall waits for the WBA to explain what its own ruling means.

Teofimo Lopez Denies Jack Catterall Mandatory Status

Teofimo Lopez claims Jack Catterall is not his WBA mandatory and says the British contender was lied to about his right to challenge for the welterweight title.

During today’s Inside the Ring show, Catterall confronted the new WBA champion after Lopez discussed facing the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner and eventually meeting Devin Haney for the undisputed championship.

“He’s not. He’s not my mandatory,” Lopez said when Catterall was identified as next in line. “By the sanctioning rules, he’s not my mandatory, and I think they lied. I think they lied to him.”

“It’s in the contract,” Catterall answered.

Teofimo’s denial conflicts with the WBA’s own published ruling. When the organization elevated Rolando Romero to Super champion in May, it sanctioned Catterall’s bout with Shakhram Giyasov for the vacant secondary title and stated that Romero had to face the winner within 180 days.

Catterall defeated Giyasov and now holds that belt. Lopez may argue that the ruling named Romero rather than whoever defeated him, or that no separate order has been issued since Saturday. Neither explanation supports his claim that Catterall was lied to. The WBA publicly connected the two titles and imposed a deadline for bringing them together.

The exchange became entertaining because Lopez tried to rewrite the situation while Catterall was on the screen looking directly at him. Rather than explain the supposed sanctioning rule, Teofimo declared that the obligation did not exist and blamed unnamed people for misleading Catterall.

After making that denial, the new champion returned to the familiar claim that he will face anyone.

“I’m always willing to fight anybody and everybody,” Lopez said.

“I’m glad you won on the weekend because I know you don’t duck nobody,” Catterall replied. “It would have been more difficult to get Rolly into the ring. I’m happy for you, but we’ve got to get it on.”

Catterall played the interaction perfectly. He congratulated Lopez, reminded him that Romero would have been harder to bring into the ring and declined to turn the conversation into a shouting match. That left Teofimo arguing against a contract he had not seen while Catterall calmly insisted the terms were already written down.

There was also some clever pressure inside Catterall’s praise. Telling Lopez, “I know you don’t duck nobody,” gave the champion little room to reject the fight without contradicting the reputation Catterall had just assigned to him.

The WBA now needs to explain the status of its own ruling. It can grant Lopez permission to pursue a unification, arrange a step-aside payment or order the title consolidation. What it cannot credibly do is remain silent while its new champion claims the other titleholder was fooled.

Lopez is clearly trying to look past the mandatory to chase the massive paydays against the Ryan Garcia vs. Conor Benn winner or a unification with Devin Haney. Catterall holds the regular belt after beating Shakhram Giyasov, which, in standard WBA procedure, makes him the direct mandatory to unify the titles.

Sports.title: Brandon Figueroa Gets Familiar Name Tomoki Kameda
Sports.content:
PBC announced Figueroa versus Kameda as the co-main event beneath Sebastian Fundora’s previously revealed WBC super welterweight title defense against Ermal Hadribeaj. The broadcast begins at 8 p.m. ET on TNT, truTV and DAZN.

Kameda’s selection is not ideal from a competitive-merit standpoint. The 35-year-old has not fought since losing a 12-round majority decision to IBF featherweight champion Angelo Leo in May 2025. He is moving directly from one failed title bid into another without recording a comeback win.

Familiarity is his appeal, but the name belongs to a fighter more than a decade removed from his best period. Kameda captured the WBO bantamweight title in 2013 and completed his three-defense reign the following year. His championship accomplishments are now part of boxing history rather than evidence of his present standing at featherweight.

Kameda has repeatedly fallen short when stepping up since that reign. He lost consecutive decisions to Jamie McDonnell in 2015, dropped a wide decision against Rey Vargas in 2019, and split two fights with Lerato Dlamini. His other wins came against middle-of-the-pack opposition before Angelo Leo defeated him last year.

That history limits how much can be taken from Kameda’s competitive performance against Leo. Another respectable defeat does not establish him as one of the leading featherweights. His recognizable name, durability and past championship remain the selling points.

Can Kameda Control Figueroa’s Pressure?

Through 47 professional fights, Kameda has never been stopped, but durability alone will not solve the tactical difficulty. Figueroa does his best work by forcing opponents into prolonged exchanges, attacking the body and maintaining a pace that becomes harder to match as rounds accumulate.

Keeping the fight at a controlled distance will require lateral movement, straight punches and counters. Kameda’s majority-decision loss to Leo showed that he can remain competitive over 12 rounds, although Figueroa presents a more exhausting physical test. That requires him to collect early rounds without allowing the champion to pin him down and begin sustained body attacks.

At featherweight, Figueroa looks physically established. Moving up from 122 pounds has not reduced his output, and the stoppage of Ball showed that his power carries late into championship fights. His combination of volume, physical pressure and finishing strength now gives opponents several concerns to manage.

Defensive openings remain available when Figueroa commits to extended combinations. Kameda’s best chance will come from making him miss during those attacks and answering before the champion resets his feet. Remaining on the ropes for extended periods would allow Figueroa to impose exactly the fight he wants.

“Brandon Figueroa is a great champion, and I know that when the bell rings, we’re going to give the fans a fight they’ll remember,” Kameda said.

This may also represent Kameda’s final title shot in a second division. More than 13 years have passed since he captured his bantamweight belt, and another defeat would leave him with consecutive losses in featherweight championship fights.

Carrington Fight Drives The Matchmaking

The booking gives PBC a practical compromise. Kameda is safer than placing Figueroa directly into another championship fight, but he is easier to promote than a little-known contender. His history, durability and competitive showing against Leo provide enough credibility for television. The weakness is that his selection follows a defeat and nearly 17 months of inactivity.

DAZN has already connected Figueroa with WBC featherweight champion Bruce Carrington. A unification between them would carry considerably more competitive value, with Carrington’s speed, movement and counterpunching testing Figueroa in ways Kameda may no longer be equipped to do.

This fight fills the space between Figueroa’s victory over Ball and a possible Carrington meeting. Kameda has enough experience to punish a poor performance, but his age, inactivity and latest result make this a favorable first defense for the champion.

Jermall Charlo will also meet Koen Mazoudier in a 10-round super middleweight bout on the October 17 card. Mazoudier defeated Sam Beck by decision on August 26 and will return fewer than eight weeks later.

Sports.title: Dmitrii Bivol And Callum Smith Agree WBO Title Fight
Sports.content:
“Please be advised that the WBO World Championship Committee has received written confirmation from RCC Boxing, on behalf of WBO Light Heavyweight Champion Dmitrii Bivol, and Matchroom Boxing, on behalf of Mandatory Challenger Callum Smith, confirming that the parties have reached terms, including an agreed date and venue for the WBO Light Heavyweight Mandatory Championship Contest. The WBO respectfully defers to the parties to formally announce the date, venue, and event details in due course,” said Olivieri on X.

Smith, 36, is finally getting the title opportunity he has waited for, but the financial value remains unknown. Bivol’s two fights with Artur Beterbiev were backed by Turki Alalshikh and carried undisputed championship status. A mandatory defense does not have the same commercial weight.

The venue will reveal more. Saudi involvement may turn the event into another major payday. If RCC Boxing and Matchroom are financing it without that support, Smith may receive considerably less than Bivol and Beterbiev earned from their two meetings.

Inactivity presents another concern for the challenger. He has not competed since going through a 12-round war with Joshua Buatsi in February 2025 and has boxed only twice since suffering a seventh-round knockout against Beterbiev in January 2024.

Bivol, 35, underwent back surgery after his questionable majority decision over Beterbiev in February 2025. He returned in May 2026 and defeated IBF mandatory Michael Eifert by a wide unanimous decision before undergoing surgery on his injured left elbow in July.

The champion has therefore boxed only once since the Beterbiev rematch and must now return from a second operation. Smith has been inactive longer, but neither man enters under ideal conditions. Bivol must show that his elbow permits him to throw combinations freely, while his challenger must overcome approximately 18 months outside the ring.

Those two Beterbiev bouts supplied Smith with a blueprint for troubling Bivol. Sustained aggression denied him room to settle, made him expend energy, and reduced the time available for his accurate combinations.

During the opening six rounds of their rematch, Beterbiev looked capable of breaking Bivol. His work rate dropped from the seventh through the 11th, however. Once he increased the pace in round 12, Bivol again looked vulnerable and close to being stopped.

Smith cannot afford similar quiet stretches. He must cut off the ring, attack the body and maintain the pace instead of following Bivol while absorbing straight punches. Knowing the plan and executing it for an entire championship bout are very different tasks.

At six feet three inches with a 78-inch reach, Smith owns major physical advantages but has not always used them effectively. He often retreats in straight lines before settling behind a static high guard near the ropes. That habit would give Bivol the stationary target he wants for his quick multi-punch combinations.

A counter left hook remains Smith’s best chance of changing the contest with one punch. Landing it cleanly will be difficult because Bivol maintains a disciplined defensive position while jabbing and rarely leaves his chin exposed for the shot that Smith used to stop Gilbert Castillo and Mathieu Bauderlique.

High guards also give Bivol opportunities rather than discouraging him. He can split the gloves with straight punches, attack around them with hooks and leave the pocket before the counter arrives. Canelo Alvarez and Gilberto Ramirez struggled to interrupt that rhythm once he began controlling the distance.

Their common opponents underline the size of Smith’s task. Bivol neutralized Canelo over 12 rounds and divided two close decisions with Beterbiev. Smith suffered a one-sided decision against Canelo before Beterbiev dropped him twice and stopped him in the seventh. Those results do not decide this contest, but they show that the champion has handled the elite opposition that overwhelmed his mandatory challenger.

At 36, this may be Smith’s final opportunity to win a world title in a second division. That urgency may force him to take risks, yet passive pursuit will not be enough. He needs to use his reach to push Bivol backward, work the body and prevent him from resetting without becoming trapped behind his guard.

Waiting preserved Smith’s mandatory position but took away valuable time near the end of his career. He finally has the opportunity he wanted. Now he must carry out an exhausting tactical blueprint against one of boxing’s most accurate technicians after approximately 18 months without competition.

Sports.title: Oscar Collazo Takes Major Flyweight Risk Against Sandoval
Sports.content:
Entering only his second fight at flyweight, Collazo is coming off a two-round stoppage of late replacement Neider Valdez. The 5-foot-2 unified minimumweight champion will give away four inches in height to the 5-foot-6 Sandoval while moving directly from a trial fight in the division to arguably its best fighter.

Sandoval earned the WBA and WBC titles by traveling to Japan and defeating Kenshiro Teraji by split decision in July 2025. He survived a fifth-round knockdown and recovered well enough to outwork Teraji across the later rounds.

That victory showed the difficulty of the task facing Collazo. The champion is larger, experienced against top opposition and capable of maintaining his output over 12 rounds. Collazo dominated at minimumweight, but beating fighters closer to his own size does not guarantee that his pressure and punching power will carry into a fight against a full-sized flyweight.

The seven-pound move from 105 to 112 represents nearly seven percent of Collazo’s former weight limit. He bypassed the 108-pound division entirely, although the Valdez bout gave him one short appearance at flyweight before challenging Sandoval. Two rounds against a late replacement could not show how his power, stamina and punch resistance will hold up against a natural 112-pound champion.

Their methods create a clear contest between precision and activity. Collazo uses timing, lateral movement and accurate body combinations, while Sandoval applied enough pressure and maintained sufficient output to defeat Teraji. The challenger must land with enough force to reduce that activity. Without earning Sandoval’s respect, the smaller man may struggle to control the pace over 12 rounds.

“Sandoval is a challenge that motivates me and my team. I was looking to make history and prove that there are no limits when you know what you’re capable of doing,” Collazo said. “This isn’t just for me. This is for Puerto Rico and to raise the level of Puerto Rican boxing.”

The southpaw stance gives Collazo a route inside. His rear left hand can reach Sandoval’s body from an angle, but he must cross the taller champion’s punching range to deliver it. Sandoval’s straight right hand and uppercut will be available whenever Collazo lowers himself or steps forward. Much may depend on how often the challenger reaches the body without taking a clean counter on his way inside.

Sandoval’s recovery against Teraji creates another question. He got up from a fifth-round knockdown and fought effectively enough over the remaining rounds to win the titles. Collazo carried useful power at 105 pounds, but hurting an established flyweight is a different physical test. Failure to slow the champion early may force him to match Sandoval’s activity deep into the contest.

His brief appearance against Valdez offered little evidence because it lasted less than two rounds. Collazo overwhelmed an opponent brought in on short notice, but Sandoval represents an entirely different level of resistance.

Rather than spending several fights adjusting to the division, Collazo is going directly after two flyweight championships while retaining his WBA and WBO minimumweight belts. Winning would give him recognized titles in two divisions simultaneously. This is far more than a ceremonial opportunity for a successful champion moving up in weight.

Sports.title: Janibek Wants Sheeraz Belt For Canelo Fight
Sports.content:
That complaint cannot conceal the competitive danger involved. Janibek is a former unified middleweight champion and the most accomplished available contender in the WBO’s top 15. Canelo is occupied with Christian Mbilli, while Diego Pacheco is pursuing another title. The WBO had few credible alternatives.

The speed of Janibek’s return still gives Sheeraz a legitimate complaint. His suspension was terminated on July 10, and he was installed as mandatory little more than a month later, allowing him to move above active super middleweights without first competing in the division. That decision favored proven championship credentials over activity at 168. Sheeraz can question that policy without claiming Janibek was still suspended when the order was issued.

Sheeraz Received A Comfortable Route

Sheeraz was given a high super middleweight ranking after his controversial draw against WBC middleweight champion Carlos Adames. His first three opponents at 168 were Edgar Berlanga, Alem Begic, and Simon Zachenhuber.

Berlanga had been heavily promoted without beating a leading super middleweight. He lost when he finally faced Canelo, returned against limited opposition, and was then stopped by Sheeraz. Begic was largely unknown when he fought for the vacant WBO title. Zachenhuber had little international profile before serving as the opponent for Sheeraz’s first defense. Neither had accomplished anything comparable to Janibek.

Placed alongside those three opponents, the former unified middleweight champion looks like gold. Moving up without a previous appearance at 168 is unusual, but it does not make Begic or Zachenhuber more qualified.

This run at super middleweight has been carefully managed. The Janibek order is the first time Sheeraz has been required to face someone with an established championship record and a realistic chance of beating him.

The styles explain some of the reluctance. Sheeraz has used his height, long jab, and right hand to control less sophisticated opponents from a distance. Janibek is a southpaw with sharper footwork, educated counters, and the experience to attack from angles Begic and Zachenhuber could not create. This is not merely a larger name. It is a considerable increase in tactical difficulty.

The Belt Comes With Responsibilities

Despite his criticism, Sheeraz has stopped short of refusing the defense. He told IFL TV that “if this is the fight, this is the fight,” while leaving the decision to his team. He also said they would examine how to make it most beneficial for him.

However, his repeated criticism makes it clear that Janibek is not the opponent Sheeraz and Queensberry wanted next. They now must decide how much they value the WBO title.

Negotiations also place Queensberry in a difficult promotional position. Allowing the defense to reach a purse bid could give another promoter control of the venue, broadcast arrangements, and conditions surrounding one of its most valuable fighters. Vacating would preserve matchmaking control but remove the championship leverage Sheeraz hopes to carry into negotiations with Canelo.

A similar issue can be seen in Teofimo Lopez’s reaction to inheriting Jack Catterall as his WBA welterweight mandatory. Teofimo wants Ryan Garcia or Conor Benn rather than a dangerous challenger carrying less commercial value. The two mandatories present the same basic inconvenience. Janibek and Catterall can defeat the champions, but neither supplies the enormous payday needed to make that danger appealing.

A decisive Janibek win could remove Sheeraz from the Canelo sweepstakes. Canelo is 36 and approaching the end of his career. If his October 31 fight with Mbilli goes badly, that opportunity may disappear before Sheeraz can rebuild from a damaging loss.

Holding the WBO belt does not guarantee Sheeraz a Canelo fight, but it supplies a unification storyline and separates him from Pacheco and other contenders pursuing the same opportunity.

That is not a reason for the organization to protect him. If boxing is going to operate as a sport instead of a popularity contest, champions must face qualified mandatories rather than selecting opponents entirely by commercial value.

The choice is simple: defend the title or surrender it. Sheeraz should not receive the championship status needed to pursue Canelo without accepting the difficult defense attached to that status.

Sports.title: George Foreman’s Drugged Water Claim Against Ali Resurfaces
Sports.content:
“It’s a theory that the fight was tampered with. For the older boxing guys what do yall think?” Prograis posted on X.

Foreman’s own account is more valuable than the theory raised by Prograis. The former heavyweight champion described receiving suspicious-tasting water shortly before the fight in his 2007 memoir, God in My Corner.

“Just before the fight with Ali, my trainer handed me a glass of liquid and said, ‘Here’s your water,’” Foreman wrote. “As I took a swig, I almost spit it out. ‘Hey, this water tastes like it has medicine in it.’”

Trainer Dick Sadler assured Foreman that it was the same water he had always received. The medicinal taste, Foreman said, remained when he went to the ring.

“After the third round, I was as tired as if I had fought 15 rounds,” Foreman wrote. “What’s going on here? Did someone slip a drug in my water?”

No test results or other evidence ever supported his account. Sadler died in 2003 and was unable to answer the version Foreman publicized four years later.

Ali Forced Foreman Beyond His Usual Script

Foreman had destroyed Joe Frazier in two rounds to win the heavyweight championship and stopped Ken Norton in the second. Those performances encouraged him to attack Ali with the same expectation of an early finish. Kinshasa produced a different fight. Foreman threw heavy punches from the opening bell, while Ali blocked shots with his arms, leaned away from others and struck him repeatedly with straight right hands. Many of Foreman’s widest punches either missed or landed without their full force.

Loose ropes helped Ali lean farther back, but the idea that Angelo Dundee deliberately loosened them remains disputed. Dundee complained about their condition and attempted to have them tightened. Ali still recognized how they could be used once the fight began.

That fatigue has a physical and tactical explanation without introducing an unidentified substance. Foreman maintained a knockout pace against an opponent who refused to disappear, forcing him to work longer than Frazier or Norton had.

Over time, his explanations for the loss included the loose ropes, referee Zack Clayton’s count and dissatisfaction with his corner. The drugged-water story later became the most serious of them.

By the eighth round, Foreman’s punches had lost much of their force. Ali landed a fast combination and dropped him for the knockout. Prograis has revived an old piece of boxing folklore, but the film continues to show Ali winning through cleaner punching, patience and control of Foreman’s aggression.

Muhammad Ali watches as George Foreman lies on the canvas during their heavyweight championship fight in Kinshasa, Zaire, on October 30, 1974. Foreman later alleged that his pre-fight water contained an unidentified substance. Photo: El Gráfico/Wikimedia Commons, public domain.

Sports.title: Vergil Ortiz Jr. Botches Ennis Fight, Leaves 154
Sports.content:
“Boots is part of the plan, but it doesn’t have to be next,” De La Hoya said in January. “Eddie, since you’re so desperate to make this fight, let’s do this: 60/40 for Vergil and 5% to the winner because I’m generous, and I’m not moving off those numbers.”

Golden Boy treated Ortiz like the established attraction, even though Ennis had been a two-belt titlist at welterweight and proven his ability to sell tickets on the East Coast. Ortiz had never headlined a major pay-per-view or generated comparable gate revenue.

The WBC interim belt gave Ortiz Jr. a negotiating tool, but it did not make him the commercial leader of the division. Golden Boy tried to turn temporary sanctioning body status into promotional dominance. Once Ennis accepted the smaller share, the biggest obstacle should have been gone. The fight still did not happen.

A breach of contract lawsuit against Golden Boy tied up much of Ortiz’s year before the dispute was settled in July. During that lost period, Ennis moved on and accepted the type of risk Ortiz’s side had avoided. He faced unified super welterweight champion Xander Zayas as the B side, helped draw 15,000 fans to Barclays Center and came away with two belts.

Their career choices produced opposite results. Ennis accepted the subordinate role because beating Zayas offered him a route to the top. Ortiz’s team fought over contractual and financial positioning before he had beaten the opponent needed to justify it.

Ennis now has everything Ortiz Jr. was trying to negotiate without fighting him: championship status, greater leverage and command of the division’s biggest fights. A bout against Josh Kelly is planned for later this year. If Ennis and WBC champion Sebastian Fundora continue winning, an undisputed fight between them can be made in 2027. Staying at 154 has placed Ennis inside a valuable series of title fights.

By moving to middleweight, Vergil Jr. has removed himself from that group. The change may reduce the strain of making 154 pounds, but the division offers fewer major names. Team Ortiz Jr. is pursuing possible fights against Jermell Charlo and Tim Tszyu, although both men have expressed interest in facing each other. If Charlo and Tszyu meet, Ortiz Jr. may find himself at 160 lacking a major opponent, a full world title or the large payday he missed against Ennis. Beating lower-profile middleweights would keep him active, but it would not replace the attention available in fights with Ennis or Fundora.

Leaving junior middleweight means Ortiz Jr. departs without getting either man or turning his interim status into full championship recognition. He spent months protecting an A side designation that brought him nothing. There was no larger purse against Ennis because there was no fight, and his bargaining position never became a championship opportunity.

Middleweight gives Ortiz a new starting point, but it also confirms how badly the Ennis negotiations were handled. Ennis took unfavorable terms, backed himself against a champion and took over at 154. Ortiz demanded control, missed the fight and abandoned the division empty handed.

Ghana News.title: ADB-UCC open new chapter of institutional collaboration
Ghana News.content:
The Agricultural Development Bank (ADB) and the University of Cape Coast (UCC) have signalled their commitment to deepening institutional cooperation following a high-level engagement between the leadership of the two institutions.

The engagement took place when the Vice-Chancellor of UCC, Prof. Dennis Worlanyo Aheto, led a delegation from the University to pay a courtesy call on the Managing Director of ADB PLC, Edward Ato Sarpong, and the Bank’s Deputy Managing Director in charge of Services, Prof. Ferdinand Ahiakpor.

The UCC delegation included Gideon Enoch Abbeyquaye, Registrar, and Mr. George Amfo-Antiri, Director of Finance.

The visit provided an important platform for the two institutions to strengthen their relationship and explore opportunities for mutually beneficial cooperation, particularly in areas that could leverage the respective strengths of academia and the financial services sector.

Welcoming the delegation, the ADB MD, Edward Ato Sarpong expressed appreciation to the UCC leadership for the visit and underscored the importance of building strong institutional partnerships.

He noted that collaboration between the banking sector and academia could create opportunities for knowledge exchange, human capital development, and innovative solutions that contribute to national development.

He reaffirmed ADB’s commitment to building sustainable relationships with reputable institutions and expressed the Bank’s readiness to explore practical areas of cooperation with UCC.

Prof. Ferdinand Ahiakpor also highlighted the importance of stronger academia-industry collaboration, noting that closer engagement between universities and businesses could help bridge the gap between academic knowledge and industry requirements.

For his part, Prof. Dennis Worlanyo Aheto expressed appreciation to the management of ADB for the warm reception and emphasised UCC’s interest in strengthening its relationship with the Bank.

He indicated that the visit was to first of all, thank and appreciate ADB for sending a delegation from Accra to congratulate him when he was appointed as the Vice-Chancellor of the University.

On institutional partnership, Prof. Aheto emphasised that closer cooperation between the two institutions could create opportunities for knowledge sharing, capacity building and other initiatives of mutual benefit.

The meeting also afforded the leadership of both institutions, an opportunity to exchange perspectives on institutional development and the important contribution that strategic partnerships can make towards developing human capital and supporting Ghana’s socioeconomic advancement.

The courtesy call marks a new chapter in the relationship between ADB and UCC, with both institutions expressing their willingness to strengthen the engagement and explore practical opportunities for deeper collaboration.

Ghana News.title: Reform of all social media should come with Meta changes, UN says
Ghana News.content:
UN human rights head Volker Türk

All of social media should be designed to be safe for children, the UN human rights chief has said after Meta settled a massive court case in the US.

Part of the deal the tech giant struck with almost all US states was to add more child safety measures - but Meta also called on TikTok and YouTube to add the same features.

The UN's high commissioner for human rights Volker Türk said governments needed to "step up rather than wait for courts and companies to act".

He added: "Children should not have to wait for a lawsuit to be safe online."

Türk said Meta's proposed changes, which include time limits and parental supervision controls, aligned with what he had been calling for - "but we're not there yet".

In May, Türk's office released a 10-point framework for regulating social media.

It included steps such as protecting data privacy and focusing on safer platform design, including better methods for verifying a user's age and avoiding exposure of such users to addictive design features.

However, the framework rejected the idea that outright bans on children's social media use were a good idea.

Meanwhile, California Attorney General Rob Bonta, who represented one of the leading states in the Meta lawsuit, said he was "looking to ensure" that TikTok adopted measures similar to Meta's.

In agreeing on Wednesday to make various changes to end the states' lawsuit, Meta said they would only be truly effective "if all our peers join us."

Bonta told US News outlet CNBC he was "interested" in speaking to TikTok and YouTube, and that TikTok was "interested in speaking with us".

Neither company has responded to requests for comment since then.

Bonta added that he had communicated with Snap, another popular social media platform among younger users.

But he warned he was "willing to take additional steps" if they did not voluntarily make changes along the lines that Meta will be making.

On Tuesday, Meta agreed to pay up to $18bn (£13.3bn) to 48 US states, plus the District of Columbia and three US territories.

The penalties will be paid over 10 years, but $5.3bn of it is contingent on YouTube and TikTok also implementing the following measures:

One-hour daily time limit

Night mode

Age assurance measures

As part of the settlement, Meta did not admit to any wrongdoing.

Ghana News.title: GMTF, Ho Teaching Hospital begin work on Volta Cardiology Centre
Ghana News.content:
The Ghana Medical Trust Fund (GMTF) and the Ho Teaching Hospital have begun discussions on steps to establish a Cardiology Centre for the Volta Region.

The engagement was led by GMTF Administrator, Adjoa Obuobia Opoku-Darko, as part of efforts to translate President John Dramani Mahama’s recent pledge to establish the facility into a workable plan.

Management of the Trust Fund and the hospital discussed the project requirements, possible implementation strategies, and how the proposed centre could complement existing specialist services at the Ho Teaching Hospital.

The discussions also focused on strengthening collaboration between the two institutions to improve access to specialised healthcare for patients with chronic and life-threatening conditions in the region.

Both sides reviewed lessons from the GMTF’s 50-patient pilot programme, which provided financial assistance to patients suffering from chronic and life-threatening conditions.

They also identified operational challenges and measures to improve service delivery as more patients are enrolled.

The meeting further assessed the ongoing onboarding of patients onto the GMTFcare digital platform. Discussions covered digital registration, claims processing and reimbursement, with both teams exploring ways to improve efficiency at the hospital.

The GMTF delegation included the Member of Parliament for Ho Central, Richmond Edem Kpotosu, and the Member of Parliament for Ketu North, Edem Agbana.

They commended President Mahama for prioritising healthcare and addressing the growing burden of non-communicable diseases through investments in specialised care.

Ms Opoku-Darko reaffirmed the Trust Fund’s commitment to building strong partnerships with healthcare institutions to expand access to affordable specialist care for Ghanaians living with chronic diseases.

She also thanked Roads and Highways Minister, Kwame Governs Agbodza, for donating three more months' salary to the Ghana Medical Trust Fund towards preparations for the construction of the Cardiology Centre.

Chief Executive Officer of the Ho Teaching Hospital, Dr Hintermann Mbroh, welcomed the continued partnership and assured the Trust Fund of the hospital’s commitment to supporting its programmes, including efforts to advance the proposed Cardiology Centre.

The engagement forms part of the GMTF’s nationwide stakeholder consultations aimed at strengthening institutional partnerships and supporting the government’s broader agenda of expanding access to quality specialist healthcare.

Ghana News.title: How Telecel M’ahitti promo is transforming lives nationwide
Ghana News.content:
When Kennedy Boakye heard his phone ring that morning at his cement shop in Nkoranza in the Bono East Region, the 46-year-old was busy helping load bags of cement into a customer’s tricycle.

The Telecel official on the call announced to Kennedy that he had won GH¢20,000 in the Telecel M’ahitti Promo. He immediately hung up. When the same Telecel official called again, Kennedy began interrogating them: “Why him? How had he won? Why were they calling him about winning?” The explanations did little to convince him.

Frustrated and overwhelmed, Kennedy handed the phone to his wife, who asked more probing questions and tried to establish whether the news was genuine. It was his wife who gave him hope that it could be real.

Arriving at Techiman for the prize presentation ceremony was the tipping point for the father of four. Kennedy, who has used his Telecel number for over a decade to make local and international calls, received the cash prize in his Telecel Cash wallet on the spot and encouraged others to bury their doubts and participate in the Telecel M’ahitti Promo.

“I own a cement shop, so I plan to invest some of the cash in my business, health and family’s development,” Kenney said.

“I encourage all to join the ongoing promo, and God can make you win. Use Telecel because it's the best, and I can assure you of that.”

So far, Kennedy is one of 17 weekly winners in the ongoing Telecel M’ahitti promo, a four-month campaign offering more than GH¢5.1 million in cash prizes.

As of Wednesday, 26th August, a total of 2,842 customers had won GH¢100 each in the daily draws, and 17 lucky customers have won GH¢20,000 each in the weekly draws.

As one of the largest consumer reward campaigns in Ghana’s telecom sector, the Telecel M’ahitti Promo will reward 12,000 customers daily with GH¢100 each, 48 customers weekly with GH¢20,000 each, and three grand prize winners monthly with GH¢1 million each.

Supervised by the National Lottery Authority – Caritas, all Telecel customers can participate for free by dialling *500#, texting WIN to 500, or activating the promotion through the Telecel Play App.

Airtime recharges, bundle purchases and Telecel Cash deposits of GH¢10 or more earn points, with bonus entries for customers who use the Telecel Play App and Telecel Cash.

Kennedy is not alone in discovering that the biggest obstacle to a big win can sometimes be believing it has happened.

About 260km away in the northern region, 24-year-old Abdul-Jalil Dokurugu had an equally unlikely route to his GH¢20,000 weekly win.

Jalil works with his uncle in a smock shop at Tamale’s Central Market. One evening after closing the shop, he was trying to buy data when he noticed the Telecel M’ahitti option after dialling *110# to purchase a bundle. He selected it almost casually, without any intention.

“I randomly selected option 8 and opted into the promo just because I wanted to know what it does,” he said. He continued to use Telecel Cash for deposits and to buy data.

When the winning call came, Jalil did not believe it. He initially ignored the subsequent calls from the Telecel office, thinking it was part of a scam. But the calls kept coming, with the explanation that he had won GH¢20,000 and the regional team would contact him.

Still suspicious, he remained unbothered until the telco’s Tamale office called and handed the phone to a Dagbani speaker who explained the win to him in his native language. He was then asked to come to the Tamale office with his uncle.

“When I got to the Telecel Tamale office, I saw that it was real. Is this a dream?” Jalil asked. For someone who completed senior high school in 2022 and is still finding his feet, he plans to invest the money in the family smock business and expand it.

The stories of Kennedy and Jalil are part of the broader national spread of the Telecel M’ahitti Promo, which is designed to give customers across Ghana's 16 regions an opportunity to win in the daily, weekly and monthly draws.

Other weekly winners have emerged from Kumasi, Sowutuom, Sefwi Anwhiaso, Obuasi, Koforidua, Teshie-Nungua and Sunyani, among others.

With the Telecel M’ahitti Promo now in its third week, there are lots of chances to participate and win in the daily, weekly and monthly draws.

Telecel Ghana has repeatedly warned customers that winners will never be asked to pay a fee, surrender their Telecel Cash PIN or make a payment to claim a prize.

Ghana News.title: Mason jailed 35 years for defiling two daughters
Ghana News.content:
A 35-year-old mason has been sentenced to 35 years’ imprisonment for repeatedly defiling his two daughters at Oyibi in Accra.

Charles Seddoh was sentenced by the Circuit Court, housed at the Domestic Violence and Victims Support Unit (DOVVSU) of the Police Headquarters, after he was found guilty on five counts of defilement and incest.

The court, presided over by Annette Sophia Essel, also ordered that the two victims be referred to a psychologist for clinical therapy to help them overcome the trauma associated with the offences.



It further directed the Police to send the victims to a shelter.



Chief Inspector Opoku Aniagyei, leading the prosecution, told the court that the 18-year-old complainant was Seddoh’s first daughter and lived with her 15-year-old sister, who was the second victim.



The prosecution said Seddoh began defiling the first victim in 2018, when she was 14 years old, and continued for about seven years.



In 2021, he began defiling the second victim when she was 11 years old.



The prosecution said whenever the victims refused his sexual advances, Seddoh beat them, denied them food and threatened not to provide for them or support their education.



It said the victims complained to their father about his conduct, and he promised to stop when they entered secondary school.



On January 3, 2025, at about 1200 hours, Seddoh allegedly forced the 15-year-old victim to have sex with him, and on January 24, 2025, at about 1400 hours, he again had sex with the 18-year-old victim.



The prosecution said on January 31, 2025, the two victims went to the Adenta DOVVSU to lodge a complaint and were issued police medical forms.



On February 4, 2025, the mother of the 18-year-old victim handed the Police a packet of Fiesta condoms, which she said Seddoh had attempted to use on her daughter.



Seddoh was arrested the same day.



On February 5, 2026, the prosecution said Seddoh led the Police, together with the victims, to the crime scene at Oyibi.

Seddoh admitted the offences in his caution statement to the Police, the prosecution said.

Ghana News.title: Ayitey Powers remanded over alleged death threat to NSA boss
Ghana News.content:
The Dansoman Circuit Court has remanded Michael Ayitey Okai, also known as Ayitey Powers, for one week for allegedly threatening to shoot Mr Yaw Ampofo Ankrah, Director-General of the National Sports Authority (NSA).

Okai, a former professional boxer, is alleged to have issued the threat in a social media video, saying: “You, Yaw Ampofo, I will shoot you with a gun.”

He has been charged with threat of death and pleaded not guilty.

The accused is expected to reappear before the court on September 2, 2026.

The prosecution told the court that the complainant, Mr Ankrah, was the Director-General of the NSA, while Okai was a former Crucial Weight boxer.

It said Okai went on social media and threatened to shoot and kill the complainant with a gun, and that the video subsequently went viral.

On August 18, 2026, the Greater Accra Regional Police Command intercepted the viral video, which allegedly showed Okai issuing the threat against Mr Ankrah.

The prosecution said the complainant lodged a complaint with the Police, following which Okai was arrested on public safety and security concerns.

It said Okai admitted making the statement in his caution statement and explained that he had made the comments out of anger.

Ghana News.title: Court orders the state to file disclosures in Wontumi bank fraud case
Ghana News.content:
An Accra High Court has ordered the state to file disclosures within 14 days in the EXIM Bank fraud case involving Bernard Antwi Boasiako, aka Wontumi.

The order follows the collapse of attempts by the prosecution and defence to reach an agreement under a plea-bargaining process initiated by Boasiako’s lawyers.

Reverend Joshua Sackey, Principal State Attorney, told the Court on Thursday that the parties had been unable to reach an agreement.

“We have not been able to reach an agreement in the plea bargaining. We seek the direction of the court to file our disclosures,” he said.

Counsel for Boasiako, Mr Samuel Atta Akyea, said he understood that plea bargaining could be pursued at any stage of the proceedings.

He said, “The continuation of the case did stop them from the plea bargaining.”

The trial judge noted that attempts at plea bargaining had failed on two occasions and that the 30-day period for the process had elapsed.

The Court consequently directed the state to file its disclosures to pave the way for a Case Management Conference (CMC) on September 22, 2026.

The case was adjourned to September 22 in the absence of Boasiako, a former Ashanti Regional Chairman of the New Patriotic Party (NPP).

Boasiako is accused of obtaining a GH¢19 million loan facility from EXIM Bank for a maize farming project on 100 acres of land.

The prosecution alleges that the project was not undertaken and that documents were presented in support of the purchase of agricultural machinery valued at GH¢4 million.

The loan facility is alleged to have increased to about GH¢30 million.

Boasiako and his farm are alleged to have committed the offences with an associate, Thomas Antwi Boasiako, who is still at large.

Boasiako, who is currently serving a prison sentence, has denied the charges.

Ghana News.title: Ghana among 8 countries selected to pilot WHO tool for stronger clinical trial systems
Ghana News.content:
Ghana has been selected as one of eight countries worldwide to pilot a World Health Organization (WHO) benchmarking tool designed to assess and strengthen institutional capacity for conducting high-quality clinical trials.

The pilot, led in Ghana by the National Vaccine Institute (NVI), is intended to help institutions identify strengths and capacity gaps in the systems needed to support ethical, efficient and scientifically rigorous clinical research.

According to a statement issued by the NVI, the draft WHO benchmarking tool moves beyond measuring the number of clinical trials conducted by an institution. Instead, it provides a structured and evidence-informed framework for assessing the systems and capabilities that support clinical trials.

The framework examines seven functional areas, including patient engagement, scientific research design, regulatory oversight, data management, trial operations, leadership and infrastructure. It includes 32 functional objectives and 112 specific outcomes.

As part of the pilot, the NVI and WHO convened a training workshop in Ho in the Volta Region to introduce institutional teams to the benchmarking tool and prepare them for self-assessments.

A comprehensive assessment exercise was subsequently conducted from Aug. 10 to 13, 2026, involving 13 Ghanaian institutions.

The participating institutions included the Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research at the University of Ghana, the University of Ghana Medical Centre, the West African Centre for Cell Biology of Infectious Pathogens, Revna Bioscience, the University of Cape Coast and Enchi Government Hospital, Dodowa Health Research Centre, the University of Health & Allied Sciences in Hohoe, the Centre for Plant Medicine Research in Mampong, KNUST's Kumasi Centre for Collaborative Research, KNUST IVI–Agogo, Kintampo Health Research Centre, the University for Development Studies in Tamale and Navrongo Health Research Centre.

NVI officials emphasised that the exercise is not intended to rank institutions against one another.

Instead, the goal is to support capacity development and continuous improvement across Ghana's clinical research ecosystem.

The Chief Executive Officer of NVI, Dr. Sodzi Sodzi-Tettey, said the work is also connected to Ghana's longer-term ambitions in vaccine development and manufacturing.

“We are starting with fill-and-finish as a practical entry point, with the long-term goal of full end-to-end manufacturing,” Sodzi-Tettey said. “The expertise gathered in this room represents the enormous brain power we need to map our institutional capability gaps and begin closing them.”

The initiative comes as Ghana seeks to strengthen its health and scientific infrastructure and expand its capacity to support research and vaccine manufacturing.

Deputy Minister of Health Dr. Grace Ayensu-Danquah said building institutional systems is an important part of achieving greater health sovereignty, particularly because research conducted outside Africa may not always adequately address the needs of African populations.

“True health sovereignty depends on the less visible groundwork—systems, policy, and institutional capacity—that precedes actual vaccine production,” she said.

Dr Ayensu-Danquah also raised the prospect of greater regional cooperation, with African countries developing specialised capabilities and working together as centres of excellence rather than each country attempting to independently produce every health product.

WHO Technical Officer for Integrated Service Delivery Dr. Angela Ackon said the benchmarking exercise would give participating institutions a structured way to evaluate their current capabilities and identify areas for improvement.

“This benchmarking exercise gives Ghanaian institutions a structured, evidence-based way to understand their own capabilities and chart a clear path for improvement,” Ackon said. “WHO is proud to stand with the National Vaccine Institute and the Government of Ghana in this important step.”

The findings from the 13 participating institutions are expected to help identify common capacity gaps and guide future investments and national priorities.

As one of eight countries involved in the global pilot, Ghana will also contribute to the further development of the WHO's benchmarking tool before its broader adoption, potentially strengthening the country's position as a destination for clinical research in Africa and beyond.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.
