World.title: Estonian Drama Theater terminates 'mistake' hiring after ecstasy admission
World.content:
The Estonian Drama Theater (Eesti Draamateater) has fired one of its staff members after he admitted to spiking two people's drinks with MDMA, also known as ecstasy.

Artistic director Hendrik Toompere Jr. said trust was broken with regard to Oliver Reimann, who allegedly spiked two coursemates' drinks with the party drug while a student at the Estonian Academy of Music and Theater (EMTA)

Toompere Jr. said the theater had misjudged the situation, calling Reimann's hiring a "mistake," and confirming his contract has been terminated.

"When trust and a peaceful working environment within the theater break down, further cooperation is unfortunately simply not possible. Theater is born out of deep trust between the actor and the director. That trust was broken," Toompere said.

Oliver Reimann. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

"Hiring him was a mistake. We have now corrected that mistake. I am sorry. Oliver has done bad things for which there can be no justification, although perhaps, in time, there can be forgiveness."

Toompere also said that when the theater reached its initial agreements with Reimann, management did not yet know about the incidents. The rumors reached them later, and Reimann did not come forward himself. When asked, he gave only a partial and downplayed explanation.

The theater initially believed the matter belonged to the past and had been resolved. "In reality, that is not the case," Toompere said.

Reimann, 24, studied at EMTA in Tallinn before joining the nearby Drama Theater. He admitted on social media earlier this week that that he had placed MDMA in the drinks of two people without their consent. Criminal proceedings have been opened against him. Reimann has also been a contributor to ETV shows, most notably "Ringvaade". ETV has said it now has no ongoing projects involving him.

World.title: Expert: Ukraine in 2021 and the Baltics today not in a comparable situation
World.content:
The circumstances surrounding the CIA director's recent visit to Moscow cannot be compared with his predecessor's trip to the Russian capital in 2021, a few months before Russia launched its full-scale war against Ukraine, ICDS head Kristi Raik said.

The Wall Street Journal reported Thursday that CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Moscow to warn Russia against attacking NATO, while Politico reported that the CIA chief warned Moscow against escalating tensions with the Baltic states. The reports also noted that then-CIA Director William Burns visited Moscow in November 2021 and sought to persuade Russia not to attack Ukraine, but the war followed nonetheless.

Kristi Raik, director of the Tallinn-based International Center for Defense and Security (ICDS), wrote in a post on X that "there is no ground for parallels between Ukraine late 2021 and the Baltic states today. In late 2021, there was clear intelligence showing Russia's preparations to invade. There is no evidence now of Russia preparing to invade the Baltic states."

Some points on parallels being drawn between 2021-2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine and 2026 Russian threat to NATO incl. the Baltic states. 1/ — Kristi Raik (@KristiRaik) August 27, 2026

However, this does not mean that Russia does not want to ratchet up tensions in an effort to persuade Western countries to abandon their support for Ukraine, Raik said. She pointed to the fall of 2022, when Ukrainian counteroffensives liberated significant areas in the Kharkiv and Kherson regions and Ukraine seized the strategic initiative, prompting Russia to issue forceful threats.

"Most importantly, both in fall 2022 and now Russia (partly through "leaks" to Western media) threatens with escalation, even use of nuclear weapons. Western countries should not fall into this trap again and let fear of escalation limit their support to Ukraine," Raik wrote.

"This is the context of CIA Director's visit to Moscow. Russia has been escalating already through sabotage acts and influence operations against NATO countries," the expert emphasized.

"One thing that is different now: there was reportedly some intelligence in 2022 suggesting that Russia was preparing for possible use of nukes. Now there is no such reporting, mere psychological pressure and verbal threats playing with western fears."

Nevertheless, the threat of a possible future invasion must be taken seriously and deterrence must remain strong, she added.

"Right now, Russia's attacks aim at stopping Western support to Ukraine. This is obviously in Russia's interest and it remains Europe's vital interest to support Ukraine," Raik concluded.

World.title: Tallinn's Knitting Raves put a crafty spin on local soft clubbing
World.content:
A Tallinn party series is inviting people to knit and crochet on the dancefloor, offering a late-evening alternative to nightclubs for beginners and veteran crafters alike.

Knitting Raves at Põhjala Factory welcome everyone from seasoned crafters to those who have never picked up needles or a crochet hook before. Organizers say dancing while knitting is easier than it sounds, and the environment can be pretty inspiring.

One organizer, Kaari Põlder, said she herself got back into crocheting thanks to the event.

"You can do anything while knitting, even dance," Põlder said, adding she was surprised by how quickly she got the hang of it. "Before attending a knitting rave, I hadn't been involved in any crafting in over 20 years."

Knitting Raves run from 6–10 p.m. at Põhjala Factory's ankruSAAL, with two DJs each playing two-hour sets of dance music and even taking requests.

People of all ages and genders are welcome, and those who would rather sit and craft can do so too.

The organizers got the idea after seeing videos of similar events in Amsterdam, where knitting raves have become popular.

"Soft clubbing" in general has gained momentum as well, offering alternatives to traditional nightlife with morning coffee shop raves, daytime dance parties and other alcohol-free events.

"Parties don't have to start so late," Põlder emphasized. "They can start at a decent hour."

Bring your own yarn, or don't

Organizer and crafts teacher Kristiin Sidok said the combination of crafting and dancing can be contagious, with some attendees arriving without a craft project in hand and leaving inspired to try one.

"You might think, 'Oh I'll just come for fun, I won't take anything with me,'" she said. "But there were several people who caught the crafting bug while there."

Sidok recommends sticking to a simple project over anything with a complicated pattern, making it easier to multitask and even chat with those around you.

"You don't have to tackle some intense project," she said.

While Sidok had made herself a special yarn bag to carry while dancing, Põlder said attendees can also borrow one on site. Craft supplies are available for purchase as well, and anyone who gets stuck with their project can turn to Sidok for help.

Põhjala Factory's next Knitting Rave kicks off this Friday at 6 p.m.

World.title: Estonia's Ministry of Finance forecasts tense fiscal situation in the coming years
World.content:
Estonia's economy is forecast to grow 2.5 percent this year, while rising defense spending and tax changes are expected to push the budget deficit to 4.4 percent of GDP, according to the Ministry of Finance's summer economic forecast.

The ministry's summer economic forecast, which will serve as the basis for next year's budget decisions, projects GDP growth of 2.5 percent this year, 2.3 percent next year and 2.4 percent in 2028.

Finance Minister Jürgen Ligi (Reform Party) said Estonia's economy has been one of the best-performing in Europe, with rapid growth and low inflation.

"Growth of 2.5 percent this year is still very impressive given the broader disruptions in the economy," Ligi said.

According to the forecast, growth this year will be driven primarily by domestic demand, as well as exports. Domestic demand will receive a boost from the introduction of a uniform €700 monthly basic exemption, which will result in growth of nearly 10 percent in the total net wage bill.

The state of public finances will remain strained in the coming years. This year, the budget deficit will rise to 4.4 percent of GDP due to increased defense spending and changes to income tax.

Next year, the deficit will reach 4.5 percent as defense spending increases further and the level of general government investment remains high. Intensive use of foreign funding will continue, supported by increasing disbursements from cohesion policy programs, while construction of Rail Baltica will be in full swing. The deficit is then projected to decline gradually, reaching 2.9 percent of GDP by 2030.

The defense spending escape clause allows the budget deficit to exceed the 3 percent limit set by the EU's founding treaty. The clause expires in 2029.

General government debt will rise to 25.9 percent of GDP this year. The increase will primarily be driven by the large budget deficit, which will increase the state's borrowing needs.

Interest costs on government debt will reach €239 million this year, broadly in line with the spring forecast. Continued financing needs will increase the debt burden by an average of nearly 3 percentage points a year over the following years, with general government debt reaching 38.6 percent of GDP by 2030.

Although Estonia's general government debt-to-GDP ratio is among the lowest in the European Union, the summer economic forecast notes that it is rising at one of the fastest rates in the EU.

Raoul Lättemäe. Source: Ken Mürk/ERR

Raoul Lättemäe, head of the ministry's fiscal policy department, said at the presentation of the forecast that Finland's government debt is nearly 90 percent of GDP and that experts there have acknowledged that curbing the country's debt burden is such a major undertaking that it cannot be accomplished within a single parliamentary term.

"The substance of it is a political question, but from an expert perspective, it is clear that this takes time," Lättemäe said.

According to the summer forecast, Estonia's export prospects will improve as economic conditions strengthen among its main export partners.

The conflict in the Middle East has not had a broader impact on prices. Lättemäe noted that there were considerable concerns when 20 percent of global freight traffic was disrupted virtually overnight at the end of February, but the feared shortages and price increases have not materialized.

"Prices have risen, but we haven't run out of fuel and the world has coped with this surprisingly smoothly and resiliently," Lättemäe said.

According to the forecast, price growth will accelerate in the fall, but inflation for the year as a whole will remain considerably lower than last year.

"Inflation has been surprisingly modest," Lättemäe said. "In the spring, we expected inflation of 4 percent; now the figure is 3.2 percent."

According to the Ministry of Finance forecast, household consumption will be supported by changes to the income tax system, slowing price growth and improving consumer confidence. Although the introduction of a uniform €700 tax-free allowance will increase average take-home pay, wage growth will vary among people at different income levels.

The unemployment rate is projected to fall toward its natural level of around 6 percent in the coming years.

Investment will remain slightly below its long-term average in the coming years, with investment in new housing particularly subdued.

Cranes at the Rail Baltica terminal site in Tallinn's Ülemiste. Source: Mait Ots / ERR

According to the forecast, the average interest rate on housing loans will remain higher than before the period of rapid price growth that began in 2021-2022. Construction activity, however, will be boosted in the coming years by Rail Baltica construction and building renovations.

The Ministry of Finance expects Estonia's exports to grow broadly in line with foreign demand over the coming years, while manufacturing output will increase and the industrial sector will regain some of its share of the economy.

World.title: Iraq, Saudi Arabia discuss border control, intelligence cooperation
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces received on Thursday a high-level Saudi security and military delegation in Baghdad to discuss strategies to enhance border control and intelligence cooperation.

According to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA), the discussions were attended by Director of the Commander-in-Chief’s Office Abdul Amir al-Shammari, the head of the Iraqi National Intelligence Service, and senior officials from Iraq’s security and intelligence agencies.

The meeting focused on improving security measures along the shared border and increasing the exchange of intelligence data.

The discussion comes after an Iraqi security delegation held meetings in Riyadh and follows diplomatic and defense dialogues between the two countries.

Baghdad and Riyadh seek improved security and military cooperation after weeks of heightened tensions in Iraq involving Iran-backed militias.

Al-Shammari met with Saudi Defense Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman earlier in August to discuss military cooperation, regional developments, and increased coordination between the two nations.

The meeting addressed cross-border drone concerns, air defense, and intelligence collaboration. It followed a joint US-Saudi airstrike targeting sites of Iran-linked militias in Iraq on July 29.

Washington and Riyadh said the operation targeted Iran-backed terrorists’ weapons and logistical facilities in response to a series of drone assaults on Saudi oil installations that they said originated in Iraqi territory.

Both Iraq and Saudi Arabia are attempting to restore security trust after the July escalation and prevent militia activities from dragging the two neighboring nations into a conflict.

World.title: Steven Fagin prepares for return to Baghdad as US envoy with economic ties in focus
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Steven Fagin, a US ambassador, is set to return to Baghdad to lead the US Mission in Iraq, with economic ties and American investment expected to be significant in his new role.

Before returning to Iraq’s capital, Fagin met with members of the US Chamber of Commerce’s US-Iraq Business Council.

Fagin met with Steve Lutes, Vice President for Middle East Affairs at the US Chamber of Commerce, and executives from major corporations with substantial interests in Iraq, such as GE Vernova, BP, and Baker Hughes.

The conversations come as Washington and Baghdad aim to capitalize on the economic momentum produced by Iraqi Prime Minister Ali Al-Zaidi’s recent visit to the United States and the Chamber’s U.S.-Iraq Business Summit.

Fagin has substantial expertise in Iraq, having previously served as deputy head of mission at the US Embassy in Baghdad and other high diplomatic positions in the area.

He is scheduled to succeed Joshua Harris, the current Charge d’Affaires and senior US diplomatic envoy in Iraq, whose term is coming to an end.

That shift was highlighted earlier Thursday, when Iraqi President Nizar Amidi met with Harris in Baghdad and reiterated Iraq’s commitment to deepening ties with the United States under the Strategic Framework Agreement.

Amidi said that Baghdad wants to expand bilateral collaboration and improve coordination in areas of mutual interest, implying that the leadership change at the US mission would result in continuity rather than a resetting of relations.

Fagin’s homecoming comes at a crucial point in US-Iraq relations. Baghdad seeks more American investment in energy, infrastructure, finance, and technology as the two nations prepare for a significant shift in their security relationship.

Iraq has set September 30 as the date for the end of the US-led coalition’s military mission, possibly shifting the focus from October on direct bilateral economic, political, and security relations.

Baghdad’s business connections with Washington are becoming more vital as the government strives to diversify an economy that is still highly reliant on oil and attract big multinational corporations.

The Chamber said that it hopes to work closely with Fagin and use his past expertise in Iraq to promote the US-Iraq commercial partnership.

His return may therefore coincide with a wider transition in relationships, from a partnership traditionally dominated by security cooperation to one in which American investment, commerce, and Iraq’s economic growth play a considerably greater role.

World.title: Iraqi security foils attempt to manufacture drones in Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s National Security Service (INSS) successfully seized 25 drone frames and closed an illegal operational production facility in Baghdad.

During a security briefing on Thursday, INSS spokesperson Arshad al-Hakim said that the whole unlawful enterprise was dismantled before production could be completed.

The security operation led to the arrest of three suspects and the seizure of 25 specialized drone frames along with various manufacturing equipment.

Officials have not identified the individuals or confirmed their affiliation; however, investigations are underway to discover whether they are associated with groups plotting national security threats.

The operation is not the only major drone-related engagement by Iraqi forces during the month of August. It is consistent with the Iraqi judiciary’s broad instruction urging courts to process illicit drone production, possession, or use severely under the state’s Anti-Terrorism Law.

Drone manufacture in Iraq is essentially an underground network of temporary assembly workshops.

Local militias have used one-way explosive drones and commercially modified unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) as their primary weapons. These groups use these means to exert their regional influence and put pressure on foreign interests.

World.title: Iraqi army reaffirms putting all weapons under state control
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi military reaffirmed on Thursday its commitment to implementing the government’s goal of putting all weapons under state control, stating that it is an irreversible sovereign matter.

The spokesperson for the commander-in-chief of the armed forces, Sabah al-Numan, stated that the government remains dedicated to regulating firearms and guaranteeing that they are under the control of the state and its official security agencies.

Al-Numan stated that a specialist committee had been created and that discussions were underway on how to control weapons in a way that preserves them, adding that the issue was a fundamental demand.

Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi is spearheading the government’s proposal to bring all weaponry under strict state control to strengthen national sovereignty, enforce the rule of law, and keep the country out of regional wars.

The effort aims to abolish autonomous armed power by September 30, 2026, when the military mission of the US-led international coalition comes to an end.

Armed factions such as Asaib Ahl al-Haq and Kataib al-Imam Ali have started to sever their autonomous ties to fully integrate into official governmental institutions.

The Iraqi Interior Ministry extended the national weapons registration procedure to the end of 2026, while continuing to purchase medium-range firearms from individuals.

Security personnel are actively targeting unauthorized organizations, carrying out raids and seizing illegal weapons.

Iraqi policymakers are considering a compromise solution to avoid deadly riots. Iran-aligned militias may keep their weapons under the Popular Mobilization Forces (PMF), a state-recognized paramilitary organization, instead of handing them over directly to official authorities.

Factions including Kataib Hezbollah, Harakat al-Nujaba, and Kataib Sayyid al-Shuhada refuse to disarm as long as any foreign military presence continues in the country.

While September 30 marks the departure of foreign forces, security officials emphasize that the date represents the start of a gradual, long-term weapon control process, not an absolute deadline for ultimate disarmament.

World.title: Iraq, Qatar’s UCC discuss oil pipeline projects to bypass Hormuz
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraqi Oil Minister Basim Khudair met on Tuesday with officials from Qatar’s UCC Holding in Baghdad to discuss critical oil pipeline projects that aim to bypass the Strait of Hormuz.

The discussions addressed establishing technical frameworks, project schedules, and contractual structures for the Basra-Haditha-Fishkhabur pipeline to Turkey and the Haditha-Baniyas pipeline to Syria, according to a statement released by the Iraqi Oil Ministry.

Iraq is prioritizing this oil pipeline network to build alternate export routes to the Mediterranean to minimize its longstanding vulnerability and reliance on maritime shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.

Khudair underlined the importance of accelerating formal contractual procedures. He requested weekly meetings between Iraqi authorities and the consortium to finalize the pipeline paths and economic models.

Qatar-based UCC Holding is leading the consortium that includes Chevron, TI Capital, and TotalEnergies to carry out the project.

The project is a network of pipelines that will be extended to the Turkish port of Ceyhan and the Syrian port of Baniyas, providing two additional outlets to enhance export flexibility.

The pipeline network will provide the country with additional export outlets on the Mediterranean, significantly reducing the risks of maritime shipping via the Strait of Hormuz.

Khudair said earlier that a country like Iraq, with its vast oil and gas reserves, cannot continue to rely on a single outlet, the Strait of Hormuz.

The Basra-Haditha pipeline project is an Iraqi venture estimated at $4.6 billion aiming to transport crude oil from the southern Iraqi province of Basra to Haditha in the western Iraqi province of Anbar.

The pipeline’s capacity is projected to be approximately 2.25 million barrels per day using 56-inch diameter pipes. This design aims to enhance domestic transportation and establish connections to future export facilities.

Reaching Haditha opens up three distinct offshore export routes: the Turkish port of Ceyhan, the Syrian port of Baniyas, and Jordan’s port of Aqaba.

Iraq’s planned oil pipeline network represents a proactive strategy to reduce dependency on Gulf marine routes, which face disruptions.

The Basra-Fishkhabur pipeline project is one of Iraq’s largest strategic energy initiatives, connecting southern oil reserves to the Turkish border.

World.title: Iraq, Shell discuss increasing gas output from Basra’s oil fields
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iraq’s Oil Ministry and Shell discussed on Wednesday strategic plans to increase gas production from oil fields in the southern province of Basra.

Deputy Oil Minister for Extraction Affairs Naseer Aziz and Shell’s Managing Director for Iraq and the UAE Fakher Bader led the discussions, according to a statement cited by the state-run Iraqi News Agency (INA).

The discussions focused on increasing the total production capacity of the Basra Gas Company (BGC), a joint venture between Iraq’s South Gas Company (SGC), Shell, and Mitsubishi, and speeding up the recovery of associated gas from southern oil fields.

To maximize state earnings, both parties reviewed strategies to increase naphtha production and exports.

The direct recovery of associated gas supports Iraq’s environmental goal to significantly reduce gas flaring at oil fields.

The initiative seeks to guarantee a reliable and stable fuel supply for domestic industries and power plants, thereby alleviating electricity shortages.

Amid regional transit issues impacting regular crude lines, enhancing hydrocarbon value through domestic gas networks provides Baghdad with critical financial stability.

World.title: Barcola move from PSG to Liverpool ‘on track’: source
World.content:
Paris – Transfer talks between Liverpool and Paris Saint-Germain over an Anfield move for Bradley Barcola are “on the right track”, a source close to the negotiations said on Thursday.

The France winger has already agreed personal terms with Liverpool, according to several media reports.

The two clubs have reportedly agreed a transfer fee which could rise to 140 million euros (£120 million, $163 million).

That would make Barcola Liverpool’s second-most expensive signing, after Alexander Isak, and would be the most money ever paid for a Ligue 1 player.

Barcola is yet to play for PSG this season amid the transfer speculation.

Liverpool have been looking to strengthen in wide areas since the departure of club great Mohamed Salah at the end of last term.

They have already signed Spain winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna in the current transfer window.

Barcola would be a statement signing for new Reds manager Andoni Iraola.

The 23-year-old scored three goals for France during their run to the semi-finals at the recent World Cup.

He was not always first-choice at PSG, with Ousmane Dembele, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue providing stiff competition for places.

But Barcola still played a key part in the capital giants winning back-to-back Champions League titles.

He has also won three Ligue 1 titles and two French Cups with PSG since joining from Lyon in 2023, scoring 39 goals in 152 appearances.

Liverpool are bidding to bounce back from a disappointing campaign last season, when their Premier League title defence ended in a fifth-placed finish, leading to the sacking of boss Arne Slot.

They rescued a 2-2 draw at Newcastle in their opening game of the season last weekend.

Luis Enrique’s PSG have been busy in the transfer market, selling Goncalo Ramos, Randal Kolo Muani and Lee Kang-in, while bringing in Maghnes Akliouche, Ferran Torres and Lucas Digne.

World.title: Swallowed by silt: Survivors recount Nepal flood horror
World.content:
Bidur – Survivors from Nepal’s flood-ravaged districts, some on stretchers, others gently supported by the shoulders, were airlifted to safety on Thursday as the constant roar of helicopters echoed across the devastated town of Bidur.

A few walked alone, their faces frozen in shock, as helicopters landed every few minutes on a football field inside the town’s military cantonment, whipping up clouds of dust.

Among the survivors was customs agent Omkar Joshi, who spent the previous night stranded on a hilltop in the border town of Timure before being rescued.

“Everything is finished,” Joshi, 35, told AFP, his voice breaking with emotion.

The town he fled had all but vanished beneath a torrent of water, mud and debris.

“Ninety percent” of its people were dead, he said, swallowed by silt.

“It is a giant graveyard. All that is left are sand and pebbles, soaked red by human blood.”

He said hundreds of people survived only by scrambling up nearby slopes as floodwaters roared through the valley below.

“It rained all night, but we stayed put till the choppers came for us,” he added.

On Wednesday, a tsunami-like wall of water and mud swept through villages and towns along Nepal’s Bhote Koshi and Trishuli rivers. Nepali police have recovered 270 bodies, but search operations continue.

Many of the missing are foreign tourists caught in the disaster, which according to the US Geological Survey was caused by a glacial collapse that resulted in an overwhelming flow of icy debris.

– Buried alive –

In Bidur, scores of anxious relatives peered through the barbed wire separating the football ground from the road, hoping to see the familiar face of a loved one.

Sita BK was searching for her younger brother Ramchandra, a schoolteacher in Timure.

“I spoke to him in the morning just before I heard the news,” said the 37-year-old. “But ever since, his phone is switched off.”

She said she had no choice but to wait.

“They (officials) said their first priority is to rescue people who are contactable,” she said. “But my brother is not.”

Nearby, Anisha Nepali sat quietly in a corner, tears running down her cheeks.

The 24-year-old had rushed back from Kathmandu on Wednesday after hearing about the disaster, but has received no news of her missing mother and younger brother.

“I have given their names, but am yet to hear anything,” she said.

Two young girls climbed out of a helicopter, still in their bright green school uniforms. A rescuer gently caressed their heads and offered them biscuits and water, before leading them away to safety.

Farther downstream, the devastation was etched into the shattered landscape of Devighat.

Residents said only one of roughly 150 houses along the banks of the Trishuli River remained intact: a four-storey old-age care home.

But rescuers said up to seven elderly residents were buried when a landslide crashed into the home as they tried to flee.

Images shared by a rescuer showed one of the victims trapped beneath an uprooted tree.

Sabir Miyan, a resident of the town, said warnings that floodwaters were racing down from the mountains had helped save lives.

“Many of us could save our lives but everything else is gone,” he said. “It is all ruins now.”

World.title: India’s petroleum products’ exports surge 8% in July

NEW DELHI: Indiaâs export of petroleum products recorded a year-on-year surge of over 8% in July, as margins improved amid a global supply shortage following Russiaâs ban on diesel exports and ample supplies of crude to India during the US-Iran ceasefire.Govt data showed India exported 2.4 million tonnes (MT) of diesel in July this year, up from 2.2 MT in the corresponding month last year, while total petroleum product exports rose from 5 MT to 5.5 MT. Diesel is currently commanding nearly 70% premium over crude, making exports lucrative for refiners despite the windfall gains tax govt brought in to ensure adequate domestic stocks.While the Indian basket of crude averages $90 per barrel this month, diesel averages $150 per barrel. Windfall tax imposed by govt, however, has ensured refiners meet domestic demand before exporting the surplus.India is the second-largest crude importer, but it has stepped up fuel exports, consolidating its position as a major supplier of refined petroleum products to neighbouring countries as well as South Asian, African and European nations.

NEW DELHI: As concerns rise over deficiencies in quality of work and premature failures in expressways and NH projects, the road transport ministry will engage a third-party inspection agency (TPIA) for inspection and examination of around 5,000 km of expressways and highway stretches from the start of construction until project completion. The agency will initially be engaged for a period of three years.TOI has learnt that the ministry has decided to onboard Engineers India Ltd (EIL), an engineering consultancy under the petroleum ministry. The agency will audit mainly expressways, six-lane and four-lane national highways.At present, third-party quality audits are conducted through independent quality auditors, who are mostly retired govt engineers empanelled by NHAI and other agencies. EIL had earlier carried out the task of third-party quality check during the construction of the Golden Quadrilateral, the countryâs first flagship highway development programme under the then PM Atal Bihari Vajpayee.In recent years, increased instances of deficiencies in NH projects have become a cause of concern, as these have attracted criticism from the public.Officials said the latest move was needed given the poor feedback from the independent auditors.The agency will be tasked with inspecting 770 km of expressways, 2,200km of six-lane highways, and another 1,000km each of NHs that are four and two lanes.Earlier this year, PMO had directed the road transport ministry to introduce independent third-party audits to ensure high-quality work.As per the plan, Engineers India Ltdâs scope will be âlimited to inspection and examinationâ of quality of work by verifying the compliance of technical specifications and standards as per contract.

World.title: Parliament may be reconvened, hints Rijiju, brings delimitation bill in focus

NEW DELHI: Keeping the opposition on edge by dropping indications about the possibility of Parliament being reconvened, parliamentary affairs minister

has said that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had made a commitment to women for speedy implementation of the womenâs reservation law and govt is working in that direction.

Citing Rijijuâs comments to India Today, Congress president

Thursday shot off a letter to the PM, demanding an all-party meeting to discuss govtâs proposal for delimitation before calling a special session of Parliament, as âindicatedâ by the union minister.

Though Rijiju made no categorical comment about an immediate session to take up the constitutional amendment bill to implement the law from 2029 with a 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats, he said Parliament has been reconvened in the past after a session was not prorogued.

The monsoon session, which ended on Aug 13, has not been prorogued yet. âAlready, the PM has made a clear-cut commitment to women of the nation that womenâs reservation and the commitment given by Parliament to women will be implemented. Based on that, we are working,â Rijiju said.

The Congress president said Rijijuâs comment ties in with the delay in the prorogation of the monsoon session of Parliament.

âThis is an issue that has enormous significance for the country.





Please do not again try and bulldoze things as you attempted on April 16-17, 2026,â Kharge wrote to Modi. The April 16-17 reference is to the discussion and voting on the bill in Lok Sabha in which the Opposition voted down govtâs proposed legislation.

The petroleum ministry appeared surprised over BPCL CMD Sanjay Khannaâs remarks made at a news conference after the companyâs AGM. A senior ministry official said that âthere have absolutely been no discussions in govt on the matterâ. âGovt has said before that there are no plans to introduce E10 fuel. World.title: Nepal flood toll hits 392; 288 Indians among 1,468 missing
World.content:
The cascading mass of water and rock swept down nearly 200km in a matter of hours, wiping out entire settlements.

With no roads, search teams face severe access issues

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Death toll in the catastrophic Nepal-Tibet flood rose to 389 by late Thursday, Nepal police said, as rescuers continued searching for hundreds swept away or cut off along the Bhote Koshi-Trishuli corridor. Three casualties are on the Tibet side, China confirmed, bringing the total number of victims to 392.Latest available National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority tally put 910 people missing or âout of contactâ in Nepal, which includes MEAâs assessment of 288 Indian citizens remaining âuncontactableâ as of late Thursday evening. Nepal has not released a nationality-wise breakup of those dead, leaving the number of Indian fatalities, if any, unconfirmed.Across the border in Tibet, Chinese authorities reported 558 people missing as of Thursday morning. Beijing too has not released a country-wise breakup, making it unclear how many Indians or citizens of other countries figured in the missing list. Another 200-odd Indians are stranded in Tibet.Indiaâs 288 âuncontactable citizensâ in Nepal included 73 working at Trishuli-1 hydropower project, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said.Among the others were tourists and pilgrims travelling in groups to or from Mount Kailash in Tibet, many from Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Kerala.By 1pm Thursday, 21 tourists from Tamil Nadu had been rescued and were being brought to Kathmandu. The 200 Indians stranded on the Tibetan side have separately sought assistance from Indian authorities.Nepal Tourism Boardâs list was narrower: it recorded 178 Indians missing or out of contact. The difference arose because Indiaâs 288 figure also covered hydropower workers and other groups outside Nepalâs tourism-based count. Indians formed the largest nationality group on Nepalâs tourist list. Nepal PM Balendra Shah said 573 people were rescued through 69 air sorties Thursday, with additional military and private helicopters kept on standby.Temporary camps were providing food, water and basic supplies, while injured people were receiving free treatment.âOur top priority right now is the life of every citizen, search and rescue of the missing, treatment of the injured, and immediate relief to affected families,â Shah said. As families searched for missing relatives, Nepal Police circulated a QR code linking to its online database of unidentified and unclaimed bodies. The site crashed soon after and remained unavailable at 10pm local time. Search teams have faced severe access problems after the flood destroyed roads and bridges, knocked out power and communications and isolated settlements in the upper valley.Families gathered at hospitals and Army centres in Kathmandu and Nuwakot, checking lists of survivors, injured people and unidentified bodies as information from remote areas remained patchy.

World.title: India, US officials discuss nuclear energy cooperation in Washington
World.content:
MUMBAI: Atomic Energy Commission chairperson, A K Mohanty, and the US secretary of the department of energy Chris Wright, held discussions to explore opportunities to further strengthen Indo-US nuclear ties for mutual benefit at the sidelines of an IAEA initiative for offshore atomic energy technologies in Washington on Wednesday

Insiders in the nuclear fraternity in Mumbai said the talks gain significance in the context of India planning to attain 100 GW of nuclear power capacity by 2047, which is expected to be achieved through government and private participation in the nuclear sector.

The Sustainable Harnessing and Advancement of Nuclear Energy for Transforming India (SHANTI) Act, passed by Parliament in Dec 2025, opened the doors for private participation in the Indian nuclear arena. On Aug 17, the department of atomic energy (DAE) launched public consultation on its draft rules for the law, which was passed to modernise the countryâs nuclear legal framework.

The meeting between Mohanty and Wright in Washington on Wednesday took place prior to the IAEA (International Atomic Energy Agency) ministerial launch of a new initiative called the Atomic Technologies Licenced For Applications At Sea (ATLAS).

World.title: CWC to hold meets on AP-TG water row on Sept. 7, on Tummidihatti on Sept. 1
World.content:
HYDERABAD

The committee constituted by the Ministry of Jal Shakti to deliberate upon the issues concerning river water management between Andhra Pradesh and Telangana in January this year, will have its second meeting on September 7 in New Delhi.

The meeting to be chaired by CWC Chairman is being convened following VIP reference of Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy. The Secretaries of Irrigation/Water Resources Departments of the two States are expected to participate.

The meeting assumes significance in the backdrop of the fresh water row between the two States, commenced with the unilateral water release to the Nagarajunsagar Right Canal by AP on Wednesday evening without approval of the Krishna River Management Board (KRMB). In response, Telangana too started releasing water to the Left Canal later in the day.

As on Thursday evening AP was drawing 7,380 cusecs of water from the Right Canal and Telangana was taking 2,070 cusecs from the Left Canal.

In the first meeting of the MoJS committee headed by the Chairman of the Central Water Commission (CWC) held on January 30, it was decided that both States would submit detailed agenda items along with supporting data for further deliberations. However, despite several reminders of the committee office, both the States are yet to send their detailed agenda.

Four officials each from the two States, officials of KRMB, GRMB, NWDA and CWC are expected to participate in the meeting to discuss further course of action.

Key meeting

A crucial meeting on the proposed Tummidihatti barrage across the Pranahita will be held in New Delhi on September 1 to discuss the technical and inter-State issues surrounding the project.

The meeting, convened by the Central Water Commission (CWC), will be chaired by its chairman and senior officials of the water resources departments of Telangana and Maharashtra are expected to participate.

The meeting follows sustained efforts by Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy to revive the project and secure an agreement with Maharashtra. Mr. Reddy had written to the Maharashtra Chief Minister on May 26, seeking a meeting between the two States to arrive at a mutually acceptable solution. He had also taken up the issue with the Prime Minister, following which the Prime Minister’s Office referred the matter to the Union Ministry of Jal Shakti.

Subsequently, on August 5, Mr. Reddy wrote to Union Jal Shakti Minister C.R. Patil, seeking the Centre’s intervention to resolve the inter-State issues and facilitate the project.

A key point in the discussions is Telangana’s proposal to raise the agreed height of the barrage from 148 metres to 152 metres. The State has been explaining to the Centre that drawing the required quantum of water through gravity at 148 metres would not be feasible and that using high-capacity pumps would substantially increase power consumption and the recurring cost of the project.

Telangana’s principal argument is that the barrage should be designed in a manner that ensures long-term benefits to the State while keeping power consumption and operational expenditure to a minimum.

The State has also cited studies conducted by the Central Water and Power Research Station (CWPRS), contending that raising the water level would result in only limited additional submergence.

The Telangana government has been pursuing the project with the Centre and Maharashtra through a series of consultations, seeking an early resolution to the outstanding issues. The project is considered important for extending irrigation to backward and drought-prone areas of Telangana.

The September 1 meeting is expected to provide an opportunity for the two States and the CWC to examine the technical aspects of the proposal and explore a way forward on the barrage

World.title: Nepal-China flash floods: People from more than 30 countries missing
World.content:
A glacier collapse in Tibet caused catastrophic flash flooding in a border area of China and Nepal. Authorities in both countries have reported at least 273 deaths and more than 1,300 people missing as of Thursday (August 27, 2026). Many were foreigners in the area for trekking or a pilgrimage to a sacred Hindu site.

Also Read : Nepal floods LIVE:

The number of missing from Wednesday's (August 26, 2026) disaster may vary across agencies because of differences in how they collected data, when it was reported and how it was verified, as well as gaps in coordination between those assembling data and those conducting rescue efforts in the affected area.

Police reported at least 270 dead and 826 missing. Local reports cited the National Emergency Operation Center as saying on Thursday (August 27, 2026) the missing included 113 Nepali tourists, 85 security personnel from the Army and police as well as 161 residents from the Rasuwa district and one from the Nuwakot district. The National Tourism Board later Thursday said 517 foreigners were missing.

State media reported at least three people died and 558 were missing in Gyirong County, Tibet. “Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported that 260 of the 558 missing people were foreigners. In addition, nearly 100 Chinese citizens were missing on the Nepal side,” China’s Foreign Ministry said.

Nepal's tourism board said 179 of those missing were from India. Officials said most were on pilgrimage to Mount Kailash in Tibet, a sacred site for Hindus. The board said 65 of the missing were from the United States, and 51 Malaysians were missing.

“Ukraine’s Foreign Ministry said 55 Ukrainians are missing. The number includes two tourist groups of 47 and seven people, in addition to one Ukrainian woman traveling with a foreign tour group,” the Ministry said.

The board said 35 Australians were missing. The board said 33 of the missing were from Britain. Nepal's tourism board said 25 of the missing were from Canada.

South Korean government officials said nine citizens working on building a hydropower plant in Nepal were missing. Eight Singaporeans were missing, according to Nepal tourism board.

Nepal's tourism board said eight tourists from Germany were missing, eight Russians, six South Africans, and six tourists from Latvia were missing.

Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi expressed worry about five Japanese nationals whom local media reported were missing.

The Nepal's tourism board also said, “Five people from New Zealand, four French citizens, three from Belgium, and three visitors from Spain were missing.”

The board said two people each from Italy, Kazakhstan, Portugal, Ireland and Netherlands were missing. It said 10 others — one each from Belarus, Finland, Hungary, Israel, Lithuania, Philippines, Bulgaria, Switzerland, Serbia and Sweden — were also missing.

World.title: At least 290 Indians remain ‘uncontactable’ after Nepal flash flood, says MEA
World.content:
In a “preliminary assessment” of the situation following the flash flood in Nepal, the Ministry of External Affairs (MEA) on Thursday (August 27, 2026) said at least 290 Indian nationals remain “uncontactable”.

Also read: Nepal flash floods LIVE updates - August 27, 2026

On India’s support to Nepal as it deals with the disaster, which has killed at least 359 people in the country, MEA official spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said, “The second consignment of 37.5 tonnes of HADR (humanitarian assistance and disaster relief) material, medicines and food packets has been handed over to Mr. Mahabir Pun, Minister for Science, Technology and Innovation, to support Nepal’s flood relief and rescue efforts. India remains committed to standing by Nepal and its people."

India had sent an aircraft carrying relief materials on Wednesday (August 26, 2026). Mr. Jaiswal said additional support would be extended.

On Thursday afternoon, Mr. Jaiswal said that two separate groups, comprising 37 and 49 people from Tamil Nadu who travelled to Kailash Manasarovar, were among the 288 Indians who could not be contacted. Later, the number was revised to 290. Giving a tentative breakdown of the Indians who remain unaccounted for so far, he said, “There is a group of 32 nationals from West Bengal who travelled with the help of Samrat Travels in Timure, which is in Rasuwa district, where this disaster happened. Then, a group of 61 Indian nationals from different States who travelled through Richa Tours, and then a group of 33 Indian nationals from Kerala.”

He said that as rescued people return to Kathmandu, arrangements would be made to facilitate their journey home.

Officials said that 63 Indian nationals employed in the Trishuli-1 project and 21 Indians from Tamil Nadu have been rescued, while the search is on to locate those who have not been heard from for over 24 hours. The situation in the disaster-hit zone from Rasuwa to Chitwan is difficult to assess because of the absence of a stable telecom network, which was disrupted by the flash flood, officials said, expressing hope that more people would be located in the coming hours.

Jaishankar holds a review meeting

As part of the ongoing process, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar held a review meeting with Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri and other senior officials of the MEA on Thursday (August 27, 2026). The meeting was also attended through video link by the Indian ambassador to Nepal, Naveen Shrivastava, and the Indian ambassador to Beijing, Vikram Doraiswamy.

“Urgent efforts are underway to ascertain the status and well-being of all Indians in the flood-affected areas,” said Mr. Jaishankar, adding that India is "working closely with the Nepali side”.

Meanwhile, family members of several of those unaccounted for so far have taken to social media to express their concern. Government sources said efforts are underway to account for those who remain “uncontactable”.

World.title: Trump signs order renaming Lake Ontario as ‘Lake America’ in U.S.
World.content:
U.S. President Donald Trump said on Thursday (August 27, 2026) that he is renaming Lake Ontario to be known as “Lake America” in the United States as he exacerbates his trade war with Canada.

The Republican President signed an executive order that updated the lake's name for the U.S. geographic naming service. Mr. Trump cannot force Canada to follow his preferred naming convention, however.

Mr. Trump has been floating the idea of the name change in recent days as the U.S. announced it was imposing 50% tariffs on $20 billion worth of Canadian goods over the weekend after talks between the countries broke down.

Mr. Trump has been needling America’s northern neighbour since he returned to the White House last year, suggesting the ally with whom the U.S. once had warm relations should instead be absorbed as the 51st state.

Canada responded to Mr. Trump’s import taxes this week by imposing retaliatory tariffs on $20 billion worth of American goods, including steel, dairy products, appliances and farm equipment

Mr. Trump, who signed the order as he was sitting at the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, had a large sign behind him propped on a stand with a map of the Great Lakes. Over Lake Ontario, in big red letters, the map read “Lake America.”

On the other wide of the President was another map with the words, “MAKING THE GREAT LAKES EVEN GREATER.”

He told reporters that Canada is “the worst” to deal with on trade. “They feel entitled and we can’t have that,” he said.

The office of Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The lake is one of multiple Great Lakes that the U.S. and Canada share borders along.

The move, which Trump said was “effective immediately,” is reminiscent of his move last year to rename the Gulf of Mexico as the “Gulf of America.’”

Mr. Trump on Thursday (August 27, 2026) suggested his push to rename bodies of water may not be finished.

“So, if you think about it, we have a gulf, and we have a lake. Now, all we need is an ocean,” Mr. Trump said. “So maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them.”

Carney says Lake Ontario’s name to remain ‘now and always’

Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday (August 27, 2026) pushed back against Mr. Trump’s renaming of Lake Ontario, citing the name’s Indigenous origins, as the row between the neighbors roiled on.

“We know that America is changing. Their trading relationships, their foreign policies, their national monuments, their hydronyms,” Mr. Carney said in a post on X.

“Canadians also know that naming reality means calling it Lake Ontario — then, now and always.”

(With inputs from AP and AFP)

World.title: Nepal flood toll hits 389; rescue work in top gear
World.content:
The death toll in the flash flood in Nepal’s Rasuwa district bordering Tibet touched 389 on Thursday (August 27, 2026), with 910 people still missing. The government issued a fresh flood alert after satellite imagery showed that a lake had formed upstream of the Bhotekoshi River due to a blockage, and warned that it could burst.

Also read: Nepal flood updates on August 27, 2026

Nepal Foreign Minister Shishir Khanal termed the flood “one of the largest natural disasters we have experienced in recent memory” even as authorities continued a massive search-and-rescue operation. “Towns after towns were wiped out in a span of a couple of hours,” he said.

Of the 910 people missing, 517 are foreign nationals. Authorities said people from more than 30 countries — with 178 Indians, 65 Americans, 53 Ukrainians, 51 Malaysians, 35 Australians, and 33 from the U.K. among them — were unaccounted for.

Separately, the Nepal Tourism Board listed 178 Indians as missing, the highest among missing foreign nationals. Most were Kailash Mansarovar Yatra pilgrims taking the Rasuwagadhi route to enter Tibet. The Board said 21 Indians were rescued.

A fresh flood warning was issued to communities and travellers along the Bhotekoshi River. Raising concerns about a possible outburst flood, the government said “satellite imagery and preliminary analysis indicate that water has accumulated at the site where flooding was reported” on Wednesday (August 26, 2026). “The lake is continuing to rise, and authorities have warned that it could breach or burst, potentially sending a sudden surge of water downstream.”

The government urged residents, travellers, rescue personnel and others in the downstream areas to remain alert. “It is advised that people stay away from riverbanks and other vulnerable areas and move to safer locations until further notice,” it said.

Prime Minister Balendra Shah reached Bidur, the district headquarters of Nuwakot, which abuts Rasuwa, by road. With 19 bridges and 40 kilometres of roads damaged, it is the last point up to which vehicles can reach.

It is unclear what caused the flash flood. According to the Nepal government, satellite imagery indicated that a snow avalanche in the Himalayan region triggered a surge of an unusually large volume of water. “Further investigations are underway to determine the role of possible glacial lakes and related events,” it said.

Since Thursday morning, personnel from the Nepal Army, Nepal Police, and the Armed Police Force raced against time to rescue survivors from mountain villages that were swept away by the flash flood on Wednesday morning. According to the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority and the Nepal Police, more than 800 people were rescued by the Army from flood-affected areas on Thursday (August 27, 2026).

World.title: 22 cricketers awarded annual contracts by Mumbai Cricket Association
World.content:
Twenty-two cricketers — 14 male and eight female — have been awarded annual contracts by the Mumbai Cricket Association. The MCA Apex Council has also constituted the Ajinkya Rahane Scholarship Fund, in a bid to recognise the distinguished career of the former India captain who retired from all formats earlier this month.

The decisions were taken at the Apex Council meeting on Thursday (August 27, 2026), with the player contract system being introduced to provide financial support to Mumbai cricketers who are not centrally contracted by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) or part of its list of targeted players.

The contracted players have been divided into three grades, with Grade A players receiving ₹12 lakh annually, Grade B ₹8 lakh and Grade C ₹6 lakh.

Siddhesh Lad and Shams Mulani are the two men in Grade A, while Mohit Avasthi, Aakash Anand and Hardik Tamore have been placed in Grade B.

Eight players, including Suved Parkar, Sairaj Patil and Himanshu Singh, form the Grade C list.

Among the women, Humairaa Kaazi and Vrushali Bhagat are the two Grade A players, while Sanika Chalke has been placed in Grade B. Five others, including Prakashika Naik and Fatima Jaffer are the Grade C players.

The MCA had announced earlier this year that it would initiate a player contract system for those outside the BCCI’s central contract and targeted-player structures. The move is aimed at providing greater recognition and financial security to players representing Mumbai.

The Apex Council also approved the Ajinkya Rahane Scholarship Fund in recognition of the former Mumbai captain’s journey from grassroots cricket to leading India in Test cricket. According to an MCA statement, the fund has received a contribution from former MCA president Sharad Pawar and will be used to support grassroots cricketers and the development of maidan cricket.

MCA president Ajinkya Naik said Rahane’s journey and achievements made him “an inspiration for young cricketers” and that the scholarship fund would help create greater opportunities at the grassroots. The Association also proposes to honour Rahane for his contribution to Mumbai and Indian cricket.

List of contracted cricketers for 2026-27

Men:

Grade A: Siddhesh Lad, Shams Mulani.

Grade B: Mohit Avasthi, Aakash Anand, Hardik Tamore

Grade C: Suved Parkar, Sairaj Patil, Himanshu Singh, Jay Jain, Sumeir

Zaveri, Atharva Bhosle, Manan Bhat, Ayush Vartak.

Women:

Grade A: Humairaa Kaazi, Vrushali Bhagat.

Grade B: Sanika Chalke.

Grade C: Prakashika Naik, Zeal D’Mello, Fatima Jaffer, Sadhvi Sanjay, Kashish Nirmal.

World.title: Bangladesh to 'positively' consider joining Makkah pact if invited: foreign minister
World.content:
Bangladesh would consider joining the Makkah Pact “positively” if invited by founding members, Foreign Minister Khalilur Rahman told parliament on Thursday.

“Joining the pact or not has not come yet, as it is subjected to the intention of the parties involved in the pact. If they invite Bangladesh to join, then we will definitely consider it positively,” the foreign minister said, assuring parliament that Dhaka would assess the potential benefits before making any decision to join.

“More importantly, we have to keep in mind that it [the Makkah Pact] is the Muslim world’s self-defence mechanism,” he added. “And this is our family’s, the Muslim family’s, internal matter. So, there is nothing for others to be concerned about.”

Separately, opposition leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-i-Islami Ameer (chief) Shafiqur Rahman said on Thursday that joining the Makkah Pact was Bangladesh’s “own decision.”

“If Bangladesh takes a decision in the interests and needs of the country and nation, no one else needs to worry about it,” he said in a statement on Facebook.

Earlier this week, Bangladesh’s State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humayun Kabir said Dhaka had expressed interest in joining the pact.

“If there is one [agreement] in West Asia, if there is a security agreement between Islamic countries, then it is not unusual to go there. Let’s see. The matter is being viewed positively,” said Kabir.

​​​​​​​Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan signed the joint defence agreement at a trilateral summit in Makkah on August 7, pledging to strengthen collective security, deepen defence cooperation and promote peace and stability in the region and beyond.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman and Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif during the summit at Al-Safa Palace.

The tripartite pact empowers member states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them, and reflects their “shared commitment to further strengthening their collective security and to promoting peace, security, and stability in the region and beyond, in pursuit of a secure and prosperous future”.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

World.title: Govt reduces petrol price by Rs0.50, diesel by Rs0.19
World.content:
The government on Thursday reduced the price of petrol by Rs0.50 per litre and high-speed diesel (HSD) by Rs0.19 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs342.60 per litre while HSD will cost Rs371.61 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on diesel.

According to a Petroleum Division notification, the new prices will be applicable on Aug 28 (Friday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: Claims that CDF Munir visited Iran as envoy for US 'incorrect, misleading': FO
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday termed claims that Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir visited Iran as an “envoy” of the United States “misleading and factually incorrect”.

The army chief met the Iranian leadership during his day-long visit to Tehran on August 24, undertaken as part of Pakistan’s diplomatic efforts to end the stalemate in the ongoing US-Iran conflict. Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi had also accompanied him.

Addressing a weekly press briefing in Islamabad on Thursday, FO Spokesperson Tahir Andrabi noted that the discussions held during CDF Munir’s visit to Tehran “focused on regional de-escalation, breaking the military stalemate and exploring a negotiated settlement to restore peace and stability”.

“I will also highlight that claims by certain quarters that the COAS and CDF visited Iran as envoy of President Trump or the US are misleading and factually incorrect, as his visit was undertaken purely in the context and backdrop of Pakistan’s role as a mediator,” he said.

Andrabi asserted that the visit underscored Islamabad’s “sincere and constructive role in bridging the difference between Washington and Tehran”. He noted that the Iranian leadership appreciated Pakistan’s efforts towards de-escalation and peaceful resolution of the conflict.

He stressed that Pakistan “remains engaged alongside our brotherly countries in sincere and concerted efforts towards resolving the crises in the Middle East and Gulf and with respect to the standoff between the US and Iran”.

“Pakistan will continue to actively pursue diplomatic engagement and support all sincere efforts aimed at reviving the peace talks and achieving a comprehensive, just and lasting resolution of the conflict,” he said.

Asked for a comment on the recent US plans for expansion of sanctions on countries doing business with Iran, Andrabi said Pakistan was “following international law and our bilateral trade agreements with Iran”.

“As such, our trade remains in consonance with our obligations,” he affirmed.

Asked about the US’s “economic war” against Iran, Andrabi expressed Islamabad’s hope that “all economic issues will also be settled in the long run” as part of a wider settlement of the US-Iran standoff.

Besides the CDF’s visit, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar also remained engaged with his counterparts on regional developments, Andrabi pointed out. He added that over the past two weeks, Dar spoke with Turkiye’s Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan three times.

A Pakistan-mediated memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed between the US and Iran in mid-June provided for the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz, and left it up to Tehran and Muscat “to define the future administration and maritime services” in the waterway, in discussion with Gulf states and in line with international law.

But the deal, which was supposed to pave the way for talks on permanently ending the war, has since fallen apart.

Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi visited Tehran on Tuesday, where he discussed a framework agreement that would establish a “temporary corridor” for shipping and a project to clear mines in the strait.

Although there has been no clear breakthrough yet, and fundamental differences persist between Iran and the US, the latest diplomatic activity has brought the political and technical dimensions of the dispute back into focus.

The Iranian position, nevertheless, remains conditional as it continues to regard the Islamabad MoU as the appropriate framework, but wants Washington to demonstrate through concrete action that it is prepared to honour its commitments.

‘Tangible actions’ needed from Kabul rather than mere assurances: FO

Responding to a query on Afghan Interior Minister Sirajuddin Haqqani’s reported remarks on a proposed security mechanism, Andrabi said: “Pakistan notes the proposal by the interim Afghan government’s interior minister for a dedicated mechanism to address contentious issues.

“We remain open to state-level dialogue. However, the sustainability of any mechanism will depend on tangible actions rather than mere assurances.”

The FO spokesperson emphasised that for any dialogue to take place, the Afghan Taliban must ensure that Afghan soil is not used to perpetrate terrorism against Pakistan.

“Kabul must honour its international commitments, including those under the Doha framework and ensure that Afghan soil is not used by hostile proxies, particularly the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan and the Baloch Liberation Army, against Pakistan,” he said.

Andrabi reiterated that Islamabad remained ready for “institutional coordination provided it results in tangible and verifiable counterterrorism measures and effective border management”.

Asked about rumours that Pakistan had informed China’s special envoy to Afghanistan that it did not desire to hold further negotiations, the FO official said he was not aware of “any such words exchanged between our side and the Chinese envoy”.

He also “categorically denied” the Afghan Taliban’s claim that linked Pakistan to recent developments in Afghanistan’s Badakhshan. He further denied that Pakistan was forming any committee regarding Afghanistan.

On Pakistan’s UN envoy calling Afghan Taliban proxies, Andrabi said: “When their activities are at the behest of a certain neighbouring country to promote terrorism in Pakistan, to promote terrorism by Fitnah Al Hind and Fitnah Al Khwarij, then, unfortunately, we will have to call them proxies, as in doing so, they are not acting in their own interest.”

He observed that “destabilising Pakistan or killing Pakistanis ought not to be the interest of the Afghan regime”.

In the past few years , Islamabad has repeatedly urged the Taliban administration in Kabul to dismantle terrorist sanctuaries on Afghan soil that are used for attacks in Pakistan. Officials say those appeals have gone unheeded.

FO rejects former Indian defence chief’s claims regarding 2025 conflict

Replying to another question, the FO spokesperson rubbished claims made by India’s ex-defence chief, Anil Chauhan, that an Indian Harop drone accidentally struck Kirana Hills near Sargodha during the May 2025 conflict after running critically low on fuel.

“We categorically reject the self-contradictory and retrospective claims made by the former Indian chief of defence staff regarding Kirana Hills,” Andrabi maintained.

He asserted that during the conflict, “Pakistan’s layered air defence network effectively thwarted India’s military objectives, while Pakistan’s subsequent response under Operation Bunyanum Marsoos demonstrated our ability to impose cost across the conflict spectrum”.

“No strategic asset or sensitive infrastructure was compromised in Pakistan. Attempts to retrospectively recast these events through selective narrative or dramatised production cannot alter the verifiable operational record of May 2025,” he said.

The FO spokesperson said that history is “established by facts and evidence, not by Bollywood-style retrospective claims”.

“These post-facto punches, if I may call them, 16 or 17 months after the war would be better directed at their faces,” he added.

Regarding a question about the removal of the structures outside Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi, Andrabi said Islamabad has “launched a strong protest” and termed the act a violation of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations.

The FO spokesperson noted that Indian “authorities used heavy machinery to demolish sheds, benches, and a walkway adjacent to the consular section” of the High Commission. He added that the facility was used by those seeking consular assistance and visas.

He pointed out that Indian actions against Pakistan’s High Commission in New Delhi were initiated “without prior notice, and therefore cannot be equated with the actions here in Islamabad”.

“Any attempt to link this incident to Islamabad’s ongoing non-discriminatory anti-encroachment drive in the Diplomatic Enclave is misleading,” Andrabi stated, noting that a notification was given to the Indian side but it “failed to remove such structures”.

He stressed that the drive “targets unauthorised structures outside all diplomatic missions, not just India, in the Diplomatic Enclave”.

Asked about a US panel’s concerns over the visit of the chief of Hindu nationalist group Rashtriya Swayamsevak Sangh (RSS), Andrabi refrained from commenting on his US trip.

However, he noted that RSS and “its affiliates and cadres have been fomenting anti-Muslim hatred in India”.

“We hope that organisations and individuals with a conscience in the US will take up these issues with the leader of the RSS if he is visiting the US. I have no particular comment to make on his US visit per se.”

Makkah pact an ‘evolving security architecture’

Asked about Bangladesh’s interest in joining the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement (MJDA) between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, the FO spokesperson said: “As an evolving security architecture, the MJDA remains open to countries who share their commitments to collective obligations and common security interests.”

The joint defence agreement signed on August 7 aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

Andrabi stressed that the pact is a “defensive framework aimed at safeguarding peace and promoting regional stability”.

He added that any formal request by another country to join the pact will be considered in consultation with Riyadh and Ankara.

“The operationalisation of the MJDA, however, remains at an early stage,” he said.

World.title: CDF Munir, Kuwaiti delegation vow to strengthen 'mutually beneficial defence partnership'
World.content:
Pakistan and Kuwait reaffirmed the resolve to “consolidate their historic and brotherly relations into a strong, enduring and mutually beneficial defence partnership”, the Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) said on Thursday.

A Kuwaiti delegation led by Defence Minister Sheikh Abdullah Ali Abdullah Al-Saleem Al-Sabah met Chief of Defence Forces (CDF) and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir at General Headquarters (GHQ) in Rawalpindi, ISPR said in a statement.

The Kuwaiti minister was accompanied by Chief of General Staff of the Armed Forces Lt Gen Khaled Darj Saad Al-Shriaan.

The two sides discussed “matters of mutual interest, regional security and bilateral defence cooperation”, ISPR said.

“Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to enhancing institutional ties and expanding mutually beneficial defence collaboration between the two brotherly countries.”

ISPR added that “the Kuwaiti delegation appreciated the professionalism, operational excellence and valuable contributions of the Pakistan Armed Forces towards regional peace and stability”.

The two sides discussed contributing to regional security and stability as well.

Pakistan and Kuwait also signed ‘Protocol Agreement 2026’, “significantly expanding bilateral military cooperation” under their 2023 Defence Cooperation Agreement, state-run Pakistan TV reported.

The pact was signed during a meeting between the Kuwait defence minister and his Pakistani counterpart Khawaja Asif in Rawalpindi.

“Pakistan’s Armed Forces will assist Kuwait in training, capacity building, border management and other mutually agreed areas of defence cooperation,” Pakistan TV added.

The signing comes about a month after Kuwait ratified the 2023 agreement with Pakistan.

Days after the ratification, Kuwaiti Foreign Minister Sheikh Jarrah Jaber Al-Ahmad Al-Sabah paid an official visit to Pakistan, where he met CDF Munir and discussed matters of mutual interest and regional security.

Sheikh Jarrah had expressed appreciation for Pakistan’s steadfast support and constructive contribution toward regional peace and stability.

During his visit, which was the first by a Kuwaiti foreign minister in more than five years, Sheikh Jarrah also called on Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and his Pakistani counterpart Ishaq Dar.

There’s been a noticeable uptick in high-level contacts between the two countries over the past few mon­ths, including exchanges between senior military officials and discussions on expanding defence cooperation, as Kuwait broadened its security partnerships amid continuing volatility across the Gulf.

World.title: Trump orders Lake Ontario to be renamed 'Lake America'
World.content:
US President Donald Trump announced on Thursday that he is renaming Lake Ontario — a large body of water shared by the United States and Canada — “Lake America”.

Trump signed an order in the White House in a move that comes amid a spiralling trade war between the world’s largest economy and its northern neighbour.

“We’re going to be changing the name of Lake Ontario effective immediately to Lake America,” the 80-year-old Republican told reporters in the Oval Office. “The Canadian officials have treated us very badly. They’re nasty people.”

The name change — which Canada is unlikely to accept — mirrors Trump’s changing of the name of the Gulf of Mexico to the Gulf of America in January 2025.

“The lake change, Lake of America, was something I’ve been thinking about for a long time, actually. As you know, we took something called the Gulf of Mexico, we changed it, and now it’s very routinely the Gulf of America,” Trump said.

“So, if you think about it, we have a Gulf and we have a lake. Now all we need is an ocean. So, maybe we’ll have to change the name of the Atlantic and/or the Pacific. Maybe we’ll change them both.”

In his inauguration speech last January, Trump said the Gulf of Mexico would be renamed the Gulf of America.

A month later, Google changed the name of the Gulf of Mexico to “Gulf of America” for those using its Maps platform inside the United States, complying with an executive order by Trump.

The tech giant wrote in a blog post that users outside the United States will continue to see both the original and new name for the Gulf of Mexico, as is the case for other disputed locations.

World.title: Smith and Cox revive England against Pakistan after Abbas strikes
World.content:
Jamie Smith and Jordan Cox both scored fifties as England recovered from a top-order collapse against Pakistan to 248-9 when bad light ended Thursday’s opening day of the second Test at Lord’s.

Veteran paceman Mohammad Abbas took three wickets for four runs in 16 balls, including the prize scalp of England captain Joe Root for just four, as the hosts slumped to 36-3 after Pakistan won the toss in helpful conditions for seam bowling.

But Smith’s 61 and 55 from Cox — his second fifty in successive Test innings — got England back into the game and turned attention away from the late-night drinking incident that saw fast bowler Brydon Carse dropped from their squad.

Abbas had fine figures of 4-56 in 15 overs and fellow seamer Mohammad Ali 3-67 in 17 when the umpires ruled it was unsafe to continue despite the floodlights illuminating the ground.

Pakistan were woeful in all departments during an innings and 103-run defeat in the first of a three-Test series at Headingley last week.

They did, however, have the worst of the conditions after losing the toss before being dismissed for meagre totals of 171 and 135.

It was a different story in London, with Pakistan captain Babar Azam, the only change to either side as he returned from a finger injury in place of stand-in skipper Salman Ali Agha, opting to field on a green-tinged pitch under grey skies following a rain delay.

Bails fly as Pakistan’s Mohammad Ali bowls out England’s Ollie Robinson for no runs on day one of the second test match between England and Pakistan at Lord’s cricket ground in London on August 27, 2026. — AFP

Fine fielding

Abbas, who has had stints with several English counties, was soon into his stride on a ground where he was named player of the match after taking eight wickets in Pakistan’s victory in their last Test at Lord’s in 2018.

The 36-year-old was fortunate, however, when Emilio Gay glanced a legside ball only for diving wicket-keeper Mohammad Rizwan to hold an excellent one-handed catch.

Ben Duckett fell for 17 when lbw to an Abbas nip-backer.

Medium-pace bowling with the ’keeper standing up to the stumps has plagued England in recent times and Rizwan was up to the wicket when Abbas pinned Root on the back leg.

Harry Brook was then bowled for 15 by a superb Ali delivery that jagged back, with England 80-4 at lunch.

Dan Lawrence had made 10 when he flicked to midwicket, only for Shan Masood to drop a seemingly routine catch.

Pakistan’s fielding was also poor as they tumbled to the bottom of the World Test Championship table with defeat in Leeds.

But when Lawrence turned spinner Ali Usman legside and set off for a non-existent single, only to be sent back by Cox, he was run out by Masood’s accurate throw from mid-wicket to Rizwan.

Cox, however, struck consecutive legside boundaries off Usman to complete an 88-ball fifty including seven fours.

His partnership of 67 with Smith ended when substitute fielder Agha, belying Pakistan’s deserved reputation as a poor fielding side, held a superb slip catch off Khurram Shahzad.

Smith, whose fifty came from a mere 63 balls, was clean bowled by Ali and two balls later the paceman dismissed tailender Ollie Robinson with another nip-backer.
